And I placed the ring on her nose and the clasps on her hands. [He changed the true order (placing-asking, 24:22-23), so that he not be "interrogated" on how he could have given before knowing who she was.]
And I bowed down and I prostrated myself to the L-rd,
and I blessed the L-rd, the G-d of my master, Abraham,
who led me in the way of truth,
to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠עַתָּ֠ה אִם־יֶשְׁכֶ֨ם עֹשִׂ֜ים חֶ֧סֶד וֶֽאֱמֶ֛ת אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֑י
pairs.english: And now, if you would do lovingkindness and truth with my master, tell me;
and if not, tell me.
And I will turn to the right [to the daughters of Ishmael] or to the left [to the daughters of Lot].
And Lavan and Bethuel answered. [Lavan, the wicked one, "jumping" to answer before his father]:
From the L-rd has the thing gone forth.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רַ֥ע אוֹ־טֽוֹב׃
pairs.english: We cannot speak to you [in refusal] ill or good.
Behold, Rivkah is before you, take (her) and go;

pairs.hebrew: וּתְהִ֤י אִשָּׁה֙ לְבֶן־אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: and let her be a wife to your master's son, as the L-rd has spoken.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֛ע עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And it was, when Abraham's bondsman heard their words,
that he bowed to the ground to the L-rd, [acknowledging good tidings].

pairs.hebrew: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א הָעֶ֜בֶד כְּלֵי־כֶ֨סֶף וּכְלֵ֤י זָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְרִבְקָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the bondsman took out vessels of silver and vessels of gold and garments, and he gave them to Rivkah;
and select fruits [from Eretz Yisrael] he gave to her brother and to her mother.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֗וּ ה֛וּא וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֖וֹ וַיָּלִ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they stayed overnight,
and they arose in the morning; and he said: Send me to my master.
And her brother and her mother [(Bethuel, who wanted to renege, having been killed by an angel)] said:

pairs.hebrew: תֵּשֵׁ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֥ אִתָּ֛נוּ יָמִ֖ים א֣וֹ עָשׂ֑וֹר אַחַ֖ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃
pairs.english: Let the maiden remain with us a year or ten months; after that, let her go.
And he said to them: Do not delay me
when the L-rd has prospered my way.
Send me and let me go to my master.
And they said: Let us call the maiden
and ask her [if she consents].
And they called Rivkah and they said to her:
Will you go with this man?
And she said: I shall go, [even against your will].
And they sent Rivkah their sister and her nurse,
and Abraham's bondsman and his men.
And they blessed Rivkah and they said to her:
Our sister, may you [and not another woman be destined to receive the blessing given to Abraham on Mount Moriah (22:17). May you] become thousands of myriads,
and may your seed inherit the gate of its foes [Ibid.]

pairs.hebrew: וַתָּ֨קׇם רִבְקָ֜ה וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֗יהָ וַתִּרְכַּ֙בְנָה֙ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וַתֵּלַ֖כְנָה אַחֲרֵ֣י הָאִ֑ישׁ
pairs.english: And Rivka and her maidens arose and they rode on the camels and they went after the man.
And the bondsman took Rivkah and he went.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִצְחָק֙ בָּ֣א מִבּ֔וֹא בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac had just come from Be'er Lachai Ro'i [(16:14) having gone there to bring Hagar back to Abraham as a wife],
and he dwelt in the land of the south.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק לָשׂ֥וּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִפְנ֣וֹת עָ֑רֶב
pairs.english: And Isaac went to pray in the field towards evening,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה גְמַלִּ֖ים בָּאִֽים׃
pairs.english: and he lifted up his eyes and he saw, and, behold, camels coming.
And Rivkah lifted her eyes,
and she saw Isaac [in his grandness],
and she slid from the camel.
And she said to the bondsman:
Who is this man walking in the field towards us?
And the bondsman said: He is my master.
And she took the veil and covered herself.
And the bondsman told Isaac
all the things that he had done [i.e., all the miracles that had been wrought for him.]
And Isaac brought her into the tent, [and she was in stead of] Sarah, his mother [(various miraculous phenomena which had ceased there with Sarah's death, recurring now)].
And she became his wife, and he loved her.
And Isaac was consoled after his mother.
And Abraham married again, a woman
[Hagar], who was called Keturah.
And she bore unto him

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־זִמְרָן֙ וְאֶת־יׇקְשָׁ֔ן וְאֶת־מְדָ֖ן וְאֶת־מִדְיָ֑ן וְאֶת־יִשְׁבָּ֖ק וְאֶת־שֽׁוּחַ׃
pairs.english: Zimran and Yakshan and Medan and Midyan and Yishbak and Shuach.
And Yakshan begot Sheva and Dedan.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י דְדָ֔ן הָי֛וּ אַשּׁוּרִ֥ם וּלְטוּשִׁ֖ם וּלְאֻמִּֽים׃
pairs.english: And the sons of Dedan were [the heads of the peoples:] Ashurim, Letushim, and Leumim.
And the sons of Midyan:
Eifah and Efer and Chanoch and Avida and Elda'ah —
all these the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham gave
all that he had [i.e., the legacy of blessing] to Isaac.
And to the sons of the concubine [Hagar] which Abraham had,
Abraham gave gifts.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֞ם מֵעַ֨ל יִצְחָ֤ק בְּנוֹ֙ בְּעוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חַ֔י
pairs.english: And he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he was still alive,
eastward, to the land of the east.
And these are the years of Abraham's life, which he lived:

pairs.hebrew: מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְחָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
pairs.english: a hundred years and seventy years, and five years. [A hundred like seventy, and seventy like five — without sin.]
And Abraham expired, and he died in a good old age,
old and content; and he was gathered to his people.
And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him [(Ishmael, having repented, granting precedence to Isaac)]

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֶל־שְׂדֵ֞ה עֶפְרֹ֤ן בֶּן־צֹ֙חַר֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃
pairs.english: in the doubled cave in the field of Efron the son of Tzochar, which is before Mamre.
The field which Abraham bought from the sons of Cheth.
There was Abraham buried, and Sarah, his wife.
And it was, after the death of Abraham,
that G d blessed Isaac his son [(the mourners' consolation)].
And Isaac dwelt at Be'er Lachai Ro'i.
And these are the progeny of Ishmael, the son of Abraham,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֜ה הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרָ֖ה לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃
pairs.english: whom Hagar the Egyptian, the bondswoman of Sarah, bore to Abraham.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל בִּשְׁמֹתָ֖ם לְתוֹלְדֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael by their names in order of birth:

pairs.hebrew: בְּכֹ֤ר יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ נְבָיֹ֔ת וְקֵדָ֥ר וְאַדְבְּאֵ֖ל וּמִבְשָֽׂם׃
pairs.english: the first-born of Ishmael — Nevayoth — and Kedar, and Adbel, and Mivsam.
And Mishma
and Suma
and Massa.
Chadad and Tema,
Yetur, Nafish, and Kedmah.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֞ם בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמֹתָ֔ם בְּחַצְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְטִֽירֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their courts [unwalled cities] and by their strongholds —
twelve princes according to their nations.
And these are the years of the life of Ishmael:

pairs.hebrew: מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים
pairs.english: a hundred years, and thirty years, and seven years.
And he expired [in righteousness] and he died, and he was gathered to his people.
And they dwelt from Chavilah until Shur,
which is before Egypt on the way to Ashur.
In the presence of all his brethren he dwelt.
And these [(Jacob and Esau)] are the progeny of Isaac the son of Abraham.
Abraham begot Isaac [i.e., After he was called "Abraham," he begot Isaac].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י יִצְחָק֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּקַחְתּ֣וֹ אֶת־רִבְקָ֗ה בַּת־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י
pairs.english: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rivkah the daughter of Bethuel the Aramite [(an evildoer)]
from Padan Aram [(a place of evildoers)],
the sister of Lavan the Aramite [(an evildoer)]
to himself as a wife, [(Rivkah retaining her integrity in spite of the above associations)].
And Isaac entreated the L rd, [praying] opposite his wife,
for she was barren.
And the L rd was entreated of him, [(but not of her, the prayer of a righteous child of a wicked father not being comparable to that of a righteous child of a righteous father)],
and Rivkah his wife conceived.
And the children wrangled within her,
and she said: If so [great is the pain of pregnancy], why (did) I [so much desire and pray for] this?
And she went [to the school of Shem] to inquire of the L rd [as to what was portended for her.]
And the L rd said to her [through Shem]: Two nations are in your womb,
and two kingdoms from your innards shall part, [one to do evil, the other to do good],
and one kingdom shall gain strength from the other, [i.e., As one falls, the other shall rise],
and the elder shall serve the younger.
And her days were filled to give birth,
and, behold, there were twins in her womb.
And the first one came out ruddy,
all like a hairy cloak,
and they called his name Esau ["all made" (i.e., complete)].

pairs.hebrew: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן יָצָ֣א אָחִ֗יו וְיָד֤וֹ אֹחֶ֙זֶת֙ בַּעֲקֵ֣ב עֵשָׂ֔ו
pairs.english: And after his brother went out, his hand grasping Esau's heel (akev), [(portending his seizure of Esau's kingdom before its consummation)],
and he called his name Yaakov.
And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
And when the youths grew up,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ צַ֖יִד אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֶ֑ה
pairs.english: Esau became a man versed in deception, a man of the field [i.e., a hunter],
and Jacob a whole (-hearted) man, a dweller of tents [i.e., of (the schools of) Shem and Ever].
And Isaac loved Esau, for [Esau "placed"] venison in his mouth,
and Rivkah loved Jacob.
And Jacob cooked a pottage,
and Esau came from the field and he was faint [with murder.]
And Esau said to Jacob:

pairs.hebrew: הַלְעִיטֵ֤נִי נָא֙ מִן־הָאָדֹ֤ם הָאָדֹם֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י עָיֵ֖ף אָנֹ֑כִי
pairs.english: "Pour down (my throat) some of this red (adom) red stuff, for I am faint"
— wherefore his name was called Edom.
And Jacob said:
Sell [as "clearly"] as the day [is clear] your birthright to me. [An evildoer such as you is not worthy of the sacrificial service (which is the prerogative of the first-born.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר עֵשָׂ֔ו הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י הוֹלֵ֖ךְ לָמ֑וּת
pairs.english: And Esau said: Behold, I am going to die.
What need have I, then, of this birthright?
And Jacob said: Swear to me as the day [is clear].
And he swore to him,
and he sold his birthright to Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וְיַעֲקֹ֞ב נָתַ֣ן לְעֵשָׂ֗ו לֶ֚חֶם וּנְזִ֣יד עֲדָשִׁ֔ים
pairs.english: And Jacob gave to Esau bread and a pottage of lentils.
And he ate, and he drank, and he arose, and he went, and
[(Scripture testifying to this effect)] Esau shamed the birthright.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם
pairs.english: And there was a famine in the land, aside from the first famine in the days of Abraham.
And Isaac went to Avimelech, king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תֵּרֵ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה
pairs.english: And the L rd appeared to him and said: Do not go down to Egypt, [for you are a "pure burnt-offering"];
dwell in the land that I shall indicate to you.

pairs.hebrew: גּ֚וּר בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ וַאֲבָרְכֶ֑ךָּ
pairs.english: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and I will bless you.
For to you and to your seed will I give all of these lands.

pairs.hebrew: וַהֲקִֽמֹתִי֙ אֶת־הַשְּׁבֻעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם אָבִֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: And I will fulfill the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
And I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens,
and I will give to your seed all of these lands,
and there will bless themselves in [the name of] your seed all the nations of the land.
Because Abraham heeded My voice [when I tried him],

and he kept My keeping [i.e., decrees for the safekeeping of the exhortations of the Torah], My mitzvoth [self-evident moral imperatives], My statutes [decrees inaccessible to reason], and My laws [(including the oral law)].
And Isaac dwelt
in Gerar.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲל֞וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ לְאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא
pairs.english: And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said: "She is my sister."

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י יָרֵא֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֔י פֶּן־יַֽהַרְגֻ֜נִי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ עַל־רִבְקָ֔ה כִּֽי־טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽוא׃
pairs.english: For he feared to say: "She is my wife," lest the men of the place kill me because of Rivkah, for she is very fair.
And it was, when the days were grown long for him there, [Isaac thinking that Rivkah was no longer in danger and relaxing his vigil],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים בְּעַ֖ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן
pairs.english: that Avimelech the king of the Philistines looked through the window,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה יִצְחָק֙ מְצַחֵ֔ק אֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and behold, Isaac sporting [i.e., lying] with Rivkah his wife.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא וְאֵ֥יךְ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא
pairs.english: And Avimelech called to Isaac and he said: But she is surely your wife! How, then, did you tell me: "She is my sister"?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יִצְחָ֔ק כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־אָמ֖וּת עָלֶֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: And Isaac said to him: For I said: Lest I die because of her.
And Avimelech said: What is this that you have done to us?
The [distinctive] one of the people [i.e., the king] had almost lain with your wife,
and, [had he done so], you would have brought guilt upon us.
And Avimelech commanded all the people, saying:

pairs.hebrew: הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
pairs.english: Whoever touches this man or his wife shall be put to death.
And Isaac sowed in that land [(though it was not so fertile as the land of the seven nations)],
and he found in that year, [a difficult year], a hundredfold [more than the estimated yield].
And the L rd blessed him.
And the man grew (i.e., prospered),

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְגָדֵ֔ל עַ֥ד כִּֽי־גָדַ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃
pairs.english: and he continued growing, until he had grown exceedingly.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ מִקְנֵה־צֹאן֙ וּמִקְנֵ֣ה בָקָ֔ר וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And he had flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and much labor,
and the Philistines envied him.

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־הַבְּאֵרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו בִּימֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And all of the wells that the servants of his father had dug in the days of Abraham, his father,
were stopped up by the Philistines [(as abetting invading armies)], and they filled them up with sand.
And Avimelech said to Isaac:
Go away from us, for you have grown much stronger than we.
And Isaac went thence,
and he camped in the valley of Gerar, and he dwelt there.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨שׇׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר ׀ אֶת־בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו
pairs.english: And Isaac returned [(before he left Gerar)] and dug the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father
and which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו׃
pairs.english: And he called them by the names by which his father had called them.
And the servants of Isaac dug in the valley,
and they found there a well of living waters.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם־רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with the shepherds of Isaac, saying: "The water is ours!"

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵֽׁם־הַבְּאֵר֙ עֵ֔שֶׂק כִּ֥י הִֽתְעַשְּׂק֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And he called the name of the well Esek ("contention"), for they contended with him [over it].
And they dug another well,
and they quarreled over it, too,
and they called its name Sitnah ("constraint").

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעְתֵּ֣ק מִשָּׁ֗ם וַיַּחְפֹּר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וְלֹ֥א רָב֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: And he traveled from there, and he dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it;

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ רְחֹב֔וֹת וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהֹוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ׃
pairs.english: and he called its name Rechovoth ("widening"), saying: For now the L rd has "widened" (things) for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.
And he went up from there
to Beersheva.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהֹוָה֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֕י אֱלֹהֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And the L rd appeared to him that night, and He said: I am the G d of Abraham your father.

pairs.hebrew: אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֣ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֙יךָ֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֔ בַּעֲב֖וּר אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדִּֽי׃
pairs.english: Do not fear, for I am with you. And I shall bless you and I shall multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham, My servant.
And he built an altar there,
and he called in the name of the L rd.
And he pitched his tent there,
and the servants of Isaac dug a well there.
And Avimelech went to him from Gerar
and a company of his friends and Phichol the captain of his host.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יִצְחָ֔ק מַדּ֖וּעַ בָּאתֶ֣ם אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to them: Why have you come to me
when you hate me and you sent me away from you?
And they said: We saw [in you as] we saw [in your father] that the L rd was with you.

pairs.hebrew: וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְנִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית עִמָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And we said: Let the oath that was between us [from the days of your father, also] be between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־תַּעֲשֵׂ֨ה עִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤ינוּ עִמְּךָ֙ רַק־ט֔וֹב וַנְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֖ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם
pairs.english: That you do not evil to us just as we did not touch you and just as we did with you only good and we sent you away in peace.
You [too, do] now [likewise unto us], O blessed of the L rd.
And he made a feast for them,
and they ate and drank.
And they arose early in the morning, and they swore to each other,
and Isaac sent them away, and they went from him in peace.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק
pairs.english: And it was on that day that the servants of Isaac came

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל־אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ
pairs.english: and told him about the well they had dug;
and they said to him: We have found water.
And he called it Shivah ("covenanting").
Therefore, the name of the city is Beersheva ("the well of the covenant")
until this day.
And when Esau was forty years,
he took as a wife Yehudith, the daughter of Be'eri the Hittite,
and Basmath, the daughter of Eilon the Hittite.
And they were a vexation of spirit
to Isaac and to Rivkah [in that they served idolatry].
And it was, when Isaac became old,
that his eyes grew dulled from seeing.
And he called to Esau, his elder son,
saying to him: "My son."
And he said to him: "Here I am."
And he said: Behold, I have become old;
I do not know the day of my death.
And now, take [(also connoting "sharpen")] I pray you, your knives [for shechitah (ritual slaughter)], your sword and your bow,
and go out into the field, and hunt me a hunting, [and not theft].

pairs.hebrew: וַעֲשֵׂה־לִ֨י מַטְעַמִּ֜ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהַ֛בְתִּי וְהָבִ֥יאָה לִּ֖י וְאֹכֵ֑לָה
pairs.english: And make me the kind of tasty dish that I like, and bring it to me and I shall eat it,
so that my soul bless you before I die.

pairs.hebrew: וְרִבְקָ֣ה שֹׁמַ֔עַת בְּדַבֵּ֣ר יִצְחָ֔ק אֶל־עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Rivkah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ עֵשָׂו֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָצ֥וּד צַ֖יִד לְהָבִֽיא׃
pairs.english: and Esau went to the field to hunt a hunting to bring [by theft, if "hunting" were not available].
And Rivkah said to Jacob her son:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֤ה שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־אָבִ֔יךָ מְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶל־עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יךָ לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: Behold, I have overheard your father saying to your brother Esau:

pairs.hebrew: הָבִ֨יאָה לִּ֥י צַ֛יִד וַעֲשֵׂה־לִ֥י מַטְעַמִּ֖ים וְאֹכֵ֑לָה
pairs.english: Bring me a hunting and make me savory food, and I shall eat,
and I shall bless you before the L rd [i.e., by His leave] before my death.
And now, my son, hearken to my voice,
to what I command you.

pairs.hebrew: לֶךְ־נָא֙ אֶל־הַצֹּ֔אן וְקַֽח־לִ֣י מִשָּׁ֗ם שְׁנֵ֛י גְּדָיֵ֥י עִזִּ֖ים טֹבִ֑ים
pairs.english: Go, now, to the flock, and take for me [(from what is mine)] from there two good goat kids, [one for a paschal offering, and one for a savory dish],

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֨ה אֹתָ֧ם מַטְעַמִּ֛ים לְאָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהֵֽב׃
pairs.english: and I shall make of them for your father the kind of tasty dish that he likes [(kid, tasting like venison)].
And bring it to your father and have him eat,
so that he bless you before his death.
And Jacob said to Rivkah, his mother:

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֣ן עֵשָׂ֤ו אָחִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂעִ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִ֥ישׁ חָלָֽק׃
pairs.english: But Esau my brother is hairy and I am smooth-skinned.
Perchance my father will feel me
and I shall be in his eyes as a deceiver,
and I will bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing!

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִמּ֔וֹ עָלַ֥י קִלְלָתְךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And his mother said to him: Your curse upon me, my son;
only hear my voice and go take (them) for me.
And he went and took (them) and brought (them) to his mother.

pairs.hebrew: וַתַּ֤עַשׂ אִמּוֹ֙ מַטְעַמִּ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָהֵ֥ב אָבִֽיו׃
pairs.english: And his mother made the kind of tasty dish that his father liked.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִ֠בְקָ֠ה אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֨י עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּנָ֤הּ הַגָּדֹל֙ הַחֲמֻדֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּ֖הּ בַּבָּ֑יִת
pairs.english: And Rivkah took the clean garments of Esau, her elder son, which were with her [for safe-keeping] in the house,
and she clothed Jacob her younger son with them.
And the skins of the goat-kids
she placed upon his hands and the smooth of his neck.
And she placed the tasty dish and the bread that she had made
in the hand of her son Jacob.
And he brought (it) to his father, and he said: "My father."
And he said: "I am here. Who are you, my son?"

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל־אָבִ֗יו אָנֹכִי֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּכֹרֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And Jacob said to his father: I am [(the one bringing food to you, and)] Esau [is] your first-born.
I have done [(many things)] as you have spoken to me.

pairs.hebrew: קֽוּם־נָ֣א שְׁבָ֗ה וְאׇכְלָה֙ מִצֵּידִ֔י בַּעֲב֖וּר תְּבָרְכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
pairs.english: Arise, I pray you, and sit [at table] and eat of my hunting so that your soul bless me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶל־בְּנ֔וֹ מַה־זֶּ֛ה מִהַ֥רְתָּ לִמְצֹ֖א בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to his son: How did you find (it) so quickly, my son?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י הִקְרָ֛ה יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְפָנָֽי׃
pairs.english: And he said: For the L rd your G d put it in my way.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב גְּשָׁה־נָּ֥א וַאֲמֻֽשְׁךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And Isaac said to Jacob: Come near and let me feel you, my son, [(Isaac having been surprised at the reply, atypical of Esau)].
Are you my son Esau or not?
And Jacob drew near to Isaac his father, and he felt him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַקֹּל֙ ק֣וֹל יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְהַיָּדַ֖יִם יְדֵ֥י עֵשָֽׂו׃
pairs.english: and he said: The voice [i.e., the tone, e.g., "Arise, I pray you"] is the voice of Jacob [(as opposed to Esau's brusque "Let my father arise")], but the hands are the hands of Esau.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֣א הִכִּיר֔וֹ כִּֽי־הָי֣וּ יָדָ֗יו כִּידֵ֛י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יו שְׂעִרֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And he did not recognize him, for his hands were like the hands of Esau his brother, hairy,
and he blessed him.
And he said: Are you this, my son Esau?
And he said: "I" [(but not: "I am Esau.")]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַגִּ֤שָׁה לִּי֙ וְאֹֽכְלָה֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנִ֔י לְמַ֥עַן תְּבָֽרֶכְךָ֖ נַפְשִׁ֑י
pairs.english: And he said: Reach (it) to me, and I will eat of the hunting of my son, so that my soul bless you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגֶּשׁ־לוֹ֙ וַיֹּאכַ֔ל וַיָּ֧בֵא ל֦וֹ יַ֖יִן וַיֵּֽשְׁתְּ׃
pairs.english: And he reached (it) to him, and he ate, and he brought him wine and he drank.
And Isaac his father said to him:
Draw near, now, and kiss me, my son.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ וַיִּשַּׁק־ל֔וֹ וַיָּ֛רַח אֶת־רֵ֥יחַ בְּגָדָ֖יו וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: And he drew near and he kissed him and he smelled the smell of his garments [into which the fragrance of Eden had entered], and he blessed him.
And he said: See, the smell of my son
is as that of a field [of apples] which the L rd has blessed.
And may G d give you [in addition to the fragrance of Eden]

pairs.hebrew: מִטַּל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹ֥ב דָּגָ֖ן וְתִירֹֽשׁ׃
pairs.english: of the dew of the heavens and the fat of the earth, and an abundance of corn and wine.
Peoples will serve you, and nations will bow down to you.

pairs.hebrew: הֱוֵ֤ה גְבִיר֙ לְאַחֶ֔יךָ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּנֵ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: Be a master to your brothers, and your mother's sons will bow down to you.
Your cursers will be cursed and your blessers will be blessed.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלָּ֣ה יִצְחָק֮ לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒
pairs.english: And it was, when Isaac finished blessing Jacob —

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י אַ֣ךְ יָצֹ֤א יָצָא֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב מֵאֵ֥ת פְּנֵ֖י יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: Jacob had just left the presence of Isaac his father,
when Esau his brother came from his hunting.
And he, too, made a savory dish and brought it to his father.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֗יו יָקֻ֤ם אָבִי֙ וְיֹאכַל֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנ֔וֹ בַּעֲבֻ֖ר תְּבָרְכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
pairs.english: And he said to his father: Let my father arise and eat from the hunting of his son, so that your soul bless me.
And Isaac his father said to him: Who are you?
And he said: I am your first-born son, Esau.
And Isaac was greatly confounded,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר מִֽי־אֵפ֡וֹא ה֣וּא הַצָּֽד־צַ֩יִד֩ וַיָּ֨בֵא לִ֜י וָאֹכַ֥ל מִכֹּ֛ל בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא וָאֲבָרְכֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: and he said: Who is it, then, that hunted a hunting and brought it to me and I ate all [the flavors that I desired] before you came, and I blessed him —
and he will, indeed, be blessed.
When Esau heard the words of his father,
he cried a great and bitter outcry,
and he said to his father: Bless me also, my father!
And he said:
Your brother came with subtlety and took your blessing.
And he said: "Is it for this that he was called 'Yaakov' ('following at the heels')?
That he would overtake me (ya'akveini) these two times?
He took my birthright,
and, behold, now he has taken my blessing!"
And he said: "Did you not keep back a blessing for me?"

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨עַן יִצְחָ֜ק וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֵשָׂ֗ו הֵ֣ן גְּבִ֞יר שַׂמְתִּ֥יו לָךְ֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־אֶחָ֗יו נָתַ֤תִּי לוֹ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים
pairs.english: And Isaac answered and he said to Esau: I made him a master over you, and all of his brothers have I given to him as bondsmen [and "whatever a bondsman acquires is acquired by his master"],
and with corn and wine have I buttressed him,
and for you, then, what can I do, my son?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶל־אָבִ֗יו הַֽבְרָכָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת הִֽוא־לְךָ֙ אָבִ֔י
pairs.english: And Esau said to his father: Do you have only one blessing, my father?
Bless me, too, my father.
And Esau raised his voice and wept.
And Isaac his father answered and he said to him:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֞ה מִשְׁמַנֵּ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה מֽוֹשָׁבֶ֔ךָ וּמִטַּ֥ל הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מֵעָֽל׃
pairs.english: Behold, of the fats of the earth [Graeca Magna] will be your dwelling, and of the dew of the heavens from above.
And by your sword will you live, and your brother will you serve.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּרִ֔יד וּפָרַקְתָּ֥ עֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֥ל צַוָּארֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: And it shall be when you [have just reason to] grieve [over the blessings' having been appropriated by Jacob (i.e., when Israel transgresses the Torah)], then you shall remove his yoke from your neck.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׂטֹ֤ם עֵשָׂו֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב עַ֨ל־הַבְּרָכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּרְכ֖וֹ אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing that his father had given him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּלִבּ֗וֹ יִקְרְבוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ אֵ֣בֶל אָבִ֔י וְאַֽהַרְגָ֖ה אֶת־יַעֲקֹ֥ב אָחִֽי׃
pairs.english: and Esau said in his heart; Let the days of mourning for my father draw near, and I will [then] kill Jacob my brother [(and not before, so as not to aggrieve my father)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְרִבְקָ֔ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנָ֣הּ הַגָּדֹ֑ל
pairs.english: And it was told to Rivkah [through the holy spirit] the thoughts of Esau her elder son,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּשְׁלַ֞ח וַתִּקְרָ֤א לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּנָ֣הּ הַקָּטָ֔ן וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו
pairs.english: and she sent and called to Jacob her younger son and said to him:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּה֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֔יךָ מִתְנַחֵ֥ם לְךָ֖ לְהׇרְגֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: Behold, Esau your brother is bethinking himself [of his brotherhood] to you, to kill you.
And now, my son, hearken to my voice.
Arise, and run away to Lavan my brother in Charan.
And remain with him for some time,
until your brother's fury is abated.

pairs.hebrew: עַד־שׁ֨וּב אַף־אָחִ֜יךָ מִמְּךָ֗ וְשָׁכַח֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: Until your brother's wrath turns from you and he forgets what you did to him,
when I will send and take you from there.
Why should I be bereft of both of you [(one killing, the other being killed in revenge)] in one day [(a presage of the future, Jacob and Esau being buried on the same day)] (See Sotah 13a).

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רִבְקָה֙ אֶל־יִצְחָ֔ק קַ֣צְתִּי בְחַיַּ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנ֣וֹת חֵ֑ת
pairs.english: And Rivkah said to Isaac: I have despised my life because of the daughters of Cheth.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־לֹקֵ֣חַ יַ֠עֲקֹ֠ב אִשָּׁ֨ה מִבְּנֽוֹת־חֵ֤ת כָּאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִבְּנ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לָ֥מָּה לִּ֖י חַיִּֽים׃
pairs.english: If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Cheth such as these of the daughters of the land, what is life to me?
And Isaac called to Jacob and he blessed him,
and he charged him, saying:
Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: ק֥וּם לֵךְ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם בֵּ֥יתָה בְתוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: Arise, go to Padan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father,

pairs.hebrew: וְקַח־לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ׃
pairs.english: and take for yourself from there a wife from the daughters of Lavan, your mother's brother.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְיַפְרְךָ֖ וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And the G d who is All-Sufficient [in His blessings] will bless you. And He will make you fruitful and will multiply you,
and you will be an assembly of peoples.

pairs.hebrew: וְיִֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ אֶת־בִּרְכַּ֣ת אַבְרָהָ֔ם לְךָ֖ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֣ אִתָּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: And He will give you [i.e., there will issue from you] the blessing of [i.e., to] Abraham [(12:2): "And I shall make you a great nation" and (26:4): "And they will bless themselves in your seed"], to you and to your seed with you,

pairs.hebrew: לְרִשְׁתְּךָ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃
pairs.english: to inherit the land of your sojournings which G d gave to Abraham.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֑ם
pairs.english: And Isaac sent Jacob, and he went to Padan-Aram,

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־לָבָ֤ן בֶּן־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י אֲחִ֣י רִבְקָ֔ה אֵ֥ם יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְעֵשָֽׂו׃
pairs.english: to Lavan the son of Bethuel the Aramite, the brother of Rivkah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֗ו כִּֽי־בֵרַ֣ךְ יִצְחָק֮ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם לָקַֽחַת־ל֥וֹ מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and that he had sent him to Padan-Aram to take for himself from there a wife

pairs.hebrew: בְּבָרְכ֣וֹ אֹת֔וֹ וַיְצַ֤ו עָלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃
pairs.english: in blessing him, charging him: Do not take wife from the daughters of Canaan,
and that Jacob had heeded his father and mother
and gone to Padan-Aram.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י רָע֖וֹת בְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were evil
in the eyes of Isaac his father.
And Esau [likewise] went to Ishmael,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת־מָחֲלַ֣ת ׀ בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת
pairs.english: and he took Machlath the daughter of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, the sister of Nevayoth [(who gave her in marriage to Esau)]
in addition to his (other) [wicked] wives for himself as a wife.
And Jacob went out of Beersheva
and he went [to go] to Charan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְגַּ֨ע בַּמָּק֜וֹם וַיָּ֤לֶן שָׁם֙ כִּי־בָ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ
pairs.english: And he came to the place [Mount Moriah] and he spent the night there, for the sun had set [of a sudden, G d causing it to set so that he should sleep there].
And he took of the stones of the place and set them around his head [to guard against animals],
and he slept in that place.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה סֻלָּם֙ מֻצָּ֣ב אַ֔רְצָה וְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ מַגִּ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה
pairs.english: And he dreamed, and, behold, a ladder set in the earth, and its top reaching the heavens,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּה֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים וְיֹרְדִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and, behold, angels of G d ascending [to heaven] and [others] descending [from heaven to earth] upon it.
And, behold, the L rd was standing over him [to guard him]. And He said:

pairs.hebrew: אֲנִ֣י יְהֹוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יךָ וֵאלֹהֵ֖י יִצְחָ֑ק
pairs.english: I am the L rd, the G d of Abraham your father, and the G d of Isaac.

pairs.hebrew: הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב עָלֶ֔יהָ לְךָ֥ אֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה וּלְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: The land on which you lie, to you shall I give it, and to your seed.
And your seed will be as dust of the earth,
and you will be strong, west and east and north and south.
And all the families of the earth will bless themselves in you and in your seed.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י עִמָּ֗ךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּ֙יךָ֙ בְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־תֵּלֵ֔ךְ
pairs.english: And, behold, I am with you, [and you need not fear Esau and Lavan], and I shall keep you, wherever you go,
and I shall return you to this land;

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱזׇבְךָ֔ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃
pairs.english: for I shall not forsake you until I have done what I have spoken [to Abraham] concerning you.
And Jacob awoke from his sleep

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָכֵן֙ יֵ֣שׁ יְהֹוָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: and he said: In truth, the L rd is in this place,
and I did not know it. [Had I known it, I would not have slept here.]
And he feared and he said: How awesome is this place!
This is none other than the house of G d,
and this is the gate of heaven [a place of prayer, whence prayers ascend to heaven].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֜ב בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֔יו
pairs.english: And Jacob arose early in the morning and he took the stone that he had placed at his head
and he set it up as a monument
and he poured oil on its top.
And he called the name of that place Beth-El ("the house of G d"),
whereas Luz had been the name of the city in the beginning.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּדַּ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב נֶ֣דֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־יִהְיֶ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים עִמָּדִ֗י
pairs.english: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: If G d will be with me, [as He promised (28:15)],

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁמָרַ֙נִי֙ בַּדֶּ֤רֶךְ הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ
pairs.english: and He will keep me on this way on which I go, [as He said (Ibid.)],
and He will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear, [as He said (Ibid.): "For I shall not forsake you"],
and I return in peace [free of sin] to my father's house, [as He said (Ibid.)],

and the L rd will be a G d for me, [conferring His name upon me, there being no blemish in my seed, as He said (Ibid.): "what I have spoken concerning you," viz. (17:17): "to be a G d to you and to your seed after you"],

pairs.hebrew: וְהָאֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּ֗את אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֙מְתִּי֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים
pairs.english: then this stone which I have set up as a pillar will be the house of G d [i.e., I shall worship the L rd upon it (as he did, viz. 35:1 and 14)],

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתֶּן־לִ֔י עַשֵּׂ֖ר אֲעַשְּׂרֶ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ׃
pairs.english: and all that You give me will I tenth to You.
And Jacob lifted his feet [on the "strength" of the glad tidings],
and he went to the land of the children of the east.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֞רְא וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְאֵ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֞ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶדְרֵי־צֹאן֙ רֹבְצִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יהָ
pairs.english: And he saw, and, behold, a well in the field, and, behold, three flocks of sheep resting near it;
for from that well they [the shepherds] would water the flocks,
and a great stone on the mouth of the well.

pairs.hebrew: וְנֶאֶסְפוּ־שָׁ֣מָּה כׇל־הָעֲדָרִ֗ים וְגָלְל֤וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר
pairs.english: And all the flocks would gather there and they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well
and water the sheep,
and they would return the stone to its place on the mouth of the well.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב אַחַ֖י מֵאַ֣יִן אַתֶּ֑ם
pairs.english: And Jacob said to them: My brothers, whence do you come?
And they said: We are from Charan.
And he said to them: Do you know Lavan the son of Nachor?
And they said: We know.
And he said to them: Is he well?
And they said: Well,
and, behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.
And he said: The day is yet long;
it is not time to gather in the kine;
water the sheep and go and graze.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לֹ֣א נוּכַל֒ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ כׇּל־הָ֣עֲדָרִ֔ים
pairs.english: And they said: We will not be able to do so until all the flocks are gathered
and they [the shepherds] roll the stone from the mouth of the well
and we water the sheep.
He was yet speaking with them

pairs.hebrew: וְרָחֵ֣ל ׀ בָּ֗אָה עִם־הַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י רֹעָ֖ה הִֽוא׃
pairs.english: when Rachel came with her father's sheep (for she was a shepherdess).

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ רָאָ֨ה יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־רָחֵ֗ל בַּת־לָבָן֙ אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֔וֹ וְאֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And it was, when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Lavan, his mother's brother, and the sheep of Lavan, his mother's brother,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיָּ֤גֶל אֶת־הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר
pairs.english: that Jacob came forward and flipped the stone from the mouth of the well
and watered the sheep of Lavan, his mother's brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel
and he lifted up his voice and cried, [seeing prophetically that she would not be buried with him].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד יַעֲקֹ֜ב לְרָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י אֲחִ֤י אָבִ֙יהָ֙ ה֔וּא וְכִ֥י בֶן־רִבְקָ֖ה ה֑וּא
pairs.english: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's kin and Rivkah's son,
and she ran and told it to her father, [her mother having died].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ לָבָ֜ן אֶת־שֵׁ֣מַע ׀ יַעֲקֹ֣ב בֶּן־אֲחֹת֗וֹ
pairs.english: And it was, when Lavan heard the talk of Jacob, his sister's son,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֤רׇץ לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיְחַבֶּק־לוֹ֙ וַיְנַשֶּׁק־ל֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ
pairs.english: that he ran towards him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house;
and he told Lavan all of these things.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לָבָ֔ן אַ֛ךְ עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה
pairs.english: And Lavan said to him: But, [though you come empty-handed], you are my bone and flesh.
And he stayed with him a month of days.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב הֲכִי־אָחִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וַעֲבַדְתַּ֖נִי חִנָּ֑ם
pairs.english: And Lavan said to Jacob: Is it because you are my brother that you would serve me for nought?
Tell me what your wage is.
And Lavan had two daughters:

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁ֤ם הַגְּדֹלָה֙ לֵאָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה רָחֵֽל׃
pairs.english: the name of the elder, Leah, and the name of the younger, Rachel.
And the eyes of Leah were soft,
and Rachel was of beautiful [facial] form and of beautiful [facial] appearance.
And Jacob loved Rachel,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶֽעֱבׇדְךָ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים בְּרָחֵ֥ל בִּתְּךָ֖ הַקְּטַנָּֽה׃
pairs.english: and he said: I shall serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter, [(Jacob making assurance doubly sure — and being deceived nonetheless)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֗ן ט֚וֹב תִּתִּ֣י אֹתָ֣הּ לָ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר
pairs.english: And Lavan said: It is better for me to give her to you than to give her to another man;
stay with me.
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֤וּ בְעֵינָיו֙ כְּיָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֔ים בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: and they were in his eyes like several days in his love for her.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב אֶל־לָבָן֙ הָבָ֣ה אֶת־אִשְׁתִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָלְא֖וּ יָמָ֑י
pairs.english: And Jacob said to Lavan: Give me my wife, for my days have been completed,
and let me come to her [and beget children (the twelve tribes)].
And Lavan gathered all the men of the place
and he made a feast.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־לֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אֵלָ֑יו
pairs.english: And it was in the evening that he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him,
and he lived with her.
And Lavan gave her Zilpah, his handmaid,
to Leah his daughter, as a handmaid.
And it was in the morning, and, behold, it is Leah! [(Rachel having given to Leah the "identity signs" that Jacob had given her, so that Leah not be shamed)].
And he said to Lavan: What is this that you have done to me?

pairs.hebrew: הֲלֹ֤א בְרָחֵל֙ עָבַ֣דְתִּי עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה רִמִּיתָֽנִי׃
pairs.english: Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why have you deceived me!
And Lavan said: It is not done thus in our place
to give the younger daughter before the elder.
Fulfill the [festal] week of this one (Leah),
and we will give you this one, too, [(after the festal week, Jacob's service beginning after the wedding)]

pairs.hebrew: בַּעֲבֹדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמָּדִ֔י ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: for the service you will render me yet another seven years.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יַעֲקֹב֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיְמַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את
pairs.english: And Jacob did thus, and he fulfilled the week of that one,
and he gave him Rachel his daughter as a wife.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Lavan gave to Rachel his daughter, Bilhah his handmaid,
to her as a handmaid.
And he came also to Rachel,
and he loved also Rachel more than Leah,
and he served him yet another seven years, [as devotedly as the first].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤רְא יְהֹוָה֙ כִּֽי־שְׂנוּאָ֣ה לֵאָ֔ה וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־רַחְמָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And the L rd saw that Leah was hated, and He opened her womb;
and Rachel was barren.

pairs.hebrew: וַתַּ֤הַר לֵאָה֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ רְאוּבֵ֑ן
pairs.english: And Leah conceived and she bore a son, and she called his name Reuven,
saying: For the L rd has seen (ra'ah Hashem) my affliction;
for now my husband will love me.
And she conceived again and she bore a son,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֤ע יְהֹוָה֙ כִּֽי־שְׂנוּאָ֣ה אָנֹ֔כִי וַיִּתֶּן־לִ֖י גַּם־אֶת־זֶ֑ה
pairs.english: and she said: For the L rd has heard (shama Hashem) that I am hated, and He has given me this one, too.
And she called his name Shimon.
And she conceived again and she bore a son,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֤ה הַפַּ֙עַם֙ יִלָּוֶ֤ה אִישִׁי֙ אֵלַ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים
pairs.english: and she said: This time my husband will join himself (yilaveh) to me, for I have borne him three sons [my share of the twelve tribes (among his four wives)].
Therefore, he called his name Levi.
And she conceived again and she bore a son,
and she said: This time, [having borne more than my share], I will thank (odeh) the L rd.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד מִלֶּֽדֶת׃
pairs.english: Therefore, she called his name Yehudah. And she left off bearing.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֣רֶא רָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽלְדָה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַתְּקַנֵּ֥א רָחֵ֖ל בַּאֲחֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And Rachel saw that she had not borne (a child) to Jacob, and Rachel envied her sister, [thinking that if Leah were not more righteous than she, she, too, would not have borne],

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ הָֽבָה־לִּ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְאִם־אַ֖יִן מֵתָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי׃
pairs.english: and she said to Jacob: "Give me children" [i.e., pray for me to bear children, as your father did for your mother], "and if not, I am dead."
And Jacob's wrath burned against Rachel,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲתַ֤חַת אֱלֹהִים֙ אָנֹ֔כִי אֲשֶׁר־מָנַ֥ע מִמֵּ֖ךְ פְּרִי־בָֽטֶן׃
pairs.english: and he said: Am I in the place of G d, who has withheld from you [(but not from me)] the fruit of the womb?

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה אֲמָתִ֥י בִלְהָ֖ה בֹּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: And she said: Here is my handmaid Bilhah. Come to her
and let her bear upon my knees, [i.e., I shall raise her child], and I, too, shall build up [i.e., bear a child] by cause of her, [(as Sarah did after she had given her handmaid Hagar to Abraham)].
And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid as a wife,
and Jacob lived with her.
And Bilhah conceived
and she bore a son to Jacob.
And Rachel said: G d judged me (danani) [and made me barren],
and He also heard my plaint and gave me a son —
wherefore she called his name Dan.
And she conceived again,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֕לֶד בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֑ל בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
pairs.english: and Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid, bore a second son to Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל נַפְתּוּלֵ֨י אֱלֹהִ֧ים ׀ נִפְתַּ֛לְתִּי עִם־אֲחֹתִ֖י גַּם־יָכֹ֑לְתִּי
pairs.english: And Rachel said: [With many] importunities (naftulim) did I importune G d [to be equal] with my sister, and I also prevailed [i.e., He was also entreated of me],
and she called his name Naftali.
And Leah saw that she had stopped bearing,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּקַּח֙ אֶת־זִלְפָּ֣ה שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
pairs.english: and she took her handmaid Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
And Zilpah, Leah's handmaid,
bore a son to Jacob.
And Leah said: "Bagad" ("Good fortune comes"),
and she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah's handmaid,
bore a second son to Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֔ה בְּאׇשְׁרִ֕י כִּ֥י אִשְּׁר֖וּנִי בָּנ֑וֹת
pairs.english: And Leah said: For my praise (be'ashri); for daughters will praise me.
And she called his name Asher.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֜ן בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּמְצָ֤א דֽוּדָאִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה
pairs.english: And Reuven went in the days of the wheat harvest, and he found violets in the field [(He took what was ownerless and not what had been harvested)],
and he brought them to Leah his mother.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ אֶל־לֵאָ֔ה תְּנִי־נָ֣א לִ֔י מִדּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנֵֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And Rachel said to Leah: Give me of the violets of your son.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הַמְעַט֙ קַחְתֵּ֣ךְ אֶת־אִישִׁ֔י וְלָקַ֕חַת גַּ֥ם אֶת־דּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: And she said to her: Is your taking my husband too little that you would also take the violets of my son?

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל לָכֵן֙ יִשְׁכַּ֤ב עִמָּךְ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה תַּ֖חַת דּוּדָאֵ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And Rachel said: Therefore, he will lie with you this night [(which was "Rachel's night")] in exchange for the violets of your son.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֣ב מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה֮ בָּעֶ֒רֶב֒ וַתֵּצֵ֨א לֵאָ֜ה לִקְרָאת֗וֹ
pairs.english: And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out towards him,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵלַ֣י תָּב֔וֹא כִּ֚י שָׂכֹ֣ר שְׂכַרְתִּ֔יךָ בְּדוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י
pairs.english: and she said: To me shall you come, for I hired you with the violets of my son;
and he lay with her in that night, He [i.e., The L rd, "aided," Issachar issuing from that union].
And G d hearkened unto Leah, [who aspired to multiply tribes],
and she conceived and she bore a fifth son to Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהִים֙ שְׂכָרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי שִׁפְחָתִ֖י לְאִישִׁ֑י
pairs.english: And Leah said: G d has given my reward (s'chari) for having given my handmaid to my husband,
and she called his name Issachar.
And Leah conceived again,
and she bore a sixth son to Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה זְבָדַ֨נִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֹתִי֮ זֵ֣בֶד טוֹב֒
pairs.english: And Leah said: The L rd has given me a goodly portion.

pairs.hebrew: הַפַּ֙עַם֙ יִזְבְּלֵ֣נִי אִישִׁ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים
pairs.english: Now my husband will consort with me (yizbeleni), for I have borne him six sons [(over and against all of his wives)].
And she called his name Zevulun.
And then she bore a daughter,
and she called her name Dinah.
And G d remembered (it) unto Rachel [that she had given her "signs" to Leah and that she was distraught lest Esau take her],
and G d hearkened unto her and He opened her womb.
And she conceived and she bore a son,
and she said: G d has gathered in (asaf) my shame.
And she called his name Yosef, saying:
May the L rd add ("yosef") unto me another son [(Rachel knowing prophetically that there would be only twelve tribes)].
And it was, when Rachel bore Joseph [the "adversary" of Esau (see Ovadiah 1:18)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־לָבָ֔ן שַׁלְּחֵ֙נִי֙ וְאֵ֣לְכָ֔ה אֶל־מְקוֹמִ֖י וּלְאַרְצִֽי׃
pairs.english: that Jacob said to Lavan: Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land.

pairs.hebrew: תְּנָ֞ה אֶת־נָשַׁ֣י וְאֶת־יְלָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֧דְתִּי אֹֽתְךָ֛ בָּהֵ֖ן וְאֵלֵ֑כָה
pairs.english: Give me [by your leave] my wives and my children for whom I served you, and let me go.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת־עֲבֹדָתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַדְתִּֽיךָ׃
pairs.english: For you know the service which I have served you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לָבָ֔ן אִם־נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And Lavan said to him: If I have found favor in your eyes,
I have found through divination that the L rd has blessed me for your sake.
And he said: State your wage
and I will give it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲבַדְתִּ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And he said to him: You know how I have served you
and how [few] your kine were with me.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֡י מְעַט֩ אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֨ה לְךָ֤ לְפָנַי֙ וַיִּפְרֹ֣ץ לָרֹ֔ב
pairs.english: For the little that you had before has increased to a multitude,
and the L rd has blessed you with my coming,
and now, when will I also [in addition to my sons] do (what is needed) for my household?
And he said: What shall I give you?
And Jacob said: You will not give me anything.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אָשׁ֛וּבָה אֶרְעֶ֥ה צֹֽאנְךָ֖ אֶשְׁמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: If you do this thing for me, I will return and graze and guard your flock.
I will pass through all your flock today,

pairs.hebrew: הָסֵ֨ר מִשָּׁ֜ם כׇּל־שֶׂ֣ה ׀ נָקֹ֣ד וְטָל֗וּא וְכׇל־שֶׂה־חוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים וְטָל֥וּא וְנָקֹ֖ד בָּעִזִּ֑ים
pairs.english: removing from there every sheep speckled and spotted, and every sheep, brownish among the flock, and the spotted and speckled among the goats, [these to be given to your sons],
and that [i.e., those of the above kind born from now on] shall be my wage.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָֽנְתָה־בִּ֤י צִדְקָתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר כִּֽי־תָב֥וֹא עַל־שְׂכָרִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And my righteousness shall answer for me on the morrow. For it [my righteousness] will come [and testify] to my wage before you, [i.e.,]

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־אֵינֶ֩נּוּ֩ נָקֹ֨ד וְטָל֜וּא בָּֽעִזִּ֗ים וְחוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים גָּנ֥וּב ה֖וּא אִתִּֽי׃
pairs.english: anything [which you find in my flock] that is not speckled and spotted among the goats or brownish among the sheep is stolen with me.
And Lavan said: Agreed!
Would that you wished it so!

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣סַר בַּיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֶת־הַתְּיָשִׁ֜ים הָֽעֲקֻדִּ֣ים וְהַטְּלֻאִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ת כׇּל־הָֽעִזִּים֙ הַנְּקֻדּ֣וֹת וְהַטְּלֻאֹ֔ת
pairs.english: And he [Lavan] removed on that day the he-goats that were ringstraked and spotted, and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted —
everything that had white in it — and everything that was brownish among the sheep,
and he [Lavan] gave them into the hands of his sons.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֗שֶׂם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים בֵּינ֖וֹ וּבֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: And he put three days distance between himself and Jacob,
and Jacob grazed the flock of Lavan that were left [i.e., the sickly and barren ones].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב מַקַּ֥ל לִבְנֶ֛ה לַ֖ח וְל֣וּז וְעַרְמ֑וֹן
pairs.english: And Jacob took a moist stick of white poplar and [a stick of] almond and of chestnut,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְפַצֵּ֤ל בָּהֵן֙ פְּצָל֣וֹת לְבָנ֔וֹת מַחְשֹׂף֙ הַלָּבָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמַּקְלֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: and he peeled them into white streaks, baring the white on the sticks.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּצֵּ֗ג אֶת־הַמַּקְלוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּצֵּ֔ל בָּרְהָטִ֖ים בְּשִֽׁקְת֣וֹת הַמָּ֑יִם
pairs.english: And he set the sticks which he had peeled in the gutters of the watering troughs

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨אןָ הַצֹּ֤אן לִשְׁתּוֹת֙ לְנֹ֣כַח הַצֹּ֔אן
pairs.english: where the flocks came to drink, opposite the flocks,
and they became heated when they came to drink [i.e., the female recoiled at the sight of the sticks and the male mated with her, and she bore in their likeness].
And the flocks became heated at the [sight of the] sticks [(as above)],
and the flocks bore ringstraked, speckled, and spotted.
And Jacob separated the sheep [that were born ringstraked and spotted],

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יִּתֵּ֠ן פְּנֵ֨י הַצֹּ֧אן אֶל־עָקֹ֛ד וְכׇל־ח֖וּם בְּצֹ֣אן לָבָ֑ן
pairs.english: and he set the face of the flock [that followed them] to the ringstraked and to all of the brownish [that he had found] in the flock of Lavan,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּֽשֶׁת־ל֤וֹ עֲדָרִים֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁתָ֖ם עַל־צֹ֥אן לָבָֽן׃
pairs.english: having put them in flocks by themselves. And he did not place them with the flock of Lavan.
And it was, whenever the early (aroused) sheep became heated,

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׂ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֧ב אֶת־הַמַּקְל֛וֹת לְעֵינֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן בָּרְהָטִ֑ים לְיַחְמֵ֖נָּה בַּמַּקְלֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: that Jacob set the sticks before the eyes of the sheep in the gutters to become heated at [the sight of] the sticks. [see 38]
And when the sheep were late (to become heated), he did not set (them) —
and the (offspring of the) late ones were Lavan's, and the early ones, Jacob's.
And the man (Jacob) grew exceedingly strong,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־לוֹ֙ צֹ֣אן רַבּ֔וֹת וּשְׁפָחוֹת֙ וַעֲבָדִ֔ים וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃
pairs.english: and he had flocks [more] fruitful [than the norm], and [(by selling them at a high price)] maidservants, manservants, camels, and asses.
And he heard the words of the sons of Lavan, saying:
Jacob has taken all that is our father's,

pairs.hebrew: וּמֵאֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔ינוּ עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת כׇּל־הַכָּבֹ֖ד הַזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: and from our father's did he gather all this substance.
And Jacob saw the face of Lavan,
and, behold, it was not with him as of yore.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב שׁ֛וּב אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ אֲבוֹתֶ֖יךָ וּלְמוֹלַדְתֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And the L rd said to Jacob: Return to the land of your fathers and to your birthplace
and I shall be with you, [it not being possible to repose my Shechinah with you while you are "linked to uncleanliness"].
And Jacob sent and he called to Rachel and to Leah
to the field to his flock.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ן רֹאֶ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י אֲבִיכֶ֔ן כִּֽי־אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֵלַ֖י כִּתְמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֑ם
pairs.english: And he said to them: I see that your father's face is not with me as of yore;
and my father's G d was with me.
And you know
that with all my strength did I serve your father.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲבִיכֶן֙ הֵ֣תֶל בִּ֔י וְהֶחֱלִ֥ף אֶת־מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּ֖י עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת מֹנִ֑ים
pairs.english: And your father deceived me and he changed my hire ten tens [i.e., a hundred times],
but G d did not allow him to do evil with me.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר נְקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כׇל־הַצֹּ֖אן נְקֻדִּ֑ים
pairs.english: If he said thus: "The speckled shall be your hire," then all the flocks bore speckled.

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר עֲקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כׇל־הַצֹּ֖אן עֲקֻדִּֽים׃
pairs.english: And if he said thus: "The ringstraked shall be your hire," then all the flocks bore ringstraked.
And G d delivered the kine of your father
and He gave them to me.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵת֙ יַחֵ֣ם הַצֹּ֔אן וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲל֑וֹם
pairs.english: And it was, at the time the flocks were heated, I lifted up my eyes and I saw in a dream:

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל־הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּֽים׃
pairs.english: Behold, the rams which went up on the sheep were ringstraked, speckled, and grizzled.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י מַלְאַ֧ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּחֲל֖וֹם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: And an angel of G d said to me in a dream: "Jacob."
And I said: "Here I am."

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שָׂא־נָ֨א עֵינֶ֤יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ כׇּל־הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל־הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And he said: Lift up your eyes now and see all the rams that go up on the sheep — ringstraked, speckled, and grizzled —

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י רָאִ֔יתִי אֵ֛ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָבָ֖ן עֹ֥שֶׂה לָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: for I have seen all that Lavan does to you.

pairs.hebrew: אָנֹכִ֤י הָאֵל֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָשַׁ֤חְתָּ שָּׁם֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָדַ֥רְתָּ לִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם נֶ֑דֶר
pairs.english: I am the G d of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar where you vowed a vow unto Me, [which it is now time to fulfill (see 28:22)].

pairs.hebrew: עַתָּ֗ה ק֥וּם צֵא֙ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְשׁ֖וּב אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ מוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃
pairs.english: Now, arise, go out of this land and return to the land of your birth.
And Rachel and Leah answered and said to him:

pairs.hebrew: הַע֥וֹד לָ֛נוּ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽינוּ׃
pairs.english: Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house? [Why, then, should we detain you?]
Does he not regard us as strangers?
For [he did not give us a dowry as is customary, but] he sold us [to you for your labor], and he also consumed our money, [withholding your wages].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י כׇל־הָעֹ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּ֤יל אֱלֹהִים֙ מֵֽאָבִ֔ינוּ לָ֥נוּ ה֖וּא וּלְבָנֵ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: But [only] all of the wealth that G d confiscated from our father is ours and our children's.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה׃
pairs.english: And now, everything that G d says to you, do.
And Jacob arose
and he lifted his sons and his wives onto the camels.
And he conveyed all of his kine and all of the substance that he had gotten,

pairs.hebrew: מִקְנֵה֙ קִנְיָנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם
pairs.english: the acquisition [maidservants, etc.] of his accession [the flocks (see 30:43)], which he had acquired in Padan Aram,
to come to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.
And Lavan had gone to shear his sheep [a three days distance (see 30:26)],
and Rachel stole her father's teraphim [to break him of idolatry].
And Jacob stole the heart of Lavan the Aramite,

pairs.hebrew: עַל־בְּלִי֙ הִגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י בֹרֵ֖חַ הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: not telling him that he fled.
And he fled, he and all that was with him,
and he arose and crossed over the river,
and he set his face towards Mount Gilead.
And it was told to Lavan on the third day
that Jacob had fled.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף אַחֲרָ֔יו דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And he took his brethren with him and pursued him, [covering] a distance of seven days [in one day],
and he overtook him in Mount Gilead.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־לָבָ֥ן הָאֲרַמִּ֖י בַּחֲלֹ֣ם הַלָּ֑יְלָה
pairs.english: And G d came to Lavan the Aramite in a dream by night

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ פֶּן־תְּדַבֵּ֥ר עִֽם־יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד־רָֽע׃
pairs.english: and He said to him: Take heed lest you speak with Jacob from good to evil. ["All the good of the wicked is evil to the righteous."]
And Lavan overtook Jacob.
And Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain.
And Lavan pitched (his tent) with his brethren in Mount Gilead.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֶת־לְבָבִ֑י
pairs.english: And Lavan said to Jacob: What have you done, that you have stolen my heart
and led away my daughters like captives of the sword?

pairs.hebrew: לָ֤מָּה נַחְבֵּ֙אתָ֙ לִבְרֹ֔חַ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֹתִ֑י וְלֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י
pairs.english: Why did you flee in secret, stealing ["my mind"] from me and not telling me?
I would have sent you away with joy and song, with timbrel and lyre.
And you did not allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters.
You have now done foolishly.
I have the power to do evil with you,

pairs.hebrew: וֵֽאלֹהֵ֨י אֲבִיכֶ֜ם אֶ֣מֶשׁ ׀ אָמַ֧ר אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֗ר
pairs.english: but the G d of your father said to me last night:

pairs.hebrew: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ מִדַּבֵּ֥ר עִֽם־יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד־רָֽע׃
pairs.english: Take care not to speak to Jacob from good to ill.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּה֙ הָלֹ֣ךְ הָלַ֔כְתָּ כִּֽי־נִכְסֹ֥ף נִכְסַ֖פְתָּה לְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And now, though you be gone, for you longed for your father's house,
why have you stolen my gods?

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֥עַן יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֑ן כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔אתִי
pairs.english: And Jacob answered and he said to Lavan [(answering first things first)]: For I was afraid.
For I said: Lest you steal your daughters from me.

pairs.hebrew: עִ֠ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֣א אֶת־אֱלֹהֶ֘יךָ֮ לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶה֒
pairs.english: With whomever you find your gods, let him not live [(for which reason Rachel died on the road)].

pairs.hebrew: נֶ֣גֶד אַחֵ֧ינוּ הַֽכֶּר־לְךָ֛ מָ֥ה עִמָּדִ֖י וְקַֽח־לָ֑ךְ
pairs.english: Before our kinsmen, point out what is with me [that is yours], and take it for yourself.
And Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֨א לָבָ֜ן בְּאֹ֥הֶל יַעֲקֹ֣ב ׀ וּבְאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֗ה וּבְאֹ֛הֶל שְׁתֵּ֥י הָאֲמָהֹ֖ת וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑א
pairs.english: And Lavan came into Jacob's [i.e., Rachel's] tent and into the tent of Leah and into the tent of the two handmaids, but he found nothing.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֹ֥הֶל רָחֵֽל׃
pairs.english: And (when) he went out of the tent of Leah, he came [again] into the tent of Rachel, [knowing her to be a "toucher"].

pairs.hebrew: וְרָחֵ֞ל לָקְחָ֣ה אֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֗ים וַתְּשִׂמֵ֛ם בְּכַ֥ר הַגָּמָ֖ל וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Rachel had taken the teraphim, and she had placed them on the camel's saddle-pillow and sat upon them.
And Lavan "felt out" the whole tent and could not find them.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־אָבִ֗יהָ אַל־יִ֙חַר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא אוּכַל֙ לָק֣וּם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ
pairs.english: And she said to her father: Let it not anger my lord that I cannot rise before you,
for I am in the way of women.
And he searched, and he could not find the teraphim.
And Jacob was wroth and he strove with Lavan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַן יַעֲקֹב֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֔ן מַה־פִּשְׁעִי֙ מַ֣ה חַטָּאתִ֔י כִּ֥י דָלַ֖קְתָּ אַחֲרָֽי׃
pairs.english: And Jacob retorted and said to Lavan: What is my offense and what is my sin that you have pursued me?
For you have "felt out" all my articles. What have you found of all your household articles?

pairs.hebrew: שִׂ֣ים כֹּ֔ה נֶ֥גֶד אַחַ֖י וְאַחֶ֑יךָ וְיוֹכִ֖יחוּ בֵּ֥ין שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃
pairs.english: Put it here before my brethren and yours, and let them judge between us.
This twenty years have I been with you.
Your ewes and your she-goats have not miscarried,
and the rams [(even a one-year-old being called a "ram")] of your flock I have not eaten.
An animal that was torn [by lion or wolf] I did not bring to you.
I bore its loss; from my hand did you require it.
Whether stolen by day or by night, [I paid for it].

pairs.hebrew: הָיִ֧יתִי בַיּ֛וֹם אֲכָלַ֥נִי חֹ֖רֶב וְקֶ֣רַח בַּלָּ֑יְלָה
pairs.english: In the day I was consumed by heat and in the night by frost,
and sleep departed from my eyes.

pairs.hebrew: זֶה־לִּ֞י עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָה֮ בְּבֵיתֶ֒ךָ֒ עֲבַדְתִּ֜יךָ אַרְבַּֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים בְּצֹאנֶ֑ךָ
pairs.english: This twenty years have I served you in your house — fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks;
and you changed [the conditions of] my hire ten tens [i.e., a hundred times].

pairs.hebrew: לוּלֵ֡י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִי֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וּפַ֤חַד יִצְחָק֙ הָ֣יָה לִ֔י
pairs.english: Had not the G d of my father, the G d of Abraham and the Dread of Yitzchak been with me,
you would now have sent me away empty.

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־עׇנְיִ֞י וְאֶת־יְגִ֧יעַ כַּפַּ֛י רָאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַיּ֥וֹכַח אָֽמֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: G d saw my affliction and the toil of my hands and He reproved (you) last night.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨עַן לָבָ֜ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַבָּנ֨וֹת בְּנֹתַ֜י וְהַבָּנִ֤ים בָּנַי֙ וְהַצֹּ֣אן צֹאנִ֔י וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לִי־ה֑וּא
pairs.english: And Lavan answered and he said to Jacob: The daughters are my daughters, and the sons are my sons, and the flocks are my flocks, and everything you see is mine.

pairs.hebrew: וְלִבְנֹתַ֞י מָֽה־אֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה לָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם א֥וֹ לִבְנֵיהֶ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלָֽדוּ׃
pairs.english: And, as for my daughters, what can I do to these today or to their children that they shall bear [i.e., How can it enter my mind to harm them?]

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֛ה נִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית אֲנִ֣י וָאָ֑תָּה
pairs.english: And now, come, let us make a covenant, I and you,
and let Him be a witness between me and you.
And Jacob took a stone
and he set it up as a monument.
And Jacob said to his brethren [i.e., his sons]: Gather stones.
And they took stones and made a heap.
And they ate there on the heap.
And Lavan called it Yegar Sahadutha ("the heap of testimony"),
and Jacob called it Gal Ed [(the same)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן הַגַּ֨ל הַזֶּ֥ה עֵ֛ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינְךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם
pairs.english: And Lavan said: This heap is testimony between me and you this day —
wherefore its name is called Gal Ed.

pairs.hebrew: וְהַמִּצְפָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔ר יִ֥צֶף יְהֹוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ
pairs.english: And (it is also called) Mitzpah, [one of them] having said [to the other]: May the L rd see [yitzef] between me and you
when one of us is absent from the other.
If you afflict my daughters [by withholding their conjugal times] and if you take wives in addition to my daughters [(Bilhah and Zilpah, too, were his daughters by a concubine)],
no man being with us,
see, G d is a witness between me and you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ הַמַּצֵּבָ֔ה
pairs.english: And Lavan said to Jacob: Behold this heap and behold this monument
which I have set up between me and you.
This heap is testimony and the monument is testimony
that I will not cross this heap to you

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־אַ֠תָּ֠ה לֹא־תַעֲבֹ֨ר אֵלַ֜י אֶת־הַגַּ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה וְאֶת־הַמַּצֵּבָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרָעָֽה׃
pairs.english: and you will not cross to me this heap and this monument for ill. [(You may not cross it for ill, but you may cross it for trade.)]

pairs.hebrew: אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י נָחוֹר֙ יִשְׁפְּט֣וּ בֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: The G d of Abraham and the god of Nachor judge between us, the god of their father [Terach].
And Jacob swore by the Dread of his father, Isaac.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּזְבַּ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֥ב זֶ֙בַח֙ בָּהָ֔ר וַיִּקְרָ֥א לְאֶחָ֖יו לֶאֱכׇל־לָ֑חֶם
pairs.english: And Jacob slaughtered a slaughtering in the mountain and he called his brethren [his close friends who were with Lavan] to partake of the meal,
and they partook of the meal and spent the night in the mountain.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם לָבָ֜ן בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיְנַשֵּׁ֧ק לְבָנָ֛יו וְלִבְנוֹתָ֖יו וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶתְהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Lavan arose early in the morning and he kissed his sons and his daughters and he blessed them
and he went, and Lavan returned to his place.
And Jacob went on his way,
and angels of G d [from Eretz Yisrael] met him [to accompany him to Eretz Yisrael].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאָ֔ם מַחֲנֵ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים זֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And Jacob said when he saw them: "This is a camp of G d,"
and he called the place Machanayim [lit., "two camps," those (angels) from outside Eretz Yisrael, who accompanied him until there, and those from Eretz Israel, who came to meet him].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֤ב מַלְאָכִים֙ לְפָנָ֔יו אֶל־עֵשָׂ֖ו אָחִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Jacob sent angels before him to Esau his brother
to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֤ו אֹתָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֔וּן לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לְעֵשָׂ֑ו
pairs.english: And he charged them, saying: Thus shall you say to my lord, to Esau:
Thus said your servant Jacob:
With Lavan did I sojourn [(You need not hate me for the blessing of mastery over my brothers (27:29), it not having been fulfilled in me; I was merely a sojourner)], and I delayed until now.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־לִי֙ שׁ֣וֹר וַחֲמ֔וֹר צֹ֖אן וְעֶ֣בֶד וְשִׁפְחָ֑ה
pairs.english: And I had [only] ox and ass, flock and manservant and maidservant, [but not "of the dew of the heavens and the fats of the earth" promised me by our father (27:28)],
and I have sent to tell my lord to find favor in your eyes [as a seeker of your love].

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּ֤אנוּ אֶל־אָחִ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־עֵשָׂ֔ו
pairs.english: And the angels returned to Jacob, saying: We came to [the one you called] your brother, [but found that we had come] to Esau [the wicked one],

pairs.hebrew: וְגַם֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ לִקְרָֽאתְךָ֔ וְאַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת אִ֖ישׁ עִמּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and he is also coming out against you, and four hundred men with him.
And Jacob feared greatly [that he might be killed], and he was distressed [that he might kill others],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֜חַץ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ וְאֶת־הַצֹּ֧אן וְאֶת־הַבָּקָ֛ר וְהַגְּמַלִּ֖ים לִשְׁנֵ֥י מַחֲנֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: and he divided the people that were with him and the flocks and the cattle and the camels into two camps.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אִם־יָב֥וֹא עֵשָׂ֛ו אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הָאַחַ֖ת וְהִכָּ֑הוּ
pairs.english: And he said: If Esau comes to the one camp and smites it [in battle],
then the remaining camp will escape, [(Jacob taking three defensive measures: gift (21), prayer (9), preparation for war (above)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֘אמֶר֮ יַעֲקֹב֒ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אָבִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם וֵאלֹהֵ֖י אָבִ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק
pairs.english: And Jacob said: The G d of my father Abraham and the G d of my father Isaac, [who under this appellation (28:13), promised to abet me (Ibid. 15)],

pairs.hebrew: יְהֹוָ֞ה הָאֹמֵ֣ר אֵלַ֗י שׁ֧וּב לְאַרְצְךָ֛ וּלְמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֖ וְאֵיטִ֥יבָה עִמָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: the L rd, who said to me [under that appellation (32:3)]: Return to your land and to your birthplace and I shall do good with you —

pairs.hebrew: קָטֹ֜נְתִּי מִכֹּ֤ל הַחֲסָדִים֙ וּמִכׇּל־הָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: I have become small [i.e., my merits have diminished] because of all of the lovingkindnesses and all of the truth [the fulfillment of all Your assurances] that You have done with Your servant.
For with my staff did I cross this Jordan,
and now I have become two camps.

pairs.hebrew: הַצִּילֵ֥נִי נָ֛א מִיַּ֥ד אָחִ֖י מִיַּ֣ד עֵשָׂ֑ו
pairs.english: Deliver me, I pray You, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau [i.e., from him who deports himself to me not as my brother, but as the wicked Esau.]

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־יָרֵ֤א אָנֹכִי֙ אֹת֔וֹ פֶּן־יָב֣וֹא וְהִכַּ֔נִי אֵ֖ם עַל־בָּנִֽים׃
pairs.english: For I fear him, lest he come and smite me, mother with children.
And You said: (I shall do) good [in your merit], I shall do good [in your fathers' merits] with you,

pairs.hebrew: וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃
pairs.english: and I shall make your seed as the sand of the sea which cannot be counted for multitude [see 28:15 and 22:17].
And he slept there that night,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִן־הַבָּ֧א בְיָד֛וֹ מִנְחָ֖ה לְעֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיו׃
pairs.english: and he took from what he possessed a present for Esau his brother.
Two hundred she-goats and twenty he-goats, [the requisite number of mates],
two hundred ewes and twenty rams.
Thirty milch camels with their colts,
forty cows and ten bulls,
twenty she-asses and ten he-asses.
And he gave them into the hands of his servants, each herd [of each kind] by itself.
And he said to his servants: Pass by before me [about a day's journey or less],

pairs.hebrew: וְרֶ֣וַח תָּשִׂ֔ימוּ בֵּ֥ין עֵ֖דֶר וּבֵ֥ין עֵֽדֶר׃
pairs.english: and make a space [as far as the eye can see] between herd and herd [to impress Esau with the bounty].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֥ו אֶת־הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּ֣י יִֽפְגׇשְׁךָ֞ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֗י וּשְׁאֵֽלְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר
pairs.english: And he charged the first, saying: If Esau my brother meets you and asks you:
To whom do you belong, and where are you going,
and for whom are these before you?
Then you shall say, [answering first things first, and last, last]: [We belong] to our servant Jacob,
[and these before us are] a present sent to my lord, Esau,
and, behold, he [Jacob], too, is behind us.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֞ו גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַשֵּׁנִ֗י גַּ֚ם אֶת־הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י גַּ֚ם אֶת־כׇּל־הַהֹ֣לְכִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֥י הָעֲדָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: And he charged the second, also the third, also all who went behind the flocks, saying:

pairs.hebrew: כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ תְּדַבְּר֣וּן אֶל־עֵשָׂ֔ו בְּמֹצַאֲכֶ֖ם אֹתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: Thus shall you speak to Esau when you find him.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם גַּ֗ם הִנֵּ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אַחֲרֵ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: And you shall say also: Behold, your servant Jacob is behind us.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־אָמַ֞ר אֲכַפְּרָ֣ה פָנָ֗יו בַּמִּנְחָה֙ הַהֹלֶ֣כֶת לְפָנָ֔י
pairs.english: For he said: I will remove his anger with the gift that goes before me,

pairs.hebrew: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ אֶרְאֶ֣ה פָנָ֔יו אוּלַ֖י יִשָּׂ֥א פָנָֽי׃
pairs.english: and then I will see his face. Perhaps he will be accepting of me.
And the present passed before him,
and he slept that night in the camp.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣קׇם ׀ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה ה֗וּא וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֤י נָשָׁיו֙ וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י שִׁפְחֹתָ֔יו וְאֶת־אַחַ֥ד עָשָׂ֖ר יְלָדָ֑יו
pairs.english: And he arose that night and took his wives and his two handmaids, and his eleven children [(having secreted Dinah in a chest so that Esau not take her)],
and he crossed the ford of Yabbok.
And he took them and passed them over the stream,
and he passed over what was his, [the beasts and the chattel].
And Jacob remained alone, [having returned for some small jars],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּאָבֵ֥ק אִישׁ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ עַ֖ד עֲל֥וֹת הַשָּֽׁחַר׃
pairs.english: and a man [Esau's guardian angel] wrestled with him until the rising of the morning star.
And he saw that he could not prevail over him,
and he touched the hollow [the upper bone] of his thigh;
and the hollow of Jacob's thigh tore loose as he wrestled with him.
And he said: Release me, for the morning star has risen, [and I must intone song (to G d) in the daytime.]
And he said: I will not release you until you bless me [i.e., until you acquiesce in my father's blessings to me and cease contesting them.]
And he said to him: What is your name?
And he said: Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ יֵאָמֵ֥ר עוֹד֙ שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And he said: Your name shall no longer be called Jacob [connoting gaining of the blessings by deception (akvah)], but Yisrael;
for you have contended (saritha) with elohim (the angel of Esau) and with men [Esau and Lavan] and you have prevailed.
And Jacob asked: "Tell me, I pray you, your name."
And he said: "Why do you ask my name?" [(the names of the angels changing according to their deputation)],
and he (the angel) blessed him there.
And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־רָאִ֤יתִי אֱלֹהִים֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל־פָּנִ֔ים וַתִּנָּצֵ֖ל נַפְשִֽׁי׃
pairs.english: For I saw elohim face to face (panim el panim), and my soul was spared.
And the dawn broke for him when he crossed Penuel,
and he was limping on his thigh.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּ֡ן לֹֽא־יֹאכְל֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־גִּ֣יד הַנָּשֶׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־כַּ֣ף הַיָּרֵ֔ךְ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: Therefore, the children of Israel do not eat the "slipping tendon" on the hollow of the thigh until this day.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י נָגַע֙ בְּכַף־יֶ֣רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּגִ֖יד הַנָּשֶֽׁה׃
pairs.english: For he touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh on the slipping tendon.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עֵשָׂ֣ו בָּ֔א וְעִמּ֕וֹ אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ
pairs.english: And Jacob lifted his eyes and he saw, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men;

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣חַץ אֶת־הַיְלָדִ֗ים עַל־לֵאָה֙ וְעַל־רָחֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֥י הַשְּׁפָחֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: and he divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two handmaids.
And he placed the handmaids and their children first,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־לֵאָ֤ה וִֽילָדֶ֙יהָ֙ אַחֲרֹנִ֔ים וְאֶת־רָחֵ֥ל וְאֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף אַחֲרֹנִֽים׃
pairs.english: and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph behind, [the most beloved hindmost].
And he passed before them, [placing himself first for the contingency of war],

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁתַּ֤חוּ אַ֙רְצָה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים עַד־גִּשְׁתּ֖וֹ עַד־אָחִֽיו׃
pairs.english: and he bowed down to the earth seven times until he came near to his brother.
And Esau ran towards him and embraced him,
and he fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
And he lifted his eyes and he saw the women and the children,
and he said: "What are these to you?"
And he said: The children that G d granted to your servant.
And the handmaids drew near, they and their children,
and they prostrated themselves.
And Leah and her children also drew near and they prostrated themselves.

And afterwards Joseph and Rachel drew near [(Joseph before Rachel, as opposed to the others, where the women went first, Joseph desiring to shield Rachel (who was very beautiful) from the gaze of Esau)], and they prostrated themselves.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לְךָ֛ כׇּל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגָ֑שְׁתִּי
pairs.english: And he said: Who is all this camp of yours [the bearers of the gifts] that I have met?
And he said: To find favor in the eyes of my lord.
And Esau said: I have much [more than I need],
my brother; let there be yours what is yours, [Esau acknowledging the blessing as Jacob's due].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֗ב אַל־נָא֙ אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ מִנְחָתִ֖י מִיָּדִ֑י
pairs.english: And Jacob said: Do not [speak thus], I pray you. If I have found favor in your eyes, take my gift from my hand.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י עַל־כֵּ֞ן רָאִ֣יתִי פָנֶ֗יךָ כִּרְאֹ֛ת פְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים
pairs.english: For it is fitting [that you do so], (for) I have seen your face, and [this is as grand in my eyes] as having seen the face of an angel [(the guardian angel of Esau, 32:24)];
and [it is also fitting that you accept my gift] because you have been conciliated by me.
Take my [greeting-] gift, I pray you, which has been brought to you [without any exertion on your part],
for the L rd has been gracious to me, and I have all [that I need].
And he pressed him, and he took it.
And he said: Travel on and go,
