pairs.english: And he lifted up his eyes and he saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲזֶה֙ אֲחִיכֶ֣ם הַקָּטֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: and he said: Is this your younger brother of whom you spoke to me?
And he said: "May G d grace you, my son," [it already having been said of the other tribes (33:5): "with which G d graced your servant"].
And Joseph hastened, for his mercies had become enkindled for his brother
and he wished to cry,
and he went into his chamber and he wept there.
And he washed his face, and he went out
and he "fortified" himself, and he said: Serve bread.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ ל֛וֹ לְבַדּ֖וֹ וְלָהֶ֣ם לְבַדָּ֑ם וְלַמִּצְרִ֞ים הָאֹכְלִ֤ים אִתּוֹ֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם
pairs.english: And they served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him, by themselves.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכְל֜וּן הַמִּצְרִ֗ים לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־הָֽעִבְרִים֙ לֶ֔חֶם
pairs.english: For the Egyptians could not eat with the Hebrews,
for it was an abomination to the Egyptians, [the Hebrews eating sheep, which the Egyptians worshiped].
And they sat [i.e., he sat them in order] before him,
the first-born according to his seniority, and the youngest, according to his youth;
and the men expressed amaze one to the other.
And he took portions from before him to them,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֜רֶב מַשְׂאַ֧ת בִּנְיָמִ֛ן מִמַּשְׂאֹ֥ת כֻּלָּ֖ם חָמֵ֣שׁ יָד֑וֹת
pairs.english: and the portion of Benjamin was five times that of the others, [Benjamin receiving his own portion, and, in addition, those sent him by Joseph, Asnath, Menasheh, and Ephraim],
and they drank and became inebriated with him, [neither he nor they having drunk wine from the day he was sold].
And he charged the one over his house, saying:

pairs.hebrew: מַלֵּ֞א אֶת־אַמְתְּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֹ֔כֶל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּכְל֖וּן שְׂאֵ֑ת
pairs.english: Fill the sacks of the men with food, as much as they can carry,
and place each one's money in the mouth of his sack.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־גְּבִיעִ֞י גְּבִ֣יעַ הַכֶּ֗סֶף תָּשִׂים֙ בְּפִי֙ אַמְתַּ֣חַת הַקָּטֹ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף שִׁבְר֑וֹ
pairs.english: And my goblet, the silver goblet, place in the mouth of the sack of the youngest and the money of his grain purchase.
And he did according to the word of Joseph, who had spoken.
Morning dawned
and the men were sent away, they and their asses.
They had left the city and had not gone far
when Joseph said to the one over his house:
Arise, pursue the men,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִשַּׂגְתָּם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה שִׁלַּמְתֶּ֥ם רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה׃
pairs.english: and when you overtake them, say to them: Why did you pay evil for good?

pairs.hebrew: הֲל֣וֹא זֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁתֶּ֤ה אֲדֹנִי֙ בּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: Is not this what my master drinks in
and through which he divines?
You have done evil by what you have done.
And he overtook them,
and he spoke these things to them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו לָ֚מָּה יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲדֹנִ֔י כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה
pairs.english: And they said to him: Why should my lord speak such things?
It would be profane in your servants to do such a thing!

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֣ן כֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָצָ֙אנוּ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֔ינוּ הֱשִׁיבֹ֥נוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: Behold, the money which we found in the mouth of our sacks we returned to you from the land of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗יךְ נִגְנֹב֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כֶּ֖סֶף א֥וֹ זָהָֽב׃
pairs.english: How, then, would we steal from your master's house silver or gold!
With whomever it is found of your servants, he shall die,
and we, too, shall be servants to my lord.
And he said: This, too, is as you say; it is true [that if one among ten is found to have stolen, all should be apprehended, but I shall be liberal, and only]
the one with whom it is found shall be my slave,
and you will be absolved.
And they hastened, and each brought his sack down to the ground,
and each opened his sack.
And he searched, beginning with the oldest, [so that they not suspect him of knowing where it was],
and finishing with the youngest,
and the goblet was found in Benjamin's sack.
And they rent their garments,
and each [individually, without requiring another's assistance] laded his ass,
and they returned to the city [(really a metropolis, but, in their eyes, merely a "city" (of ten) in its defenselessness before them)].
And Judah and his brothers came to the house of Joseph,
and he was still there [waiting for them],
and they fell before him to the ground.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף מָֽה־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Joseph said to them: What is this deed that you have done?

pairs.hebrew: הֲל֣וֹא יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּֽי־נַחֵ֧שׁ יְנַחֵ֛שׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֹֽנִי׃
pairs.english: Did you not know that a man such as I could divine [that you had stolen the goblet]?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֗ה מַה־נֹּאמַר֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י מַה־נְּדַבֵּ֖ר וּמַה־נִּצְטַדָּ֑ק
pairs.english: And Judah said: What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak and how shall we justify ourselves?
[We did not sin in this instance (of the goblet), but] G d has found [a way to exact punishment for] the [former] sin of your servants.

pairs.hebrew: הִנֶּ֤נּוּ עֲבָדִים֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י גַּם־אֲנַ֕חְנוּ גַּ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־נִמְצָ֥א הַגָּבִ֖יעַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: We are slaves to my lord, both we, both him in whose hand the goblet has been found.
And he said: It were profane in me to do this!

pairs.hebrew: הָאִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִמְצָ֨א הַגָּבִ֜יעַ בְּיָד֗וֹ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י עָ֔בֶד
pairs.english: The man in whose hand the goblet is found — he shall be my servant.
And you, go up in peace to your father.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ אֵלָ֜יו יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיֹּ֘אמֶר֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִי֒
pairs.english: And Judah drew near to him and he said: I entreat you, my lord,
let your servant speak a word [that will enter] in the ears of my lord.
And let not your wrath burn against your servant [— whence we may infer that he spoke "strong words" to him],
for you are [as eminent in my eyes] as Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants:

Do you have a father or a brother? [From the very beginning you were plotting against us. Why did you ask all these questions? Were we asking for your daughter in marriage? Or were you asking for our sister?]

pairs.hebrew: וַנֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֔י יֶשׁ־לָ֙נוּ֙ אָ֣ב זָקֵ֔ן וְיֶ֥לֶד זְקֻנִ֖ים קָטָ֑ן
pairs.english: And [in spite of this, we concealed nothing from you, but] we said to my lord: We have an old father and a small child of his old age,
and his brother died [(Judah lying here out of fear that he be told to bring him too)],
and he alone was left to his mother, [Benjamin having no other brother from that mother],
and his father loves him.
And you said to your servants: Bring him down to me
that I may set my eye upon him.

pairs.hebrew: וַנֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל הַנַּ֖עַר לַעֲזֹ֣ב אֶת־אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And we said to my lord: The youth will not be able to leave his father,
for if he leaves his father he may die [on the road (as his mother did)].

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ אִם־לֹ֥א יֵרֵ֛ד אֲחִיכֶ֥ם הַקָּטֹ֖ן אִתְּכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And you said to your servants: If your younger brother does not come down with you,
you shall see my face no more.
And it was, when we went up to your servant, my father,
and we told him the words of my lord,
that our father said:
Return, buy for us a little food.
And we said: We cannot go down.
If our younger brother is with us then we will go down.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־לֹ֣א נוּכַ֗ל לִרְאוֹת֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְאָחִ֥ינוּ הַקָּטֹ֖ן אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אִתָּֽנוּ׃
pairs.english: For we will not be able to see the man's face if our younger brother is not with us.
And your servant, my father, said to us:

pairs.hebrew: אַתֶּ֣ם יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁנַ֖יִם יָֽלְדָה־לִּ֥י אִשְׁתִּֽי׃
pairs.english: You know that my wife (Rachel) bore me two sons.
And the one went from me.
And I said: Surely, he has been torn.
And I have not seen him until now.
And if you take this one, too, from me,
then a mishap will befall him, [for "Satan prosecutes in time of danger"],
and you will bring down my hoary head with evil to the grave. [Benjamin is my consolation for Rachel and Joseph. If he dies, it is as if they all died in one day.]
And now, if I come to your servant, my father,
and the youth is not with us,
and his soul is bound up with his soul —
Then it shall be, if he sees that the youth is not (with us), he will die,

pairs.hebrew: וְהוֹרִ֨ידוּ עֲבָדֶ֜יךָ אֶת־שֵׂיבַ֨ת עַבְדְּךָ֥ אָבִ֛ינוּ בְּיָג֖וֹן שְׁאֹֽלָה׃
pairs.english: and your servants will have brought down the hoary head of your servant, our father, with sorrow to the grave.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י עַבְדְּךָ֙ עָרַ֣ב אֶת־הַנַּ֔עַר מֵעִ֥ם אָבִ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: [And I am more importunate in this than my other brothers], for your servant has gone surety for the youth to my father, saying:
If I do not bring him back to you,
then I will have sinned against my father all of the days, [to be cut off in both worlds].

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה יֵֽשֶׁב־נָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַנַּ֔עַר עֶ֖בֶד לַֽאדֹנִ֑י
pairs.english: And now, let your servant stay, I pray you, instead of the youth as a servant to my lord,
and let the youth go up with his brothers.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־אֵיךְ֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל־אָבִ֔י וְהַנַּ֖עַר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ אִתִּ֑י
pairs.english: For how can I go up to my father if the youth is not with me —

pairs.hebrew: פֶּ֚ן אֶרְאֶ֣ה בָרָ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְצָ֖א אֶת־אָבִֽי׃
pairs.english: lest I see the evil that shall befall my father.

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־יָכֹ֨ל יוֹסֵ֜ף לְהִתְאַפֵּ֗ק לְכֹ֤ל הַנִּצָּבִים֙ עָלָ֔יו
pairs.english: And Joseph could not tolerate all [i.e., the Egyptians] standing over him [and witnessing his brothers' shame in his revealing himself to them],
and he called: "Take out every man from my presence!"

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹא־עָ֤מַד אִישׁ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ בְּהִתְוַדַּ֥ע יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶל־אֶחָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And no man stood with him when Joseph revealed himself to his brothers.
And he raised his voice in weeping,
and (the men of) Egypt heard it,
and the household of Pharaoh heard it.
And Joseph said to his brothers: "I am Joseph.
Is my father still alive?"

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ לַעֲנ֣וֹת אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִבְהֲל֖וּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And his brothers could not answer him, for they were confounded [with shame] before him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶל־אֶחָ֛יו גְּשׁוּ־נָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וַיִּגָּ֑שׁוּ
pairs.english: And Joseph said to his brothers, [seeing them recoiling from him in shame]: "Draw near to me, I pray you." And they drew near,
and he said, [showing them his circumcision]: I am Joseph your brother,
whom you sold to Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ אַל־תֵּעָ֣צְב֗וּ וְאַל־יִ֙חַר֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י הֵ֑נָּה
pairs.english: And now, do not be grieved, and do not vex yourselves that you sold me here,
because for sustenance did G d send me before you.
For two years have passed thus far of the [years of] famine in the midst of the land,

pairs.hebrew: וְעוֹד֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־חָרִ֖ישׁ וְקָצִֽיר׃
pairs.english: and five years are yet to come in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
And G d has sent me before you
to provide for you a remnant in the land
and to keep you in life for a great deliverance.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹֽא־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִי֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים
pairs.english: And now, it is not you who sent me here, but G d.
And He made me a "father" [a friend and patron] to Pharaoh
and a master to all his house, and a ruler throughout the land of Egypt.
Hasten and go up to my father [(Eretz Yisrael is the highest of all the lands)],

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ בִּנְךָ֣ יוֹסֵ֔ף
pairs.english: and say to him: Thus said your son Joseph:
G d has made me master of all Egypt —
come down to me; do not wait.
And you will sit in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me,
you and your children and your children's children,
and your flocks and your herds and all that you have.
And I will provide for you there.
For five years of famine yet remain —
lest you and your household and all that you have become impoverished.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֤ה עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ רֹא֔וֹת וְעֵינֵ֖י אָחִ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין
pairs.english: And, behold, your eyes see and the eyes of my brother Benjamin [(Just as I bear no rancor towards Benjamin, who was not a party to my being sold, so I bear none towards you)]
that [I am honored and that I am circumcised as you are, and that] the mouth that speaks to you [speaks in the holy tongue].

pairs.hebrew: וְהִגַּדְתֶּ֣ם לְאָבִ֗י אֶת־כׇּל־כְּבוֹדִי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְאִיתֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And tell my father of all my glory in Egypt and of all that you have seen.
And hasten and bring down my father here.
And he fell on the neck of his brother Benjamin, and he wept [over the two Temples that were destined to be in the portion of Benjamin, which would be destroyed],
and Benjamin wept on his neck, [over the sanctuary of Shiloh, that was destined to be in the portion of Joseph, which would be destroyed.]
And he kissed all his brothers and he wept upon them,
and afterwards, [i.e., after they saw him weeping and well disposed towards them,] his brothers spoke with him, [having been ashamed to do so previously].

pairs.hebrew: וְהַקֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמַ֗ע בֵּ֤ית פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֖אוּ אֲחֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף
pairs.english: And the news reached the house of Pharaoh: "The brothers of Joseph have come."
And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֱמֹ֥ר אֶל־אַחֶ֖יךָ זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ
pairs.english: And Pharaoh said to Joseph: Tell your brothers: Do this.
Load your beasts [with grain],
and go to the land of Canaan.
And take your father and your households and come to me,
and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt [Goshen],
and you will eat the fat of the land.
And you have been commanded [by me to tell them]: Do this:

pairs.hebrew: קְחוּ־לָכֶם֩ מֵאֶ֨רֶץ מִצְרַ֜יִם עֲגָל֗וֹת לְטַפְּכֶם֙ וְלִנְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: Take for yourselves from the land of Egypt wagons for your little ones and for your wives,
and take your father and come.
And let your eyes not begrudge your goods,
for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.
And the children of Israel did so,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֥ם יוֹסֵ֛ף עֲגָל֖וֹת עַל־פִּ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: and Joseph gave them wagons at Pharaoh's bidding,
and he gave them provision for the way.
To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of clothing,
and to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver
and five changes of clothing.
And to his father he sent according to this (count):
ten asses carrying of the good of Egypt [(old wine, of which old men are especially fond)],

pairs.hebrew: וְעֶ֣שֶׂר אֲתֹנֹ֡ת נֹֽ֠שְׂאֹ֠ת בָּ֣ר וָלֶ֧חֶם וּמָז֛וֹן לְאָבִ֖יו לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃
pairs.english: and ten she-asses carrying grain and bread and relish for his father for the road.
And he sent his brothers and they went.
And he said to them: Do not quarrel on the way, [fearing that in their shame over having sold him, they might come to accuse one another of having instigated the act.]
And they went up from Egypt
and they came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ ל֜וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר ע֚וֹד יוֹסֵ֣ף חַ֔י
pairs.english: And they told him: Joseph is still alive,
and [they told him] that he was the ruler over all the land of Egypt;
and his heart faltered, for he did not believe them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֣ת כׇּל־דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹסֵף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם
pairs.english: And they spoke to him all the words of Joseph that he spoke to them

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֲגָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח יוֹסֵ֖ף לָשֵׂ֣את אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: and he saw the wagons (agaloth) that Joseph sent to take him [(a "sign" of Joseph to his father — "eglah (like agalah) arufah" (see Deuteronomy 21) having been Joseph's study when he took leave of his father)];
and the spirit of Jacob their father revived. [The Shechinah, which had departed from him, again reposed upon him.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֛ב עוֹד־יוֹסֵ֥ף בְּנִ֖י חָ֑י
pairs.english: And Israel said: Much [joy still awaits me since] my son Joseph still lives.
I shall go and see him before I die.
And Israel journeyed and all that was with him
and he came to Beersheva,
and he offered sacrifices to the G d of his father Isaac, [(Isaac, not Abraham, the honor of one's father taking precedence to that of his grandfather.)]
And G d said to Jacob in the visions of the night:
Jacob, Jacob [(the doubling connoting affection)],
and he said: Here I am, [ready to do Your bidding].
And He said: I am the Almighty, the G d of your father.
Do not fear [being constrained to leave Eretz Yisrael and] going down to Egypt;
for a great nation shall I make you there.
I shall go down with you to Egypt,
and I shall also bring you up [to Eretz Yisrael for burial],
and Joseph shall place his hand on your eyes.
And Jacob arose from Beersheva,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־יַעֲקֹ֣ב אֲבִיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־טַפָּם֙ וְאֶת־נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם
pairs.english: and the sons of Israel bore Jacob their father and their little ones and their wives
on the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to take him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֶת־רְכוּשָׁם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָֽכְשׁוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן
pairs.english: And they took their cattle and their substance which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, [(having given their acquisitions in Padan Aram to Esau in exchange for his share in the Mearath Hamachpelah)],
and they came to Egypt,
Jacob and all of his seed with him.
His sons and the sons of his sons with him,
his daughters and the daughters of his sons, [Serach the daughter of Asher and Yocheved the daughter of Levi]; and all of his seed
he brought with him to Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨לֶּה שְׁמ֧וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הַבָּאִ֥ים מִצְרַ֖יְמָה יַעֲקֹ֣ב וּבָנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And these are the names of the children of Israel who were coming [(at that time)] to Egypt: Jacob and his sons —
the first-born of Jacob, Reuven.
And the sons of Reuven:
Chanoch and Falu, and Chetzron and Carmi.
And the sons of Shimon:
Yemuel and Yamin and Ohad and Yachin and Tzochar
and Shaul the son of the Canaanitess [Dinah, who had been ravished by a Canaanite, Shchem. (When Shchem was killed, Dinah refused to leave until Shimon swore that he would take her in marriage)].
And the sons of Levi:
Gershon, Kehoth, and Merari.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה עֵ֧ר וְאוֹנָ֛ן וְשֵׁלָ֖ה וָפֶ֣רֶץ וָזָ֑רַח
pairs.english: And the sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah and Peretz and Zarach.
And Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Peretz were Chetzron and Chamul.
And the sons of Issachar:
Tola and Puvah and Yov and Shimron.
And the sons of Zevulun:
Sered and Elon and Yachle'el.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָֽלְדָ֤ה לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֔ם
pairs.english: These are the sons of Leah, which she bore to Jacob in Padan Aram [(the males being ascribed to Leah, for when the woman "sows" first, she bears a male)],
and Dinah his daughter [(when the man sows first, he begets a female)] —
all the souls of his sons and daughters, thirty-three [(with the inclusion of Yocheved the daughter of Levi, who was born just as they entered Egypt.)]
And the sons of Gad:
Tzifyon and Chagi and Shuni and Etzbon,
Eri and Arodi and Areli.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֗ר יִמְנָ֧ה וְיִשְׁוָ֛ה וְיִשְׁוִ֥י וּבְרִיעָ֖ה וְשֶׂ֣רַח אֲחֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the sons of Asher: Yimnah and Yishvah and Yishvi and Beriah, and Serach their sister.
And the sons of Beriah, Chever and Malkiel.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י זִלְפָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָבָ֖ן לְלֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: These are the sons of Zilpah, who Lavan gave to Leah his daughter.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֤לֶד אֶת־אֵ֙לֶּה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה נָֽפֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: And she bore these to Jacob, sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel, the wife [(Rachel being singled out as the "wife," the mainstay)] of Jacob,
Joseph and Benjamin.
And there were born unto Joseph in the land of Egypt —

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֣ן אֹ֑ן
pairs.english: borne to him by Asnath the daughter of Poti Fera, the priest of On —
Menasheh and Ephraim.
And the sons of Benjamin:
Bela and Becher and Ashbel and Gera and Naaman,
Echi and Rosh and Muppim and Chuppim and Ard.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּ֖ד לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: These are the sons of Rachel, who were borne to Jacob.
All the souls, fourteen.
And the sons of Dan:
Chushim.
And the sons of Naftali:
Yachtze'el and Guni and Yetzer and Shilem.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִלְהָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן לָבָ֖ן לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: These are the sons of Bilhah, who Lavan gave to Rachel his daughter.
And she bore these to Jacob.
All the souls, seven.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַ֠נֶּ֠פֶשׁ הַבָּאָ֨ה לְיַעֲקֹ֤ב מִצְרַ֙יְמָה֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י יְרֵכ֔וֹ
pairs.english: All of the soul [all one "soul" in that they served one G d] coming [i.e., at the time of their coming] with Jacob to Egypt, the issue of his loins,
aside from the wives of the sons of Jacob,
all of the soul, sixty-six.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֛ף אֲשֶׁר־יֻלַּד־ל֥וֹ בְמִצְרַ֖יִם נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the sons of Joseph which were born to him in Egypt, two souls.
All of the soul of the house of Jacob that came to Egypt were seventy, [the sixty-six finding Joseph and his two sons there, and Yocheved being born there upon their entry.]

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־יְהוּדָ֞ה שָׁלַ֤ח לְפָנָיו֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף לְהוֹרֹ֥ת לְפָנָ֖יו גֹּ֑שְׁנָה
pairs.english: And Judah he sent before him to Joseph to pave the way [for settlement] before him [(i.e., before he reached there)] to Goshen.
And they came to the land of Goshen.
And Joseph [himself] reined his chariot [in his fervor to honor his father],
and he went up to Israel his father in Goshen,
and he [Joseph] appeared before him, and he [Joseph] fell on his neck,
and he wept and wept on his neck.
And Israel said to Joseph: If I should die now, [I would be consoled]

pairs.hebrew: אַחֲרֵי֙ רְאוֹתִ֣י אֶת־פָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י עוֹדְךָ֖ חָֽי׃
pairs.english: having seen your face; for you are yet alive.
And Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's house:
I shall go up and tell Pharaoh:

pairs.hebrew: אַחַ֧י וּבֵית־אָבִ֛י אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־כְּנַ֖עַן בָּ֥אוּ אֵלָֽי׃
pairs.english: My brothers and my father's house from the land of Canaan have come to me.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֙ רֹ֣עֵי צֹ֔אן כִּֽי־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה הָי֑וּ
pairs.english: And [I shall tell him further that] the men are shepherds, for they were (always) cattle keepers;
and their flocks and herds and all that is theirs they have brought.
And it shall be, when Pharaoh calls to you
and says: What is your occupation?

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִקְנֶ֜ה הָי֤וּ עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ מִנְּעוּרֵ֣ינוּ וְעַד־עַ֔תָּה גַּם־אֲנַ֖חְנוּ גַּם־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: Then you shall say: Your servants have been cattle keepers from our youths until now, both we and our fathers.
(Say this) so that you be settled in the land of Goshen, [which you require for pasture. And he will settle you there, away from him,]
for the abomination of Egypt are all who graze sheep, [sheep being an object of idolatry to them,]
And Joseph came and told it to Pharaoh, and he said:

pairs.hebrew: אָבִ֨י וְאַחַ֜י וְצֹאנָ֤ם וּבְקָרָם֙ וְכׇל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֔ם בָּ֖אוּ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: My father and my brothers and their flocks and their herds and all that is theirs have come from the land of Canaan,
and, behold, they are in the land of Goshen.
And from the "edge" of his brothers, [the least vigorous (so that Pharaoh not impress them into military service)], he took five men,
and he presented them to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to his brothers: What is your occupation?
And they said to Pharaoh: Your servants are shepherds,
both we and our fathers.
And they said to Pharaoh: To sojourn in the land did we come.
For there is no pasture for your servants' flocks.
For the famine is sore in the land of Canaan.
And now, let your servants abide in the land of Goshen.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph:
Your father and your brothers have come to you.
The land of Egypt is before you.

pairs.hebrew: בְּמֵיטַ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ הוֹשֵׁ֥ב אֶת־אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־אַחֶ֑יךָ יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן
pairs.english: In the best of the land settle your father and your brothers. Let them live in the land of Goshen.

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־יָדַ֗עְתָּ וְיֶשׁ־בָּם֙ אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֔יִל וְשַׂמְתָּ֛ם שָׂרֵ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה עַל־אֲשֶׁר־לִֽי׃
pairs.english: And if you know of any experts among them [in shepherding], appoint them overseers over mine [i.e., my sheep].

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־יַֽעֲקֹ֣ב אָבִ֔יו וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And Joseph brought Jacob his father and presented him to Pharaoh,
and Jacob gave Pharaoh salutation.
And Pharaoh said to Jacob:
How many are the days of the years of your life?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י מְגוּרַ֔י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Jacob said to Pharaoh: The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years.

pairs.hebrew: מְעַ֣ט וְרָעִ֗ים הָיוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י
pairs.english: Few and troubled have been the days of the years of my life,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֣א הִשִּׂ֗יגוּ אֶת־יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י אֲבֹתַ֔י בִּימֵ֖י מְגוּרֵיהֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and they did not attain [in good] to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojournings.
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh [in leave-taking],
and he left Pharaoh's presence.
And Joseph settled his father and his brothers,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם אֲחֻזָּה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּמֵיטַ֥ב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ רַעְמְסֵ֑ס
pairs.english: and he gave them a holding in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Ramses [in Goshen],
as Pharaoh had commanded.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְכַלְכֵּ֤ל יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־אֶחָ֔יו וְאֵ֖ת כׇּל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Joseph fed his father and his brothers and all of his father's household
bread [sufficient for all, even] for the little ones [to "finger"].
And [(a reversion to the beginning of the years of famine)] there was no bread in all the land,
for the famine was extremely severe,

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֜לַהּ אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן מִפְּנֵ֖י הָרָעָֽב׃
pairs.english: and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished in the famine.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְלַקֵּ֣ט יוֹסֵ֗ף אֶת־כׇּל־הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ הַנִּמְצָ֤א בְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וּבְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשֶּׁ֖בֶר אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣ם שֹׁבְרִ֑ים
pairs.english: And Joseph gathered all the money found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan [which they had given him] for the grain that they had purchased,
and Joseph brought the money to the house of Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֹּ֣ם הַכֶּ֗סֶף מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֘יִם֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֒עַן֒
pairs.english: And the money was exhausted in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֩אוּ֩ כׇל־מִצְרַ֨יִם אֶל־יוֹסֵ֤ף לֵאמֹר֙ הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ לֶ֔חֶם
pairs.english: And all of Egypt came to Joseph, saying: Give us bread.

pairs.hebrew: וְלָ֥מָּה נָמ֖וּת נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃
pairs.english: Why should we die before you? For the money is at an end.
And Joseph said: Bring your kine
and I will give (it) to you for your kine
if the money is at an end.
And they brought their kine to Joseph,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָהֶם֩ יוֹסֵ֨ף לֶ֜חֶם בַּסּוּסִ֗ים וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַצֹּ֛אן וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבָּקָ֖ר וּבַחֲמֹרִ֑ים
pairs.english: and Joseph gave them bread for the horses and for the flocks of sheep and for the herds of cattle and the asses.
And he led them with bread for all of their kine in that year.

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּתֹּם֮ הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִוא֒ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ אֵלָ֜יו בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית
pairs.english: And that year ended and they came to him in the second year [of the years of famine]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא־נְכַחֵ֣ד מֵֽאֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֚י אִם־תַּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔סֶף וּמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֑י
pairs.english: and they said to him: We will not conceal it from my lord that the money and the kine are gone [and that all has come] to [the hand of] my lord.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י בִּלְתִּ֥י אִם־גְּוִיָּתֵ֖נוּ וְאַדְמָתֵֽנוּ׃
pairs.english: Nothing remains before my lord if not our bodies and our ground.

pairs.hebrew: לָ֧מָּה נָמ֣וּת לְעֵינֶ֗יךָ גַּם־אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ גַּ֣ם אַדְמָתֵ֔נוּ
pairs.english: Why should we perish before your eyes, both we and our ground?
Buy us and our ground for bread,
and we and our ground will be servants to Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: וְתֶן־זֶ֗רַע וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵשָֽׁם׃
pairs.english: And give us seed so that we will live and not die, and the ground will not be desolate. [(Even though Joseph said (45:6): "And five years are yet to come in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest," once Jacob came to Egypt, "blessing came at his heels," they began to sow and the famine ended.)]
And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־מָכְר֤וּ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵ֔הוּ כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק עֲלֵהֶ֖ם הָרָעָ֑ב
pairs.english: For every man in Egypt sold his field; for the famine intensified over them.
And the land became Pharaoh's possession.

And he [Joseph] transferred the people to cities [from one city to another as a sign that they no longer had a holding in the land, (Joseph intending in this that his brothers not be branded as "exiles.")]
from one end of the border of Egypt to the other.
Only the land of the priests he did not buy.
For the priests had a dole from Pharaoh,

pairs.hebrew: וְאָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־חֻקָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן לָהֶם֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה
pairs.english: and they ate their dole which Pharaoh had given them,
wherefore they did not sell their land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם הֵן֩ קָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֥ם הַיּ֛וֹם וְאֶת־אַדְמַתְכֶ֖ם לְפַרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And Joseph said to the people: Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh.
Here is seed for you and sow the ground.
And it shall be in the ingathering that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh,

pairs.hebrew: וְאַרְבַּ֣ע הַיָּדֹ֡ת יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶם֩ לְזֶ֨רַע הַשָּׂדֶ֧ה
pairs.english: and four parts shall be your own for seed for the field [each year]
and for your food and [as food] for those in your houses [manservants and maidservants] and as food for your little ones.
And they said: You have kept us alive.
May we find favor in the eyes of my lord [to do with us as you said]
and we will be servants to Pharaoh [to pay him the yearly tribute].

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹתָ֣הּ יוֹסֵ֡ף לְחֹק֩ עַד־הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה עַל־אַדְמַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְפַרְעֹ֖ה לַחֹ֑מֶשׁ
pairs.english: And Joseph made it a statute [without repeal] until this day over the land of Egypt that a fifth of it reverted to Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: רַ֞ק אַדְמַ֤ת הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם לֹ֥א הָיְתָ֖ה לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
pairs.english: Only the land of the priests alone did not revert to Pharaoh.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֑שֶׁן
pairs.english: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen,
and they had a holding in it,
and they were fruitful and they multiplied exceedingly.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחִ֤י יַעֲקֹב֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י יְמֵֽי־יַעֲקֹב֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.
And the days of Israel "drew near to die" [(This phrase always connotes not attaining to the age of one's father. Isaac lived 180 years, and Jacob, 147)].
And he called to his son, to Joseph, [who was in a position to carry out what he asked] and he said to him:

pairs.hebrew: אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ שִֽׂים־נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֣חַת יְרֵכִ֑י
pairs.english: If I have now found favor in your eyes, place your hand under my thigh [and swear]
that you will do with me lovingkindness and truth. [(The lovingkindness one does with the dead is one of "truth" in that there is no expectation of reciprocation.)]
Do not bury me in Egypt.
And I will lie [i.e., expire] with my fathers,
and you shall carry me from Egypt and bury me in their burial place.
And he said: I shall do as you say.
And he said: Swear to me.
And he swore to him.

And Israel bowed [("In the fox's time (of authority; here, an allusion to Joseph's rule), bow down to him.")] towards the head of the bed [i.e., towards the Shechinah, which rests above the head of the sick.]
And it was, after these things,
that it was told to Joseph: Behold, your father is sick;

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י בָנָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and he took his two sons with him, Menasheh and Ephraim, [for Jacob to bless them before his death].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה בִּנְךָ֥ יוֹסֵ֖ף בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And it was told to Jacob: Behold, your son Joseph is coming to you.
And Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed, [according honor to royalty].
And Jacob said to Joseph:

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֥ל שַׁדַּ֛י נִרְאָֽה־אֵלַ֥י בְּל֖וּז בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: The Almighty G d appeared to me in Luz in the land of Canaan,
and He blessed me.
And He said to me: Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you,
and I will make of you a congregation of peoples, [two additional tribes issuing from him, Ephraim and Menasheh (see 35:11)],

pairs.hebrew: וְנָ֨תַתִּ֜י אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃
pairs.english: and I will give this land to your seed after you for an eternal blessing.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֡ה שְׁנֵֽי־בָנֶ֩יךָ֩ הַנּוֹלָדִ֨ים לְךָ֜ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם
pairs.english: And now, your two sons who were born to you in the land of Egypt
before I came to you to Egypt — they are mine, [in the number of my other sons, to take a corresponding portion in the land].
Ephraim and Menasheh as Reuven and Shimon shall be to me.
And if you have issue after them, they shall [not be numbered with my sons, but they shall] be yours.
By the name of their brothers [Ephraim and Menasheh] shall they be called in [taking] their inheritance.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֣י ׀ בְּבֹאִ֣י מִפַּדָּ֗ן מֵ֩תָה֩ עָלַ֨י רָחֵ֜ל בְּאֶ֤רֶץ כְּנַ֙עַן֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ
pairs.english: [And though I tax you to carry me for burial to the land of Canaan though I did not exert myself similarly for your mother], for when I came from Padan, Rachel died upon me in the land of Canaan on the road,
just a kivrah [a short distance] before Efrath,

pairs.hebrew: וָאֶקְבְּרֶ֤הָ שָּׁם֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔ת הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
pairs.english: and I buried her there on the road to Efrath, which is Bethlehem, [without even taking her into Bethlehem — bear no rancor against me for this, for I did so by Divine command, that Rachel might implore mercy for her children when they passed that way in the exile of Nevuzaradan (see Jeremiah 31)].

And Israel saw the sons of Joseph [and wished to bless them — when the Shechinah departed from him, (for Yeravam and Achav were destined to descend from Ephraim, and Yehu and his sons from Menasheh)],
and he said: "Who are these!" [i.e., Whence did they issue that they are not fit to be blessed?]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־אָבִ֔יו בָּנַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־לִ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּזֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And Joseph said to his father: They are my sons, whom G d has given me through this. [He showed him the articles of engagement and the kethubah, and Jacob implored the L rd for the return of the Shechinah, and it again reposed upon him.]
And he said: Take them now to me and I will bless them.

pairs.hebrew: וְעֵינֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כָּבְד֣וּ מִזֹּ֔קֶן לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְא֑וֹת
pairs.english: And the eyes of Israel were heavy from age; he could not see.
And he drew them near to him,
and he kissed them, and he embraced them.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף רְאֹ֥ה פָנֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א פִלָּ֑לְתִּי
pairs.english: And Israel said to Joseph: I did not think to see your face,

pairs.hebrew: וְהִנֵּ֨ה הֶרְאָ֥ה אֹתִ֛י אֱלֹהִ֖ים גַּ֥ם אֶת־זַרְעֶֽךָ׃
pairs.english: and, behold, G d has shown me your children too!
And Joseph took them out from between his knees [in order to place them in the right position for blessing; one to the right, the other to the left.]
And he prostrated himself to the ground [after he had walked backwards in deference to his father].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֣ח יוֹסֵף֮ אֶת־שְׁנֵיהֶם֒ אֶת־אֶפְרַ֤יִם בִּֽימִינוֹ֙ מִשְּׂמֹ֣אל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: And Joseph took both of them: Ephraim with his right hand, to the left of Israel,
and Menasheh [the first-born] with his left hand, to the right of Israel,
and he presented (them) to him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־יְמִינ֜וֹ וַיָּ֨שֶׁת עַל־רֹ֤אשׁ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וְה֣וּא הַצָּעִ֔יר
pairs.english: And Israel stretched out his right hand and placed it on the head of Ephraim, though he was the younger,
and his left hand on the head of Menasheh.
He crossed his hands designedly, [knowing full well] that Menasheh was the first-born.
And he blessed Joseph, saying:

pairs.hebrew: הָֽאֱלֹהִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ הִתְהַלְּכ֨וּ אֲבֹתַ֤י לְפָנָיו֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֔ק
pairs.english: The G d before whom my fathers walked — Abraham and Isaac —

pairs.hebrew: הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ הָרֹעֶ֣ה אֹתִ֔י מֵעוֹדִ֖י עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: the G d who has sustained me from the very beginning until this day —

pairs.hebrew: הַמַּלְאָךְ֩ הַגֹּאֵ֨ל אֹתִ֜י מִכׇּל־רָ֗ע יְבָרֵךְ֮ אֶת־הַנְּעָרִים֒
pairs.english: The angel who is wont to redeem me from all evil [e.g., 31:11], let him bless the youths [Menasheh and Ephraim],

pairs.hebrew: וְיִקָּרֵ֤א בָהֶם֙ שְׁמִ֔י וְשֵׁ֥ם אֲבֹתַ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֑ק
pairs.english: and let my name be called in them, and the name of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac,
and may they proliferate [veyidgu, like fish (dagim)] abundantly, [(like fish, not prey to the evil eye)] in the midst of the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹסֵ֗ף כִּי־יָשִׁ֨ית אָבִ֧יו יַד־יְמִינ֛וֹ עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וַיֵּ֣רַע בְּעֵינָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on the head of Ephraim, and it was bad in his eyes;

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְמֹ֣ךְ יַד־אָבִ֗יו לְהָסִ֥יר אֹתָ֛הּ מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשׁ־אֶפְרַ֖יִם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃
pairs.english: and he took his father's hand to remove it from the head of Ephraim to the head of Menasheh.
And Joseph said to his father: Not so, my father,
for this one is the first-born;
place your hand on his head.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן אָבִ֗יו וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יָדַ֤עְתִּֽי בְנִי֙ יָדַ֔עְתִּי
pairs.english: And his father demurred and he said: I know, my son, I know [that he is the first-born].
He, too, will be a people, and he, too, will be great, [Gideon being destined to descend from him, for whom the L rd will perform a miracle],
but his younger brother will be greater than he, [Joshua being destined to descend from him, who will inherit the land and teach Torah to Israel],
and the nations will be full of [the praises of him and] his seed [when he makes the sun stand still in Giveon, and the moon in the valley of Ayalon].
And he blessed them on that day, saying:

pairs.hebrew: בְּךָ֗ יְבָרֵ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְשִֽׂמְךָ֣ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כְּאֶפְרַ֖יִם וְכִמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: In you [i.e., in your blessings] will Israel bless [their sons in future generations], saying: "May G d make you as Ephraim and Menasheh."
And he placed Ephraim [in his blessing] before Menasheh [for precedence in the banners (see Numbers 2:18 and 10:22) and for the altar consecration by the princes of the tribes (Ibid. 7)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף הִנֵּ֥ה אָנֹכִ֖י מֵ֑ת
pairs.english: And Israel said to Joseph: Behold, I am going to die,
and G d will be with you,
and He will return you to the land of your fathers.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֞י נָתַ֧תִּֽי לְךָ֛ שְׁכֶ֥ם אַחַ֖ד עַל־אַחֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And I, [likewise, for your exertions in my burial,] I have given you Shchem [as a burial plot] as an additional (portion) over your brothers,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֤ר לָקַ֙חְתִּי֙ מִיַּ֣ד הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחַרְבִּ֖י וּבְקַשְׁתִּֽי׃ {פ}
pairs.english: which [i.e., the city of Shchem] I took from the hand of the Emori with my sword and with my bow [when they sought to kill Shimon and Levi for avenging Dinah].
And Jacob called to his sons and said:
Gather together and I will reveal to you
what will happen to you in the end of days. [He desired to reveal to them the "end of days" (the time of the Messiah), and the Shechinah departed from him and he began to say other things.]
Gather together, and hear, sons of Jacob,
and hearken to Israel your father.
Reuven, you are my first-born,
my might, and the first of my strength [i.e., the first drop (of semen), Jacob never having emitted semen (until the conception of Reuven)].
[As first-born, yours should have been] an accession of dignity [the priesthood] and an accession of strength [sovereignty],
[but because of your] precipitousness, like that of [rushing] waters, you shall not gain these accessions.
For when you went up on your father's bed [(35:22), this being the "precipitousness"],
then you profaned [(the name of) Him, i.e., the Shechinah], who was wont to go up on my bed.
Shimon and Levi are brothers, [in one counsel against Shchem and against Joseph].
Tools [of murder] stolen [from the blessing of Esau] are their swords.

In their plot [against Moses in the episode of Zimri of the tribe of Shimon (Numbers 25:6-25)], let my soul not come [i.e., let my name not be mentioned (as, indeed, it was not, it not being written there (Ibid. 14) "the son of Shimon the son of Jacob."]
With their assembly [that of Korach of the tribe of Levi], let my glory not be united, [as, indeed, it was not, it not being written there (Ibid. 16:1) "the son of Levi the son of Jacob"];
for in their wrath they slew a man [Chamor and the men of Shchem],
and in their wilfullness they razed [i.e., they would raze] an ox [Joseph].

pairs.hebrew: אָר֤וּר אַפָּם֙ כִּ֣י עָ֔ז וְעֶבְרָתָ֖ם כִּ֣י קָשָׁ֑תָה
pairs.english: Cursed be their wrath [(but not they themselves)], for it is fierce, and their anger, for it is sore.
I shall divide them [from each other] in Jacob [(Levi shall not be counted among the number of the tribes (for inheritance)],
and I shall scatter them in Israel.
Judah! [(Jacob beckoning him conciliatingly upon observing him to move back in fear of reprimand as his brothers had just been reprimanded) You are not as they, but] your brothers will praise you.
Your hand [in the days of David (Judah's descendant)] shall be upon the nape of your foes.
The sons of your father shall bow down to you.
[A prophecy concerning David:] A whelp [when Saul was king, at which time David "led out and brought in Israel" (II Samuel 5:2)], a lion [when David became king] is Judah. From

[suspicion of] "tearing" ["Joseph is torn; a wild beast (i.e., Judah, 'the lion') has devoured him" (37:33)] you arose, my son [Judah (see Ibid. 26). And you, likewise, rose above having Tamar killed by admitting the truth (Ibid. 38:26). Therefore,]

pairs.hebrew: כָּרַ֨ע רָבַ֧ץ כְּאַרְיֵ֛ה וּכְלָבִ֖יא מִ֥י יְקִימֶֽנּוּ׃
pairs.english: he crouched, he lay down as a lion [in the days of Solomon (I Kings 5:5): "every man (lying) under his vine, etc."], and as a lioness — Who shall rouse him!
The scepter shall not depart from Judah [from David on, (an allusion to) the Exilarchs of Bavel, who rule with the scepter by royal edict],
nor a lawgiver from between his feet [(an allusion to) the disciples, the Nassiate of Eretz Yisrael]
until Shiloh comes, [the king, Messiah, sovereignty being his (shelo)],
and to him will be an assembly of nations.
[A prophecy concerning the land of Judah, which will flow with wine:] He [a man of Judah] will bind to the vine his foal [and will load it from that one vine],
and to the [one] vine branch, the colt of his ass.
He will wash his raiment in wine, and his garment in the blood of grapes.
His eyes will be red from [the drinking of] wine,
and his teeth white from [an abundance of] milk, [his land providing choice pasture for his herds.]
Zevulun will dwell on the seacoast
and he will be found in the harbor, [Zevulun engaging in commerce to supply the needs of Issachar, engaged in Torah study];
and the end of his (border) will be near Tziddon.
Issachar is a bony [staunch] ass, [bearing the yoke of Torah],
lying down [for repose] between the bounds [of the cities, where he carries his "merchandise"].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤רְא מְנֻחָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב וְאֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ כִּ֣י נָעֵ֑מָה
pairs.english: And he saw that repose [i.e., his portion in the land] was good [and fruitful] and that the land was pleasant,
and he lowered his shoulder to bear [the yoke of Torah],
and he was [to all of his brothers in Israel] a "taskwork servant" [ruling for them on Torah law and on intercalations].
[A prophecy concerning Samson:] Dan shall take vengeance [of the Philistines] for his people,
the tribes of Israel [being] as one [with him].
Dan will be a serpent on the way, a shififon ["hisser"] on the path,
that bites the horse's heels,
causing its rider to fall backwards. [Samson, by buckling the temple pillars, killed the Philistines in the temple without touching them directly.
For Your salvation I hope,
O L rd. [An allusion to Samson's "Remember me, I pray You, etc." (Judges 16:28) before dying.]
Gad, troops (gedudim) will come forth from him. [They will cross the Jordan with their brothers for the conquest of Eretz Israel],
and he will troop [back, none missing, in his] tracks [to his inheritance in trans-Jordan].
[What comes] from [the portion of] Asher, rich shall be his fare,
and he shall furnish a royal repast.
Naftali is a hind let loose [(an allusion to the Genosar Valley, whose fruits are "quick" to ripen)],
evoking words of praise.
A son of favor is Joseph,
a son of favor [alighting] upon the eye [of his beholder].
[The] daughters [of Egypt] would step [upon the wall] to gaze [at his beauty].
And they [(his brothers) and Potiphar and his wife (by incarcerating him)] embittered him, and they [his brothers] became contenders (against him),
and the arrow wielders [i.e., the arrow-tongued] hated him.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב בְּאֵיתָן֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיָּפֹ֖זּוּ זְרֹעֵ֣י יָדָ֑יו
pairs.english: And his strength was firmly established, and his arms were goldened [(an allusion to the placing of the signet upon his hand)]
by the strength of Jacob —
whence [he rose to become] the head-stone of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: מֵאֵ֨ל אָבִ֜יךָ וְיַעְזְרֶ֗ךָּ וְאֵ֤ת שַׁדַּי֙ וִיבָ֣רְכֶ֔ךָּ
pairs.english: [This (glory) came to you] from the G d of your father, and He shall abet you; and with the Almighty [was your heart when you resisted your mistress] and He will bless you —

pairs.hebrew: בִּרְכֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ מֵעָ֔ל בִּרְכֹ֥ת תְּה֖וֹם רֹבֶ֣צֶת תָּ֑חַת
pairs.english: blessings of heaven from above, blessings of the deep, lying below,
blessings of fecundation [(i.e., the males will beget)] and of womb [(i.e., the females will not miscarry)].

pairs.hebrew: בִּרְכֹ֣ת אָבִ֗יךָ גָּֽבְרוּ֙ עַל־בִּרְכֹ֣ת הוֹרַ֔י עַֽד־תַּאֲוַ֖ת גִּבְעֹ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: The blessings [i.e., G d's blessings] of your father (Jacob) have surpassed the blessings of [G d to] my begetters (Abraham and Isaac), [my blessings being] until the ends of the hills [the four corners] of the world [(28:14)].

pairs.hebrew: תִּֽהְיֶ֙יןָ֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹסֵ֔ף וּלְקׇדְקֹ֖ד נְזִ֥יר אֶחָֽיו׃ {פ}
pairs.english: They (the blessings) shall [all] descend upon the head of Joseph and upon the crown of him who was separated from his brothers.
Benjamin is a wolf that will tear [(a prophetic allusion to (Judges 21:21): "And you will snatch for yourselves, etc." and to Saul's conquest)].
In the morning [of Israel's ascendancy] he [Saul] will eat the spoils,
and in the evening [i.e., in their decline, the Babylonian exile], he [(Mordechai and Esther, both of the tribe of Benjamin)] will divide the spoil [of Haman].
All of these are the tribes of Israel, twelve,

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠זֹ֠את אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר לָהֶ֤ם אֲבִיהֶם֙ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אוֹתָ֔ם
pairs.english: and this [i.e., what is stated above] is what their father spoke of them, and he blessed [all of] them;
each according to his blessing did he bless "them" [collectively, aside from the individual blessings].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֣ו אוֹתָ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲנִי֙ נֶאֱסָ֣ף אֶל־עַמִּ֔י
pairs.english: And he commanded them and he said to them: I shall be gathered unto my people, [(the souls being gathered into a place where they are secreted)];

pairs.hebrew: קִבְר֥וּ אֹתִ֖י אֶל־אֲבֹתָ֑י אֶ֨ל־הַמְּעָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׂדֵ֖ה עֶפְר֥וֹן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃
pairs.english: bury me with my fathers in the cave which is in the field of Efron the Chitti.

pairs.hebrew: בַּמְּעָרָ֞ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּשְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵי־מַמְרֵ֖א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן
pairs.english: In the cave which is in the field of Machpelah before Mamre in the land of Canaan,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁר֩ קָנָ֨ה אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָֽבֶר׃
pairs.english: which field Abraham bought from Efron the Chitti for a burial holding.

pairs.hebrew: שָׁ֣מָּה קָֽבְר֞וּ אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֗ם וְאֵת֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ
pairs.english: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.

pairs.hebrew: שָׁ֚מָּה קָבְר֣וּ אֶת־יִצְחָ֔ק וְאֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: There they buried Isaac and Rivkah his wife.
And there I buried Leah.
The purchase of the field and the cave that is in it
from the children of Cheth.
And Jacob finished commanding his sons,
and he gathered his feet into the bed,
and he expired, and he was gathered to his people [("death" not being ascribed to him)].
And Joseph fell on his father's face,
and he wept over him, and he kissed him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֨ו יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶת־עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶת־הָרֹ֣פְאִ֔ים לַחֲנֹ֖ט אֶת־אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father.
And the physicians embalmed Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּמְלְאוּ־לוֹ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יִמְלְא֖וּ יְמֵ֣י הַחֲנֻטִ֑ים
pairs.english: And forty days were completed for him, the days of embalming thus being completed,
and Egypt mourned him seventy days [(from the beginning of the embalming) for he had brought blessing upon them, the famine ending and the waters of the Nile being blessed].
And the days of weeping passed,
and Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying:

pairs.hebrew: אִם־נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם דַּבְּרוּ־נָ֕א בְּאׇזְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: If I have found favor in your eyes, speak thus, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh:

pairs.hebrew: אָבִ֞י הִשְׁבִּיעַ֣נִי לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ מֵת֒
pairs.english: My father adjured me, saying: I am going to die.

pairs.hebrew: בְּקִבְרִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן שָׁ֖מָּה תִּקְבְּרֵ֑נִי
pairs.english: In my grave, which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan — there shall you bury me.
And now, let me go up, I pray you, and bury my father, and I will return.
And Pharaoh said:
Go up and bury your father, as he adjured you. [If not for your oath I would not let you go.]
And Joseph went up to bury his father,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּֽעֲל֨וּ אִתּ֜וֹ כׇּל־עַבְדֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ זִקְנֵ֣י בֵית֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל זִקְנֵ֥י אֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and there went up with him all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house and all the elders of the land of Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹל֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאֶחָ֖יו וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And all the house of Joseph and his brothers and his fathers' house.

pairs.hebrew: רַ֗ק טַפָּם֙ וְצֹאנָ֣ם וּבְקָרָ֔ם עָזְב֖וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃
pairs.english: Only their little ones and their flocks and their herds they left in the land of Goshen.
And there went up with him also chariots, also horsemen.
And the camp was greatly laden.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַד־גֹּ֣רֶן הָאָטָ֗ד אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן
pairs.english: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad [so called because it was surrounded by thorns (atadim)] on the other side of the Jordan,
and they made great and sore lamentation there,
and he made mourning for his father, seven days.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֡רְא יוֹשֵׁב֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֜י אֶת־הָאֵ֗בֶל בְּגֹ֙רֶן֙ הָֽאָטָ֔ד
pairs.english: And the inhabitants of the land, the Canaani, saw the mourning in the threshing floor of Atad,
and they said: This is great mourning (evel) for Egypt,

pairs.hebrew: עַל־כֵּ֞ן קָרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ אָבֵ֣ל מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
pairs.english: wherefore they called it Evel-Mitzrayim, which is beyond the Jordan.
And his sons did to him thus,
as he had commanded them [viz. (13)]:

And his sons [and not his sons' sons (who were born of Canaanite women)] bore him [in the positions he assigned to them (corresponding to the traveling order of the flags in the desert)] to the land of Canaan,
and they buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָה֩ אַבְרָהָ֨ם אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה לַאֲחֻזַּת־קֶ֗בֶר מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃
pairs.english: which field Abraham had bought as a burial holding from Efron the Chitti before Mamre.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨שׇׁב יוֹסֵ֤ף מִצְרַ֙יְמָה֙ ה֣וּא וְאֶחָ֔יו וְכׇל־הָעֹלִ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers [first] and all who went up with him [(as opposed to their leaving, when the Egyptians went first (8), the Egyptians granting them precedence after witnessing the honor accorded them by the kings of Canaan)] to bury his father,
after he had buried his father.
And the brothers of Joseph saw that their father was dead [i.e., his death was made "manifest" in Joseph's no longer inviting them to dine with him, as he had before in his father's honor],
and they said: Perhaps Joseph will hate us

pairs.hebrew: וְהָשֵׁ֤ב יָשִׁיב֙ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֚ת כׇּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּמַ֖לְנוּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and will requite unto us all of the evil which we caused him.
And they appointed [the sons of Bilhah as messengers] to Joseph to say:
Your father commanded before his death, saying [(He had not so commanded, but they "dissimulated for the sake of peace")]:

pairs.hebrew: כֹּֽה־תֹאמְר֣וּ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף אָ֣נָּ֡א שָׂ֣א נָ֠א פֶּ֣שַׁע אַחֶ֤יךָ וְחַטָּאתָם֙ כִּי־רָעָ֣ה גְמָל֔וּךָ
pairs.english: Thus shall you say to Joseph: "Forgive, I pray you, the offense of your brothers and their sin. For they requited evil unto you."

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א נָ֔א לְפֶ֥שַׁע עַבְדֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ
pairs.english: And now, we pray you, forgive the offense of the servants of the G d of your father. [Though your father is dead, his G d lives, and they are His servants.]
And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
And his brothers also went [in addition to their deputation], and they fell before him
and they said: Behold, we are your servants.
And Joseph said to them: Do not fear,
for am I in the place of G d? [If He protected me from all of you, how could I alone injure you?]
And you thought evil against me.
G d thought it for good,

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֗עַן עֲשֹׂ֛ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֥ת עַם־רָֽב׃
pairs.english: in order to do as this day to give life to a great populace.
And now, do not fear.
I will sustain you and your little ones.
And he comforted them and he spoke to their hearts [reassuringly].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יוֹסֵף֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם ה֖וּא וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו
pairs.english: And Joseph abode in Egypt, he and his father's house.
And Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
And Joseph saw of Ephraim sons of the third generation.

pairs.hebrew: גַּ֗ם בְּנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יֻלְּד֖וּ עַל־בִּרְכֵּ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃
pairs.english: Also the sons of Machir the son of Menasheh were raised on Joseph's knees.
And Joseph said to his brothers: I am dying,
and G d shall remember you

pairs.hebrew: וְהֶעֱלָ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֛ע לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
pairs.english: and bring you up from this land to the land that He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And Joseph beswore the children of Israel, saying:
G d will remember you
and you will bring up my bones from here.
And Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten,
and they embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצְרָ֑יְמָה
pairs.english: And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt, [Scripture mentioning them again, after their death, in G-d's love for them];
with Jacob, a man and his household they came.
Reuven, Shimon,
Levi, and Judah.
Issachar, Zevulun,
and Benjamin.
Dan, Naftali,
Gad, and Asher.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִ֗י כׇּל־נֶ֛פֶשׁ יֹצְאֵ֥י יֶֽרֶךְ־יַעֲקֹ֖ב שִׁבְעִ֣ים נָ֑פֶשׁ
pairs.english: And all the souls who issued from Jacob's thigh were seventy souls,
and Joseph [— the same Joseph who tended his father's flock] was [king] in Egypt.
And Joseph died, and all of his brothers,
and all of that generation.
And the children of Israel were fruitful, and teemed [six in one birth],
and multiplied, and became exceedingly strong,
and the land was filled with them.
And a new king arose over Egypt
who [deported himself as if he] did not know Joseph.
And he said to his people:

pairs.hebrew: הִנֵּ֗ה עַ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֥ב וְעָצ֖וּם מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
pairs.english: Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more numerous and more powerful than we.
Ready yourselves to plot against it, lest it increase,

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־תִקְרֶ֤אנָה מִלְחָמָה֙ וְנוֹסַ֤ף גַּם־הוּא֙ עַל־שֹׂ֣נְאֵ֔ינוּ
pairs.english: and it shall be, in the event of war, that it, too, will be added to our foes,
and it will war against us and go up out of the land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מִסִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן עַנֹּת֖וֹ בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And they placed over it tax officers in order to afflict it with their [Egypt's] toils.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֜בֶן עָרֵ֤י מִסְכְּנוֹת֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אֶת־פִּתֹ֖ם וְאֶת־רַעַמְסֵֽס׃
pairs.english: And it built, [fortifying them as] treasure cities for Pharaoh — Pithom and Ramses.
And as [much as] they would afflict it,
so did it multiply and so did it burst forth.
And they were sick of their lives before the children of Israel.
And Egypt worked the children of Israel
with (back-) breaking labor.
And they embittered their lives with hard toil:
with mortar, and with brick, and with all the labor of the field;
all of the labor with which they worked them was (back-) breaking.
And the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives,
the name of the one, Shifrah [Yocheved, so called because she "beautifies" (meshapereth) the infant],
and the name of the second, Puah [Miriam, so called because she "coos" (poah) to the infant].
And he said: When you deliver the Hebrew women, and you see upon the birth-stool
that it is a son, then you shall kill him [(his astrologers having told him that a male would be born who would save Israel)],
and if it is a daughter, then she shall live.
And the midwives feared G-d

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֣א עָשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: and they did not do as the king of Egypt spoke to them,
and they sustained the males.
And the king of Egypt called to the midwives and said to them:

pairs.hebrew: מַדּ֥וּעַ עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ן הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־הַיְלָדִֽים׃
pairs.english: Why have you done this thing and sustained the males?

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּאמַ֤רְןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א כַנָּשִׁ֛ים הַמִּצְרִיֹּ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת
pairs.english: And the midwives said to Pharaoh: For not as the Egyptian women are the Hebrew women,
for they are [as expert as] midwives.
Before the midwives come to them, they are delivered [of themselves].
And G-d did good unto the midwives,
and the people multiplied and grew very strong.
And it was, because the midwives feared G-d,
that He made them houses [the houses of the Cohanim and the Levites from Yocheved, and the house of kingdom from Miriam (this being "the good" that He did unto them)].
And Pharaoh commanded his entire people, saying:
Every son that is born, into the Nile shall you throw him,

and every daughter shall you keep alive. [On the day of Moses' birth, Pharaoh's astrologers told him that the Jewish savior had been born and that he would be smitten by water, for which reason he decreed that all males be cast into the Nile — not knowing that Moses was destined to be "smitten" through the waters of Merivah (Numbers 20:13)].
And there went a man from the house of Levi
and took the daughter of Levi [after he had separated from her because of Pharaoh's decree (to drown the males)].
And the woman conceived and bore a son,
and she saw that he was good, [the house being filled with light at his birth],
and she hid him for three months.
And she could conceal him no longer,

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּֽקַּֽח־לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥הֿ בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת
pairs.english: and she took for him a reed casque [resistant to hard and soft], and she coated it with loam [on the inside] and with pitch [on the outside, so that "that tzaddik" not smell the foul odor of the pitch],
and she put the child in it,
and she placed it in the rushes by the banks of the Nile.
And his sister stood from afar
to know what would be done with him.
And the daughter of Pharaoh went down to the Nile to bathe,
and her maidens walked by the riverside,
and she saw the casque in the midst of the rushes,
and she sent her handmaid and she took it.
And she opened it and she saw the child, and, behold, a youth crying [(His voice was as that of a youth)]
and she pitied him
and she said: This is one of the Hebrew children.
And his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter:

pairs.hebrew: הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת
pairs.english: Shall I go and call for you a Hebrew nursing woman
to nurse the child for you? [many Egyptian women having attempted to nurse him — without success (Moses being destined to speak with the Shechinah)].
And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Go.
And the maiden went [She went with alacrity, like a youth],
and she called the child's mother.

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת־פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת־הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י
pairs.english: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: Take [Heilichi (hei lichi — "This is yours," an unwitting prophecy)] this child and nurse him for me,
and I will give you your wage.
And the woman took the child and she nursed it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֙הוּ֙ לְבַת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי־לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן
pairs.english: And the child grew, and she brought it to Pharaoh's daughter, and he was a son to her.
And she called his name Mosheh,
saying: "For out of the water did I take him" (meshithihu)].
And it was in those days that Moses grew [in greatness, Pharaoh appointing him over his house],
and he went out to his brothers and he saw [i.e., he took to heart] their toils,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מַכֶּ֥ה אִישׁ־עִבְרִ֖י מֵאֶחָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and he saw an Egyptian man [an overseer] striking a Hebrew man [an officer] of his brothers.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ
pairs.english: And he turned here and there and he saw that there was no man [destined to issue from the Egyptian as a proselyte],
and he smote the Egyptian and he buried him in the sand.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵא֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנֵֽי־אֲנָשִׁ֥ים עִבְרִ֖ים נִצִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And he went out on the second day, and, behold, two Hebrew men [Dathan and Aviram] quarreling,
and he said to the wicked one ["wicked" by reason of lifting his hand to strike]: Why would you strike your fellow [your "fellow" in wickedness]?

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יֹּ֠אמֶר מִ֣י שָֽׂמְךָ֞ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ
pairs.english: And he said: Who made you a man [(when you are yet a youth)], an officer and a judge over us?

pairs.hebrew: הַלְהׇרְגֵ֙נִי֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֖גְתָּ אֶת־הַמִּצְרִ֑י
pairs.english: Would you speak [the Ineffable Name] to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּירָ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אָכֵ֖ן נוֹדַ֥ע הַדָּבָֽר׃
pairs.english: And Moses was afraid, and he said: In truth, the thing has become known.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לַהֲרֹ֣ג אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And Pharaoh heard this thing [through Dathan and Aviram], and he sought to kill Moses [He handed him over to the executioner, but the sword did not prevail against him (see 18:4)],
and Moses fled from Pharaoh,
and he abode in the land of Midian, and he sat at the well, [patterning himself after Jacob, who found his match thereby].
And the priest of Midian [the chief among them (who had given up idolatry)] had seven daughters,
and they came and drew water and they filled up the trough
to give their father's flock to drink.
And the shepherds came and drove them away [because of the ban (on their father)],
and Moses arose and he rescued them, and he gave their flock to drink.
And they came to Reuel their father,
and he said: Why did you hasten to come today?

pairs.hebrew: וַתֹּאמַ֕רְןָ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י הִצִּילָ֖נוּ מִיַּ֣ד הָרֹעִ֑ים
pairs.english: And they said: An Egyptian man rescued us from the shepherds,
and he also drew water for us, and he gave the flock to drink.
And he said to his daughters: And where is he?
Why did you leave the man?
Call him and let him eat bread. [Perhaps he will marry one of you.]
And Moses consented to remain with the man,
and he gave Tzipporah his daughter to Moses (as a wife).
And she bore a son and he called his name Gershom.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר גֵּ֣ר הָיִ֔יתִי בְּאֶ֖רֶץ נׇכְרִיָּֽה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: For he said: I was a stranger (ger) in a foreign land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִי֩ בַיָּמִ֨ים הָֽרַבִּ֜ים הָהֵ֗ם וַיָּ֙מׇת֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: And it was in the course of those many days [when Moses was in Midian] that the king of Egypt died [(He was stricken with leprosy, tantamount to death, and slaughtered Jewish infants and bathed in their blood)],
and the children of Israel moaned under the toil, and they cried out,
and their outcry ascended to G-d from the toil.
And G-d heard their outcry,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־בְּרִית֔וֹ אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־יִצְחָ֥ק וְאֶֽת־יַעֲקֹֽב׃
pairs.english: and G-d remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
And G-d saw the children of Israel,
and G-d knew [i.e., He "took it to heart."]

pairs.hebrew: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן
pairs.english: And Moses grazed the flock of Yithro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian,
and he led the flock by way of the wilderness [so that it not graze in others' fields],
and he came to [what was later called] the mountain of G-d, to Chorev.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יֵּרָ֠א מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו בְּלַבַּת־אֵ֖שׁ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַסְּנֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And an angel of the L-rd appeared to him in the heart of the fire in the midst of the bush, [G-d "identifying Himself" with the sufferings of Israel].
And he saw, and, behold, the bush was burning with fire,
and the bush was not consumed.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אָסֻֽרָה־נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶ֥ה הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses said: I will turn away thither and see this great sight,
why the bush is not consumed.
And the L-rd saw that he had turned aside to see.
And G-d called to him from the midst of the bush,
and He said: Moses, Moses. And he said: Here I am.
And He said: Do not come near here.
Remove your shoes from your feet,

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ עוֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו אַדְמַת־קֹ֖דֶשׁ הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: for the place that you are standing upon is holy ground.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב
pairs.english: And He said: I am the G-d of your father, the G-d of Abraham, the G-d of Isaac, and the G-d of Jacob.
And Moses covered his face,
for he was afraid to look at G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהֹוָ֔ה רָאֹ֥ה רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־עֳנִ֥י עַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said: I have seen the afflictions of My people who are in Egypt,
and their outcry have I heard under their taskmasters,
for I have known [i.e., taken to heart] their tribulations.
And I went down to save it from the hand of Egypt

pairs.hebrew: וּֽלְהַעֲלֹתוֹ֮ מִן־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִוא֒ אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ טוֹבָה֙ וּרְחָבָ֔ה
pairs.english: and to bring it up from that land to a good and broad land,
to a land flowing milk and honey,

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־מְק֤וֹם הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃
pairs.english: to the place of the Canaani, the Chitti, the Emori, the Perizi, the Chivi, and the Yevussi.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֛ה צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּ֣אָה אֵלָ֑י
pairs.english: And now, the outcry of the children of Israel has come to Me,

pairs.hebrew: וְגַם־רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־הַלַּ֔חַץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם לֹחֲצִ֥ים אֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: and I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.
And now, go, and I will send you to Pharaoh,
and you will take out My people, the children of Israel, from Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים מִ֣י אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אֵלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses said to G-d: Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh [i.e., How am I worthy that I should speak with kings],
and [how have the Jews merited it] that I should take the children of Israel out of Egypt?
And He said [(in answer to "Who am I?") It is not you who is the protagonist here,] for I shall be with you,

and this [the non-consumed bush] is the sign for you that I have sent you [(and it is in My power to save.) And, in answer to "How have the Jews merited it, etc.", there is a great thing in store for them, viz.:]

pairs.hebrew: בְּהוֹצִֽיאֲךָ֤ אֶת־הָעָם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם תַּֽעַבְדוּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָהָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: when you take the people out of Egypt, you will serve G-d on this mountain [and receive the Torah there].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֣י בָא֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒
pairs.english: And Moses said to G-d: Behold, when I come to the children of Israel

pairs.hebrew: וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י לָהֶ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: and say to them: "The G-d of your fathers sent me to you,"
and they say to me: "What is His name?" what shall I tell them?

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶֽהְיֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And G-d said to Moses: I shall be [with them in this affliction] as I shall be [with them in the bondage of the other kingdoms. (Moses replied: "Sufficient the suffering unto its time!")]
And He [in accord] said: Thus shall you say to the children of Israel:
"I shall be" sent me to you.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֩אמֶר֩ ע֨וֹד אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כֹּֽה־תֹאמַר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒
pairs.english: And G-d said further to Moses: Thus shall you say to the children of Israel:

pairs.hebrew: יְהֹוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: The L-rd, the G-d of your fathers, the G-d of Abraham, the G-d of Isaac, and the G-d of Jacob, sent me to you.
This [the Tetragrammaton] is My name forever (leolam) [written as "le'alem" ("to be concealed," i.e., not to be pronounced)],
and this ["A-do-nai"] is My remembrance [i.e., pronunciation] from generation to generation.

pairs.hebrew: לֵ֣ךְ וְאָֽסַפְתָּ֞ אֶת־זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵהֶם֙
pairs.english: Go and gather the elders [i.e., the dignitaries] of Israel, and say to them:

pairs.hebrew: יְהֹוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ נִרְאָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם יִצְחָ֥ק וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר
pairs.english: The L-rd, the G-d of your fathers, has appeared to me — the G-d of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — saying:

pairs.hebrew: פָּקֹ֤ד פָּקַ֙דְתִּי֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הֶעָשׂ֥וּי לָכֶ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: I have remembered you ("pakod, etc.") and what has been done to you in Egypt.
And I have said that I will bring you up from the affliction of Egypt

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י
pairs.english: to the land of the Canaani, the Chitti, the Emori, the Perizi, the Chivi, and the Yevussi
to a land flowing milk and honey.
And they will hearken to your voice, [this formula ("pakod, etc.") having been handed down to them as a "password" from Jacob and Joseph (Genesis 50:24-25)],

pairs.hebrew: וּבָאתָ֡ אַתָּה֩ וְזִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֗יִם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֵלָיו֙
pairs.english: and you and the elders of Israel shall come to the king of Egypt and say to him:
The L-rd, the G-d of the Hebrews, has visited us;

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה נֵֽלְכָה־נָּ֞א דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְנִזְבְּחָ֖ה לַֽיהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
pairs.english: and now, let us go, we pray you, a distance of three days in the desert, and we shall sacrifice to the L-rd our G-d.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֣י יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֠י לֹֽא־יִתֵּ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֛ם מֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרַ֖יִם לַהֲלֹ֑ךְ
pairs.english: And I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go,
if not by [My manifesting] a strong hand.

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֤י אֶת־יָדִי֙ וְהִכֵּיתִ֣י אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹל֙ נִפְלְאֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And I will stretch out My hand and I will smite Egypt with all of My wonders which I shall do in its midst,
and then he will send you out.
And I will put the favor of this people in the eyes of Egypt;

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י תֵֽלֵכ֔וּן לֹ֥א תֵלְכ֖וּ רֵיקָֽם׃
pairs.english: and when you go, you will not go empty-handed.

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׁאֲלָ֨ה אִשָּׁ֤ה מִשְּׁכֶנְתָּהּ֙ וּמִגָּרַ֣ת בֵּיתָ֔הּ כְּלֵי־כֶ֛סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּשְׂמָלֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And a woman shall ask of her neighbor and of the woman who lives in her house articles of silver and articles of gold and garments,
and you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters,
and you shall empty out Egypt.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַן מֹשֶׁה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר וְהֵן֙ לֹֽא־יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לִ֔י
pairs.english: And Moses answered and he said: But they will not believe me,
and they will not hearken to my voice;
for they will say: The L-rd did not appear to you.
And the L-rd said to him: "What is this in your hand?"
And he said: "A staff."
And He said: Throw it to the ground.
And he threw it to the ground and it became a serpent, [a "hint" to Moses that he had plied the serpent's craft — slander (in saying that the Jews would not believe him)],
and Moses fled from before it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה שְׁלַח֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ וֶאֱחֹ֖ז בִּזְנָב֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Stretch out your hand and seize its tail.
And he stretched out his hand and grasped it,
and it became a staff in his hand.

pairs.hebrew: לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־נִרְאָ֥ה אֵלֶ֛יךָ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: So that they believe that the L-rd appeared to you, the G-d of their fathers,

pairs.hebrew: אֱלֹהֵ֧י אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִצְחָ֖ק וֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
pairs.english: the G-d of Abraham, the G-d of Isaac, and the G-d of Jacob.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֩אמֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ ע֗וֹד הָֽבֵא־נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to him again: Put your hand into your bosom.
And he put his hand into his bosom and he took it out,
and, behold, it was leprous as snow [(leprosy being the punishment for slander (see Numbers 12)].
And He said: Return your hand to your bosom,
and he returned his hand to his bosom.

And he took it from his bosom, and, behold, it had resumed its fleshy appearance, [whence it is derived that G-d's goodly measure is more expeditious than His punitive one ("from his bosom," as opposed to "took it out," above, implying that it had healed upon contact with his bosom)].

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ אִם־לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן
pairs.english: And it shall be, if they do not believe you, and they do not hearken to the message of the first sign,

then they will believe the message of the last sign, [already having precedent (— as in the instance of Pharaoh and Avimelech, who were smitten with plague because of Sarah —) that the intenders of harm to them are smitten with plague.]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֡ה אִם־לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֡ינוּ גַּם֩ לִשְׁנֵ֨י הָאֹת֜וֹת הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּן֙ לְקֹלֶ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And it shall be, if they do not believe, also these two signs, and they do not hearken to your voice,
then you shall take of the waters of the Nile, and you shall spill it upon the dry land.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָי֤וּ הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקַּ֣ח מִן־הַיְאֹ֔ר וְהָי֥וּ לְדָ֖ם בַּיַּבָּֽשֶׁת׃
pairs.english: And the waters that you take from the Nile — they shall become blood upon the dry land.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־יְהֹוָה֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי
pairs.english: And Moses said to the L-rd: I pray You, O L-rd, I am not a man of words,

pairs.hebrew: גַּ֤ם מִתְּמוֹל֙ גַּ֣ם מִשִּׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּ֛ם מֵאָ֥ז דַּבֶּרְךָ֖ אֶל־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ
pairs.english: also [(connoting an additional day)] from yesterday, also from the day before, also from when You began to speak to Your servant [this being the seventh day of Moses' opposition to the mission (in deference to Aaron's seniority)];
for heavy of speech and heavy of tongue am I.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו מִ֣י שָׂ֣ם פֶּה֮ לָֽאָדָם֒
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to him: Who made a mouth for man,

pairs.hebrew: א֚וֹ מִֽי־יָשׂ֣וּם אִלֵּ֔ם א֣וֹ חֵרֵ֔שׁ א֥וֹ פִקֵּ֖חַ א֣וֹ עִוֵּ֑ר
pairs.english: or who makes one mute or deaf or seeing or blind?
Is it not I, the L-rd?
And now, go, and I shall be with your mouth,
and I will teach you what to speak.
And he said: I pray You, O L-rd,
send, now, by the hand of [him] You are wont to send [i.e., Aaron].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֨ף יְהֹוָ֜ה בְּמֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֙יךָ֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י
pairs.english: And the anger of the L-rd burned against Moses, and He said: Is not Aaron your brother the Levite? [i.e., He was destined to be the Levite, and you, the Cohein — Now, he shall be the Cohein, and you, the Levite].
I knew that he shall surely speak.

pairs.hebrew: וְגַ֤ם הִנֵּה־הוּא֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתֶ֔ךָ וְרָאֲךָ֖ וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: And, also, behold, he shall come out towards you [when you go to Egypt] and he shall see you and he shall rejoice in his heart [and he will not (as you think) be offended by your rise to eminence (for which reason Aaron merited the choshen, the breast-plate, worn over the heart)].
And you shall speak to him, and you shall place the words in his mouth,
and I shall be with your mouth and with his mouth;
and I shall teach you what to do.
And he shall speak on your behalf to the people,
and he shall be a spokesman for you [in that you are "heavy of speech"],
and you shall be a master to him.
And this staff take in your hand,
wherewith you shall do all the signs.
And Moses went and he returned to Yether, his father-in-law [to be granted leave to go, for he had sworn to (remain with) him],

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אֵ֣לְכָה נָּ֗א וְאָשׁ֙וּבָה֙ אֶל־אַחַ֣י אֲשֶׁר־בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶרְאֶ֖ה הַעוֹדָ֣ם חַיִּ֑ים
pairs.english: and he said to him: Let me go, I pray you, and return to my brothers who are in Egypt and see if they still live.
And Yithro said to Moses: Go to peace.
