pairs.english: And the incense that you make, in its composition [(the number of its spices)] you shall not make for yourselves.
Holy shall it be to you for the L-rd. [You shall make it only for His name alone.]
One who makes its like to smell it
shall be cut off from his people. [But one may make it of what he owns, in its composition, for Temple use.]
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
See, I have called by name [to do My work]
Betzalel the son of Uri the son of Chur of the tribe of Judah.
And I have filled him with the spirit of G-d,
with wisdom [to learn from others], with understanding [to learn from what he has learned], with knowledge [the holy spirit], and with (skill in) all work.
To do [the] artistic work [of a weaver],
to work in gold, silver, and copper.
And in stone work, to fill [the stone into its setting],
and in wood work, to do all (kinds of) work.

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲנִ֞י הִנֵּ֧ה נָתַ֣תִּי אִתּ֗וֹ אֵ֣ת אׇהֳלִיאָ֞ב בֶּן־אֲחִֽיסָמָךְ֙ לְמַטֵּה־דָ֔ן
pairs.english: And I, behold, I have placed with him Ahaliav the son of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan.
And in the heart of all the wise of heart [who are among you] I have placed wisdom,
and they shall make all that I have commanded you:
The tent of meeting and the ark for the [tablets of the] testimony,
and the lid that is on it
and all the implements of the tent.
And the table and its implements,
and the menorah [made of] pure [gold], and all its implements,
and the incense altar.
And the burnt-offering altar and all its implements,
and the kiyyor, and its pedestal.
And the mesh vestments [see Numbers 4]
and the consecrated garments of Aaron the Cohein,
and the garments of his sons for ministering.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת שֶׁ֧מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֛ה וְאֶת־קְטֹ֥רֶת הַסַּמִּ֖ים לַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And the anointing oil, and the spice incense for [smoking in the sanctuary, which is] holy.
As all that I have commanded you shall they make.
And the L-rd said
to Moses, saying:

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֞ה דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַ֥ךְ אֶת־שַׁבְּתֹתַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹ֑רוּ
pairs.english: And you, speak to the children of Israel, saying […Even though I commanded you to charge them concerning the work of the mishkan, do not make light of the Sabbath to override it by that work], but [though you be eager and zealous in that work], My Sabbaths shall you keep.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ א֨וֹת הִ֜וא בֵּינִ֤י וּבֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: For it is a [great] sign between Me and you for your generations [that I chose you, by bequeathing to you My day of rest for your rest],
[for the nations] to know that I, the L-rd, sanctify you.

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת כִּ֛י קֹ֥דֶשׁ הִ֖וא לָכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you.
Those who profane it, [treating it like a weekday] shall be put to death [(if there were witnesses and warning)].

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֗י כׇּל־הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה בָהּ֙ מְלָאכָ֔ה וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמֶּֽיהָ׃
pairs.english: For whoever does work upon it, that soul [(in the absence of warning)] shall be cut off from the midst of its people.
Six days may work be done,

pairs.hebrew: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י שַׁבַּ֧ת שַׁבָּת֛וֹן קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַיהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: and on the seventh day (there shall be) a Sabbath of resting [(not merely casual resting, but complete resting, where all work, even for preparation of food, is forbidden)], holy unto the L-rd, [the keeping of its sanctity being for His name and by His charge.]

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הָעֹשֶׂ֧ה מְלָאכָ֛ה בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
pairs.english: Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall be put to death.
And the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath
to observe the Sabbath for their generations, an eternal covenant.

pairs.hebrew: בֵּינִ֗י וּבֵין֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל א֥וֹת הִ֖וא לְעֹלָ֑ם
pairs.english: Between Me and the children of Israel it is a sign forever.

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים עָשָׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ
pairs.english: For six days the L-rd made the heavens and the earth,
and on the seventh day He rested and [His spirit] was restored [(G-d using human terms that can be "assimilated by the ear" (of flesh and blood)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֤ר אִתּוֹ֙ בְּהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י
pairs.english: And He gave to Moses when He finished speaking with him [(the statutes and the judgments in Mishpatim)] on Mount Sinai,
the two tablets of the testimony,

stone tablets written by the finger of G-d. ["There is no 'earlier' and 'later' in the Torah" (This section is out of chronological order.) The incident of the golden calf preceded the charge to build the mishkan. For on the seventeenth of Tammuz the tablets were broken, and on Yom Kippur the L-rd was reconciled with Israel. And the next day they began donating for the mishkan, which was erected on the first of Nissan.] ("when He finished (kechalotho) speaking with him") ["kechalotho" is written defective (without the vav). The Torah was given to Moses as a gift, as a bride (kallah) is given to a groom, for he could not (in the order of nature) have learned all of it in such a short time.] ("when He finished speaking with him") [Moses heard the halachah first from the L-rd, and then they "reviewed" it together.] ("tablets" — luchoth) ["luchoth" is written defective (without the vav), intimating (in the Hebrew) that the tablets were identical.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן־הָהָ֑ר
pairs.english: And the people saw that [(according to their reckoning — which was erroneous!)] Moses delayed in descending the mountain,
and the people [the mixed multitude] rose up in a body upon Aaron and said to him:

pairs.hebrew: ק֣וּם ׀ עֲשֵׂה־לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ
pairs.english: Arise, make for us gods who will go before us [(they desired many gods)],

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־זֶ֣ה ׀ מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֙נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה־הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: for this Moses [(Satan showed them an image of Moses being carried (as one dead) in the firmament of heaven)], the man, who brought us up from the land of Egypt [and guided us on the way], we do not know what has become of him, [and we need gods to guide us in his stead].
And Aaron said to them:

pairs.hebrew: פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: Remove the golden rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters,

and bring them to me. [Aaron reasoned that the women and children would be reluctant to part with their jewelry and that in the meantime Moses would descend (but the men did not wait and they removed their own jewelry)]. ...

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ֙ כׇּל־הָעָ֔ם אֶת־נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאׇזְנֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And all the people disburdened themselves of the golden rings that were in their ears
and brought them to Aaron.
And he took it from their hands and he bound it in a scarf [and cast it into a crucible],
and he made it [by agency of the sorcerers of the mixed multitude] into a molten calf,

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: and they [the mixed multitude] said: These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. ...
And Aaron saw [that it had in it the spirit of life and that "Satan's act had succeeded," and he could not repel them completely], so he built an altar before it [as a "delaying tactic"]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהֹוָ֖ה מָחָֽר׃
pairs.english: and Aaron called out and he said: "There will be a festival for the L-rd tomorrow!" [Aaron expecting that Moses would appear before they could worship the golden calf, and that they would, indeed, serve the L-rd.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֙ימוּ֙ מִֽמׇּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּעֲל֣וּ עֹלֹ֔ת וַיַּגִּ֖שׁוּ שְׁלָמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And they arose early the next day, [Satan rousing them], and they offered up burnt-offerings and presented peace-offerings,
and the people sat to eat and drink,
and they arose to make sport [i.e., to commit adultery and to kill. (Chur, Miriam's son, who rebuked them, was killed here.)]
And the L-rd spoke [harshly] to Moses:
Go, descend [from your greatness. I gave you greatness only for their sake (At that time Moses was banished by the Heavenly Court)],

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱלֵ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: for your people [(the mixed multitude, that you proselytized of your own volition)] that you brought up from the land of Egypt, has wrought corruptly.
They have turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them.
They have made for themselves a molten calf,
and they have bowed down to it, and they have slaughtered to it, and they have said:

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
And the L-rd said to Moses:

pairs.hebrew: רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiff-necked people [They turn the "hard part" (the back) of their neck to those who would rebuke them.]

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּה֙ הַנִּ֣יחָה לִּ֔י וְיִֽחַר־אַפִּ֥י בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכַלֵּ֑ם
pairs.english: And now, leave Me and let My wrath burn against them and I will annihilate them [(the L-rd "hinting" to Moses that his praying for them can save them)],
and I will make of you a great nation.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְחַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר
pairs.english: And Moses prayed before the L-rd his G-d, and he said:
Why, O L-rd, should Your anger burn against Your people

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֙אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃
pairs.english: whom you took out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand? [Does rancor not obtain only with one wise man vis-à-vis another? with one strong man vis-à-vis another?]

pairs.hebrew: לָ֩מָּה֩ יֹאמְר֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר בְּרָעָ֤ה הֽוֹצִיאָם֙ לַהֲרֹ֤ג אֹתָם֙ בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּ֨לְכַלֹּתָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה
pairs.english: Why should Egypt say: "For evil did He take them out, to kill them in the mountains and to wipe them from the face of the earth!"
Turn from Your burning wrath
and bethink Yourself [to turn to good] the evil [intended] for Your people.

pairs.hebrew: זְכֹ֡ר לְאַבְרָהָם֩ לְיִצְחָ֨ק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתָּ לָהֶם֮ בָּךְ֒
pairs.english: Remember unto Abraham, Isaac, and Israel what You swore to them in You [i.e., by Your eternal essence (Abraham — (Genesis 22:16), Isaac — (Ibid. 26:3), Israel — (Ibid. 35:11)],

pairs.hebrew: וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבֶּה֙ אֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֔ם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם
pairs.english: and You said to them: I shall multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens,

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶתֵּן֙ לְזַרְעֲכֶ֔ם וְנָחֲל֖וּ לְעֹלָֽם׃
pairs.english: and all of this land of which I spoke, I shall give to your seed, and they shall inherit it forever.
And the L-rd bethought Himself of the evil
which He had intended for His people.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּ֜פֶן וַיֵּ֤רֶד מֹשֶׁה֙ מִן־הָהָ֔ר וּשְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָעֵדֻ֖ת בְּיָד֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Moses turned and descended from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand,
tablets written [(miraculously) to be readable] on both sides;
on this side and on that were they written.
And the tablets are the work of G-d [Himself],

pairs.hebrew: וְהַמִּכְתָּ֗ב מִכְתַּ֤ב אֱלֹהִים֙ ה֔וּא חָר֖וּת עַל־הַלֻּחֹֽת׃
pairs.english: and the writing is the writing of G-d, inscribed on the tablets.
And Joshua heard the sound of the people in its clamor [(They were regaling and laughing)],
and he said to Moses: "There is a sound of war in the camp."
And he (Moses) said: There is no sound of strength
and there is no sound of weakness.
An agonizing sound do I hear [i.e., a sound of blaspheming and vilifying that agonizes the soul of the hearer.]

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרַב֙ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־הָעֵ֖גֶל וּמְחֹלֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And it was, when he drew near to the camp, that he saw the calf and dances,
and Moses' wrath burned, and he cast the tablets from his hands,
and he broke them at the foot of the mountain.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־הָעֵ֨גֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ
pairs.english: And he took the calf that they had made, and he burned it with fire,
and he ground it until it was fine (dust),
and he scattered it over the water,

and he gave the children of Israel to drink [with the intent of testing them like sototh (women suspected of adultery (see Numbers 5:11-31). Three death penalties were adjudicated: Where there were witnesses and warning — death by the sword (viz. 27 below) as in the instance of ir hanidachath (a city the majority of whose inhabitants have gone astray after idolatry. See Deuteronomy 13:13-19); where there were witnesses, but not warning — death by plague (viz. 35 below); where there were neither witnesses nor warning — death by hydrokon, the waters "inspecting" them (as in the instance of the sotah's draught) and their stomachs bursting].
And Moses said to Aaron:
What did this people do to you! [i.e., How much suffering must you have endured]
so that you [not] bring upon it [this] great sin!
And Aaron said: Let my master's wrath not burn.

pairs.hebrew: אַתָּה֙ יָדַ֣עְתָּ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בְרָ֖ע הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: You know the people, that it is [in a] bad [way, always "proving" the L-rd.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לִ֔י עֲשֵׂה־לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵלְכ֖וּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ
pairs.english: And they said to me: Make for us gods who will go before us,

pairs.hebrew: כִּי־זֶ֣ה ׀ מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֙נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם
pairs.english: for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt,
we do not know what has become of him.

pairs.hebrew: וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ־לִ֑י
pairs.english: And I said to them [(only) one thing]: "Who has gold?" [And] they [hurried and] disburdened themselves and gave it to me.
And I cast it into the fire, [not knowing that this calf would emerge],
and this calf emerged.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤רְא מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י פָרֻ֖עַ ה֑וּא
pairs.english: And Moses saw the people, that it was "exposed";
for Aaron had exposed it for scorn in [the mouths of] those rising up against them.
And Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and he said:
"Whoever is for the L-rd, [let him come] to me!"
And there gathered unto him all the sons of Levi [(whence it is seen that the entire tribe was kasher)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
pairs.english: And he said to them: Thus said the L-rd, the G-d of Israel [(viz. 22:19): "He who slaughters to idolatry shall be put to death")]:
Let every man put his sword on his thigh.

pairs.hebrew: עִבְר֨וּ וָשׁ֜וּבוּ מִשַּׁ֤עַר לָשַׁ֙עַר֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהִרְג֧וּ אִֽישׁ־אֶת־אָחִ֛יו וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת־קְרֹבֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: Let him pass back and forth from gate to gate in the camp and kill; a man, his brother [by his mother (but not by his father, i.e., a non-Levite)], a man, his neighbor, and a man, his relative.
And the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִן־הָעָם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ׃
pairs.english: and there fell from the people on that day about three thousand men.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה מִלְא֨וּ יֶדְכֶ֤ם הַיּוֹם֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And Moses said: [You, who kill them,] fill your hands this day [i.e., By this you will be invested (see 28:41) to be Cohanim)] to the L-rd.
For each man [will be so invested (by having killed)] his son [i.e., his daughter's son by a non-Levite] and his brother [(as in 27)],
to bestow upon you blessing this day.
And it was on the next day that Moses said to the people:
You have committed a great sin.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּה֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה אוּלַ֥י אֲכַפְּרָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד חַטַּאתְכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: And now, I shall go up to the L-rd. Perchance, I will shield you from your sin.
And Moses returned to the L-rd and he said:

pairs.hebrew: אָ֣נָּ֗א חָטָ֞א הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה
pairs.english: I implore You — This people has committed a great sin,
and they have made for themselves gods of gold [(If You had not lavished so much gold upon them, they would not have sinned)].
And now, if You will bear their sin, [good — do not erase me,]

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־אַ֕יִן מְחֵ֣נִי נָ֔א מִֽסִּפְרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתָֽבְתָּ׃
pairs.english: but if not, erase me, I pray You, from Your book that You have written [(Erase me from Your entire Torah, so that it not be said about me that I was not worthy enough to implore mercy for Israel.)]
And the L-rd said to Moses:
Whoever sinned against Me, him shall I erase from My book.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֞ה לֵ֣ךְ ׀ נְחֵ֣ה אֶת־הָעָ֗ם אֶ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ לָ֔ךְ
pairs.english: And now, go and lead the people whither I have spoken to you.
Behold, my angel [ — but not I — ] shall go before you,

and, [though I grant your petition not to destroy them outright,] on the day of My accounting [for other sins], I shall reckon their sin [of the golden calf] against them. ["No punishment comes upon Israel which does not contain some payment for the sin of the golden calf."]
And the L-rd smote the people with plague [(those who had sinned in the presence of witnesses but who had not been warned — see 20 above)]

pairs.hebrew: עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֶת־הָעֵ֔גֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אַהֲרֹֽן׃ {ס}
pairs.english: because they had made the calf that Aaron had made.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ לֵ֣ךְ עֲלֵ֣ה מִזֶּ֔ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Go, ascend from here [(Eretz Yisrael is the highest of all lands)],

pairs.hebrew: אַתָּ֣ה וְהָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱלִ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: you and the people [("the people," as opposed to "your people" (see 32:7)], whom you brought up from the land of Egypt

pairs.hebrew: אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֠שְׁבַּ֠עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֨ם לְיִצְחָ֤ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַרְעֲךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶֽנָּה׃
pairs.english: to the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying: "To your seed shall I give it."
And I shall send an angel before you.

pairs.hebrew: וְגֵֽרַשְׁתִּ֗י אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י וְהַֽחִתִּי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃
pairs.english: And I shall drive out the Canaani, the Emori, the Chitti, the Perizi, the Chivi, and the Yevussi. [(The Girgashi left of its own accord.)]
[And you shall bring them up] to a land flowing with milk and honey.
[I tell you that I will send an angel before you] for I shall not ascend in your midst.
For you are a stiff-necked people, [and when My shechinah is in your midst and you rebel against Me, My wrath is intensified.] (I shall not ascend in your midst, then,) lest I destroy you on the way.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הָרָ֛ע הַזֶּ֖ה וַיִּתְאַבָּ֑לוּ
pairs.english: And the people heard this evil thing [(that the shechinah would not abide with them)] and they mourned,
and none of them put on his adornment [(the crowns that were bequeathed them at Chorev when they said (24:7): "We shall do and we shall hear.")]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַתֶּ֣ם עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֔רֶף
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Say to the children of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people.
If I ascended in your midst [and you rebelled against Me in your stiff-neckedness, I would rage against you for] one instant and I would annihilate you.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַתָּ֗ה הוֹרֵ֤ד עֶדְיְךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְאֵדְעָ֖ה מָ֥ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And now, [with this punishment you shall be smitten immediately — that you] remove your adornment from you, and [(as to the balance of your punishment)], I shall know what to do to you.
And the children of Israel divested themselves of their adornment [which had been bequeathed them]
at Mount Chorev.

pairs.hebrew: וּמֹשֶׁה֩ יִקַּ֨ח אֶת־הָאֹ֜הֶל וְנָֽטָה־ל֣וֹ ׀ מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה הַרְחֵק֙ מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה
pairs.english: And Moses [from that sin onwards] would take the tent (his tent) and pitch it outside the camp [saying: "He who is banished from the Teacher is banished from the student (Moses)"], far from the camp [(two thousand cubits)],
and he would call it "the tent of meeting" [for seekers of Torah.]

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָה֙ כׇּל־מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ יְהֹוָ֔ה יֵצֵא֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
pairs.english: And all who sought the L-rd [(whence it is derived that "soliciting an elder is like paying attendance upon the shechinah")] would go out to the tent of meeting that was outside the camp.
And it was, when Moses went out [to go] to the tent,

pairs.hebrew: יָק֙וּמוּ֙ כׇּל־הָעָ֔ם וְנִ֨צְּב֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ פֶּ֣תַח אׇהֳל֑וֹ
pairs.english: that all the people would rise, and each one would stand at the door of his tent
and look after Moses [out of respect, and not sit down] until he had come to the tent.
And it was, when Moses came to the tent,

pairs.hebrew: יֵרֵד֙ עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן וְעָמַ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל
pairs.english: the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the door of the tent,
and He would speak, with Moses [hearing].

pairs.hebrew: וְרָאָ֤ה כׇל־הָעָם֙ אֶת־עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן עֹמֵ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל
pairs.english: And all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tent,

pairs.hebrew: וְקָ֤ם כׇּל־הָעָם֙ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ פֶּ֥תַח אׇהֳלֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and all the people would rise and bow down [to the shechinah], each one at the door of his tent.

pairs.hebrew: וְדִבֶּ֨ר יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל־פָּנִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְדַבֵּ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ
pairs.english: And the L-rd would speak, with Moses [hearing], face to face, as a man speaks with his fellow.
And [after the L-rd's speaking], he would return to the camp [and teach the elders what he had learned. (Moses followed this practice from Yom Kippur until the mishkan was erected.)]

pairs.hebrew: וּמְשָׁ֨רְת֜וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בִּן־נוּן֙ נַ֔עַר לֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֹֽהֶל׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And his attendant, Joshua the son of Nun, a youth, would not depart from within the tent.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־יְהֹוָ֗ה רְ֠אֵ֠ה אַתָּ֞ה אֹמֵ֤ר אֵלַי֙ הַ֚עַל אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה
pairs.english: And Moses said to the L-rd: See, You say to me: "Bring up this people,"

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א הֽוֹדַעְתַּ֔נִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּשְׁלַ֖ח עִמִּ֑י
pairs.english: and You did not apprise me whom You would send with me. [Your sending an angel is not acceptable to me.]

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֤ה אָמַ֙רְתָּ֙ יְדַעְתִּ֣יךָֽ בְשֵׁ֔ם וְגַם־מָצָ֥אתָ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָֽי׃
pairs.english: And You said [see 19:9]: "I have known you by name" [i.e., I have singled you out from others], "and you have also found favor in My eyes."
And now, if I have, indeed, found favor in Your eyes,

pairs.hebrew: הוֹדִעֵ֤נִי נָא֙ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֔ךָ וְאֵדָ֣עֲךָ֔ לְמַ֥עַן אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: make known to me Your ways [i.e., the reward for finding favor in Your eyes], so that I know You [i.e., Your measure of reward], so that I find [what the nature of the reward is for finding] favor in Your eyes.
And see that this nation is Your people, [and I cannot see myself being rewarded if they are not].
And He said: My face [i.e., I Myself] shall go [and not an angel],
and I shall give you rest.
And he said to Him: [This, indeed, is what I desire, for] if You Yourself do not go, [but an angel],
do not bring us up from here.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַמֶּ֣ה ׀ יִוָּדַ֣ע אֵפ֗וֹא כִּֽי־מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמֶּ֔ךָ
pairs.english: For how, otherwise, will it be known that I and Your people have found favor in Your eyes?
Is it not by Your going with us?

pairs.hebrew: וְנִפְלִ֙ינוּ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמְּךָ֔ מִכׇּ֨ל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And [I have yet another request: that You not repose Your shechinah on the nations of the world so that] I and Your people be distinct from all the people on the face of the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֑ה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: This thing, too, that you have spoken [(to repose My shechinah no more on the nations of the world)] will I do.
For you have found favor in My eyes and I have known you by name.
And [sensing it to be an opportune moment] he said:
Show me, I pray you, Your glory.
And He said: I shall cause all of My goodness to pass before you [when you are concealed in the cave],

and I shall call in the name of the L-rd before you [to teach you the order of imploring mercy even when the merit of the fathers (zcuth avoth) no longer obtains. And you teach Israel to pray according to that order ("the Thirteen Attributes") and their prayers for mercy will thereby be granted];

pairs.hebrew: וְחַנֹּתִי֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָחֹ֔ן וְרִחַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲרַחֵֽם׃
pairs.english: and I shall be gracious when I desire to be so, and I shall be merciful when I desire to be so, [(but later (34:10) He assured Moses that "the Thirteen Attributes" are never unavailing)].
And He said: You shall not be permitted to see My face [even when I pass all My good before you];
for no man can see Me and live.

And the L-rd said: Behold, [in the mountain where I am wont to speak with you], there is a place with Me [i.e., set aside for Me for your needs (so that you not be harmed), where you will see what you shall see],
and you will stand on the rock.
And it shall be, when My glory passes by,
that I shall place you in the cleft of the rock,
and I shall cover you with My "palm" until I have passed.
Then I shall remove My palm,
and you shall see My back [(He showed him the head-knot of His tefillin)],
but My face shall not be seen.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה פְּסׇל־לְךָ֛ שְׁנֵֽי־לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִ֖ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Hew (p'sal) for yourself two stone tablets like the first [(He showed him a sapphire quarry and said to him: "The chips (psoleth) shall be yours" (thus, "for yourself." Moses grew wealthy from them.)] [Moses broke the first tablets; he was, therefore, told to hew the second.]

pairs.hebrew: וְכָתַבְתִּי֙ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֔ת אֶ֨ת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֛וּ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֥ת הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁבַּֽרְתָּ׃
pairs.english: And I shall write on the tablets the words which were on the first tablets, which you broke.
And be ready in the morning,
and go up in the morning to Mount Sinai,
and stand for Me there on the top of the mountain.
And let no man go up with you,
and also let no man be seen on all of the mountain.

pairs.hebrew: גַּם־הַצֹּ֤אן וְהַבָּקָר֙ אַל־יִרְע֔וּ אֶל־מ֖וּל הָהָ֥ר הַהֽוּא׃
pairs.english: The flocks and the herds, too, shall not graze opposite that mountain. [Because the first tablets were given amidst shouting, sound, and throng, the evil eye prevailed against them (and they were broken). There is nothing more desirable than "modesty."]
And he hewed two stone tablets like the first,

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם מֹשֶׁ֤ה בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: and Moses arose early in the morning, and he went up to Mount Sinai as the L-rd had commanded him,
and he took in his hand two stone tablets.
And the L-rd descended in a cloud
and He stood with him there,
and He called in the name of the L-rd [(see 33:19)]:
And the L-rd passed before him and He called

"Hashem (Yod-Keh-Vav-Keh), Hashem, [the attribute of mercy: one (Hashem) before the sin; one, after sinning and repentance], the G-d [(Kel, likewise the attribute of mercy)], who is merciful and gracious,

slow to anger, [withholding His anger in anticipation of repentance], and abundant in lovingkindness [to those who are in need of it, being deficient in merit], and truth, [paying goodly reward to the doers of His will],
Preserving [a man's] lovingkindness [before Him] for two thousand [generations],
forgiving [deliberate] sin, and [acts of] rebellion (against the L-rd), and transgression —
but not absolving [completely].

pairs.hebrew: פֹּקֵ֣ד ׀ עֲוֺ֣ן אָב֗וֹת עַל־בָּנִים֙ וְעַל־בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִֽים׃
pairs.english: He remembers the sin of the fathers upon sons [who persist in their fathers' ways], and upon sons of sons, upon the third [generation] and upon the fourth."
And Moses hastened [when he saw the shechinah passing by and heard the "calling"],
and he bowed to the ground and prostrated himself.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אִם־נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י
pairs.english: And he said: If I have now found favor in Your eyes, my L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: יֵֽלֶךְ־נָ֥א אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּקִרְבֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֤י עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֙רֶף֙ ה֔וּא
pairs.english: let my L-rd go in our midst [as You have promised (33:14) and even] if it is a stiff-necked people [and it rebels against You, (concerning which You have said (Ibid. 33:3): "Lest I destroy you on the way")],
You will (nevertheless) forgive our sin and our transgression, and You will make us Your [distinct] portion [viz. (Ibid.16)].
And He said: Behold, I am making a covenant [for this].

pairs.hebrew: נֶ֤גֶד כׇּֽל־עַמְּךָ֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה נִפְלָאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־נִבְרְא֥וּ בְכׇל־הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבְכׇל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם
pairs.english: Before all your people shall I make (wondrous) distinctions [(whereby you will be distinguished from all other nations, on whom My shechinah will not repose)], which (wonders) have never been created in all the land and in all the nations.

pairs.hebrew: וְרָאָ֣ה כׇל־הָ֠עָ֠ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֨ה בְקִרְבּ֜וֹ אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ כִּֽי־נוֹרָ֣א ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י עֹשֶׂ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: And all the people in whose midst you are will see the work of the L-rd. For it is awesome, what I am to do with you.

pairs.hebrew: שְׁמׇ֨ר־לְךָ֔ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוְּךָ֣ הַיּ֑וֹם
pairs.english: Be heedful of what I command you this day.

pairs.hebrew: הִנְנִ֧י גֹרֵ֣שׁ מִפָּנֶ֗יךָ אֶת־הָאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וְהַחִתִּי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃
pairs.english: Behold, I am driving out before you the Emori, the Canaani, the Chitti, the Perizi, the Chivi, and the Yevussi [(The Girgashi left of its own accord.)]

pairs.hebrew: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ פֶּן־תִּכְרֹ֤ת בְּרִית֙ לְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה בָּ֣א עָלֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: Be heedful lest you make a covenant with the inhabitant of the land to which you are coming,
lest it be a snare in your midst.
But their altars shall you raze,
and their monuments shall you break,
and their trees devoted to idolatry shall you cut down.
For you shall not bow down to another god.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ קַנָּ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ אֵ֥ל קַנָּ֖א הֽוּא׃
pairs.english: For the L-rd, Kana ("zealous") is His name, [zealous in exacting payment and not overlooking things]; He is a zealous G-d.
Lest you make a covenant with the inhabitant of the land
and they stray after their gods and sacrifice to their gods,

and he call to you and you eat from his sacrifice. [I shall regard your eating from his sacrifice as acknowledging his idolatry, for, as a result, "You will take of his daughters for your sons, etc."]
And you will take of his daughters for your sons,
and his daughters will stray after their gods,
and they will cause your sons to stray after their gods.
Molten gods
you shall not make for yourself.
The festival of matzoth shall you keep.

pairs.hebrew: שִׁבְעַ֨ת יָמִ֜ים תֹּאכַ֤ל מַצּוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ךָ לְמוֹעֵ֖ד חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָאָבִ֑יב
pairs.english: Seven days shall you eat matzoth as I commanded you, in the appointed time in the month of aviv [the first ripening].
For in the month of aviv you went out of Egypt.
All firstlings of the womb [in man] are Mine,
and (of) all of your kine that bears a male, the firstling of an ox or a sheep.

And the firstling of an ass [(but not another unclean beast)] you shall redeem with a lamb [(He gives the lamb to the Cohein. It is chullin (non-sacred) in the hand of the Cohein, and the owner may work with the firstling)].
And if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck [with a hatchet. (He caused a monetary loss to the Cohein — let him incur such a loss!)].
All the first-born of your sons shall you redeem;
and they [the children of Israel, when they go up to Jerusalem for the festival,] shall not appear before Me empty-handed, [but they shall bring the prescribed offering].
Six days shall you work,
and on the seventh day shall you rest.
From [mundane] plowing and harvesting shall you rest [(to exclude harvesting the omer which is a mitzvah, and which overrides the Sabbath)].

pairs.hebrew: וְחַ֤ג שָׁבֻעֹת֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לְךָ֔ בִּכּוּרֵ֖י קְצִ֣יר חִטִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And the festival of Shavuoth shall you make for yourself, the first-fruits of the wheat harvest, [the "two breads" (see Leviticus 23:16-17), the first wheat meal-offering brought to the Temple, (the meal-offering of the omer brought on Pesach, being of barley)],
and the festival of the ingathering (Succoth), [when you gather your produce from the field to the house], the circuit of the year [i.e., the beginning of the new year].
Three times in the year

pairs.hebrew: יֵרָאֶה֙ כׇּל־זְכ֣וּרְךָ֔ אֶת־פְּנֵ֛י הָֽאָדֹ֥ן ׀ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: shall all of your males appear before the L-rd, Hashem (Yod-Keh-Vav-Keh), the G-d of Israel.

For I shall drive out nations from before you, and I shall broaden your boundary, [so that, being far from the Temple, you will not be able to appear before Me constantly, for which reason I am providing these three festivals for you (to do so)].
And no man shall covet your land

pairs.hebrew: בַּעֲלֹֽתְךָ֗ לֵרָאוֹת֙ אֶת־פְּנֵי֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃
pairs.english: when you go up to appear before the L-rd your G-d three times in the year.

You shall not slaughter while chametz [still] is present, the blood of My [Pesach] offering [(an exhortation (against possessing chametz) to the slaughterer, the tosser of the blood, and any of the members of the "company" (for that offering)].
And there shall not tarry overnight [off the altar] until morning, the slaughtering [i.e., the eimurin (the consecrated parts)] of the festival of Pesach. [The same applies to all offerings.]

pairs.hebrew: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: The first of the first-fruits of your land [i.e., of the seven species mentioned in praise of your land (Deuteronomy 8:8)] you shall bring to the house of the L-rd your G-d.
You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk. [(This excludes (from Torah interdiction) fowl, where there is no "mother's milk")]. [See 23:19].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּתׇב־לְךָ֖ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Write for yourself these words [(but you are not permitted to write oral Torah)];

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֞י עַל־פִּ֣י ׀ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה כָּרַ֧תִּי אִתְּךָ֛ בְּרִ֖ית וְאֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: for according to these words have I made with you a covenant and with Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֣ם עִם־יְהֹוָ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה
pairs.english: And he was there with the L-rd forty days and forty nights.

pairs.hebrew: לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔ל וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א שָׁתָ֑ה
pairs.english: Bread he did not eat and water he did not drink.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֗ת אֵ֚ת דִּבְרֵ֣י הַבְּרִ֔ית עֲשֶׂ֖רֶת הַדְּבָרִֽים׃
pairs.english: And He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י בְּרֶ֤דֶת מֹשֶׁה֙ מֵהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וּשְׁנֵ֨י לֻחֹ֤ת הָֽעֵדֻת֙ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּרִדְתּ֖וֹ מִן־הָהָ֑ר
pairs.english: And it was, when Moses descended [(with the second tablets, on Yom Kippur)] from Mount Sinai — with the two tablets of the testimony in the hand of Moses, when he descended from the mountain —

pairs.hebrew: וּמֹשֶׁ֣ה לֹֽא־יָדַ֗ע כִּ֥י קָרַ֛ן ע֥וֹר פָּנָ֖יו בְּדַבְּר֥וֹ אִתּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: that Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone [(the light projecting like horns)] from His having spoken with him.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨רְא אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְכׇל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קָרַ֖ן ע֣וֹר פָּנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And Aaron and all of Israel saw Moses, and, behold, the skin of his face shone,
and they were afraid to approach him.
And Moses called to them,
and there returned to him Aaron and all the princes of the assembly,
and Moses would speak to them [the behest of the L-rd].
And after that [i.e., after he had taught the elders], all the children of Israel would approach,

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַוֵּ֕ם אֵת֩ כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהֹוָ֛ה אִתּ֖וֹ בְּהַ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
pairs.english: and he would command them all that the L-rd had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
And when Moses finished speaking with them,
he would place a mask on his face, [in deference to the rays of splendor, that not all "feast their eyes on them."]

pairs.hebrew: וּבְבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה לִפְנֵ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ יָסִ֥יר אֶת־הַמַּסְוֶ֖ה עַד־צֵאת֑וֹ
pairs.english: And when Moses came before the L-rd to speak with Him, he would put off the mask until he went forth;

pairs.hebrew: וְיָצָ֗א וְדִבֶּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצֻוֶּֽה׃
pairs.english: and he would go forth and speak to the children of Israel what he had been commanded.

pairs.hebrew: וְרָא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה כִּ֣י קָרַ֔ן ע֖וֹר פְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: And the children of Israel beheld Moses' face, for the skin of Moses' face shone.

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵשִׁ֨יב מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־הַמַּסְוֶה֙ עַל־פָּנָ֔יו עַד־בֹּא֖וֹ לְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: And [when he took leave of them], Moses would put the mask back on his face until he came to speak with Him, [when he would doff it].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶֽת־כׇּל־עֲדַ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And Moses assembled [on the day after Yom Kippur, when he had descended from the mountain] the entire congregation of the children of Israel, and he said to them:

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת אֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: These are the things that the L-rd commanded to do.
Six days may work be done,

pairs.hebrew: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֥ם קֹ֛דֶשׁ שַׁבַּ֥ת שַׁבָּת֖וֹן לַיהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: and on the seventh day it shall be holy for you, a Sabbath of resting for the L-rd.

Whoever does work on it shall be put to death. [Moses states the exhortation against working on the Sabbath before charging them with the work of the mishkan by way of apprising them that it does not override the Sabbath.]
You shall not light a fire in all of your dwellings
on the Sabbath day.
And Moses said to the entire congregation of the children of Israel, saying:
This is the thing that the L-rd commanded [me] to say [to you].
Take from yourselves an offering for the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ל נְדִ֣יב לִבּ֔וֹ יְבִיאֶ֕הָ אֵ֖ת תְּרוּמַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: Everyone whose heart prompts him shall bring it, the offering of the L-rd:
gold, silver, and copper.
And blue wool, and purple wool, and scarlet wool,
and linen, and goats' hair.
And rams' skins dyed red, and tachash skins,
and acacia wood.
And oil for the lighting,
and spices for the anointing oil and for the burning of the incense.
And shoham stones and filling stones
for the ephod and for the choshen.
And all the wise of heart among you

pairs.hebrew: יָבֹ֣אוּ וְיַעֲשׂ֔וּ אֵ֛ת כׇּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: shall come and make all that the L-rd has commanded:

The mishkan [(The bottom spreads, seen from the inside, are called "mishkan")], its tent [(the tent of goats' hair curtains serving as a roof)], and its covering [(the covering of ram and tachash hides)],
its hooks, its beams, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets.
The ark and its staves, the kaporeth
and the parocheth partition.
The table and its staves and all of its vessels,
and the show-bread.
And the menorah of lighting and its implements [tongs and snuff-dishes], and its lamps [cups into which the oil and wicks were put],
and the oil for lighting. [This, too, required "wise of heart," its processing being different from that of other oils.]

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־מִזְבַּ֤ח הַקְּטֹ֙רֶת֙ וְאֶת־בַּדָּ֔יו וְאֵת֙ שֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת קְטֹ֣רֶת הַסַּמִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And the incense altar and its staves, and the anointing oil, and the incense spices,
and the entrance screen [on the east (26:36)] for the entrance of the mishkan.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת ׀ מִזְבַּ֣ח הָעֹלָ֗ה וְאֶת־מִכְבַּ֤ר הַנְּחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ אֶת־בַּדָּ֖יו וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֑יו
pairs.english: The burnt-offering altar and its copper lattice, its staves and all its implements,
the kiyyor and its pedestal.
The curtains of the court, its pillars and its sockets,
and the screen of the gate of the court [on the east (27:16)].
The pegs of the mishkan [(for securing the curtain ends in the ground so that they not flap in the wind)],
and the pegs of the court, and their cords.
The mesh vestments for covering the holy [appurtenances (the ark, the table, the menorah, and the altars)],
the consecrated garments of Aaron the Cohein,
and the garments of his sons for ministering.
And the entire assembly of the children of Israel
went forth from Moses' presence.
And there came every man whose heart moved him.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ נָדְבָ֨ה רוּח֜וֹ אֹת֗וֹ הֵ֠בִ֠יאוּ אֶת־תְּרוּמַ֨ת יְהֹוָ֜ה
pairs.english: And everyone whose spirit prompted him brought the offering of the L-rd

pairs.hebrew: לִמְלֶ֨אכֶת אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ וּלְכׇל־עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ וּלְבִגְדֵ֖י הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: for the work of the tent of meeting and for all of its labor and for the consecrated vestments.
And the men came along with the women.

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֣ל ׀ נְדִ֣יב לֵ֗ב הֵ֠בִ֠יאוּ חָ֣ח וָנֶ֜זֶם וְטַבַּ֤עַת וְכוּמָז֙ כׇּל־כְּלִ֣י זָהָ֔ב
pairs.english: All whose heart prompted them brought armband and nose-ring and finger-ring and chumaz [a pudendal ornament] — all ornaments of gold —

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־אִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵנִ֛יף תְּנוּפַ֥ת זָהָ֖ב לַיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: and every man who brought an offering of gold to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇל־אִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־נִמְצָ֣א אִתּ֗וֹ תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ וְעִזִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And every man with whom was found blue wool or purple wool or scarlet wool or linen or goats' hair

pairs.hebrew: וְעֹרֹ֨ת אֵילִ֧ם מְאׇדָּמִ֛ים וְעֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים הֵבִֽיאוּ׃
pairs.english: or rams' hides dyed red or tachash hides brought it.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־מֵרִ֗ים תְּר֤וּמַת כֶּ֙סֶף֙ וּנְחֹ֔שֶׁת הֵבִ֕יאוּ אֵ֖ת תְּרוּמַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: All who set aside an offering of silver or copper brought the offering of the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ נִמְצָ֨א אִתּ֜וֹ עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֛ים לְכׇל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה הֵבִֽיאוּ׃
pairs.english: And all with whom was found acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
And every woman wise of heart spun with her hands.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבִ֣יאוּ מַטְוֶ֗ה אֶֽת־הַתְּכֵ֙לֶת֙ וְאֶת־הָֽאַרְגָּמָ֔ן אֶת־תּוֹלַ֥עַת הַשָּׁנִ֖י וְאֶת־הַשֵּֽׁשׁ׃
pairs.english: And they brought spun, the blue wool, the purple wool, the scarlet wool, and the linen.

pairs.hebrew: וְכׇ֨ל־הַנָּשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָשָׂ֥א לִבָּ֛ן אֹתָ֖נָה בְּחׇכְמָ֑ה
pairs.english: And all the women whose hearts lifted them with wisdom
spun the goats' hair [directly from their backs].

pairs.hebrew: וְהַנְּשִׂאִ֣ם הֵבִ֔יאוּ אֵ֚ת אַבְנֵ֣י הַשֹּׁ֔הַם וְאֵ֖ת אַבְנֵ֣י הַמִּלֻּאִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the princes (of the tribes) brought [(after nothing else remained to be brought)] the shoham stones and the filling stones
for the ephod and for the choshen.
And the spice and the oil for lighting
and for the oil of anointment and for the incense spices.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָדַ֣ב לִבָּם֮ אֹתָם֒
pairs.english: Every man and woman whose heart prompted them

pairs.hebrew: לְהָבִיא֙ לְכׇל־הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: to bring for all of the work that the L-rd had commanded to do by the hand of Moses —
the children of Israel brought an offering to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רְא֛וּ קָרָ֥א יְהֹוָ֖ה בְּשֵׁ֑ם
pairs.english: And Moses said to the children of Israel: See, the L-rd has called by name
Betzalel the son of Uri the son of Chur [Miriam's son] of the tribe of Judah.
And He filled him with the spirit of G-d,
with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge, and with (skill in) all work.
And to devise designs,
to work in gold, silver, and copper.
And in stone work, to fill [the stone into its setting],
and in wood work to do all kinds of artistic work.
And to teach, He put it in his heart,
he and Ahaliav the son of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan.
He filled them with wisdom of heart

pairs.hebrew: לַעֲשׂוֹת֮ כׇּל־מְלֶ֣אכֶת חָרָ֣שׁ ׀ וְחֹשֵׁב֒ וְרֹקֵ֞ם בַּתְּכֵ֣לֶת וּבָֽאַרְגָּמָ֗ן בְּתוֹלַ֧עַת הַשָּׁנִ֛י וּבַשֵּׁ֖שׁ וְאֹרֵ֑ג
pairs.english: to do every work of craftsman, artist, and embroiderer, in blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and linen; and weaver,
doing all work and making designs.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשָׂה֩ בְצַלְאֵ֨ל וְאׇהֳלִיאָ֜ב וְכֹ֣ל ׀ אִ֣ישׁ חֲכַם־לֵ֗ב אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן יְהֹוָ֜ה חׇכְמָ֤ה וּתְבוּנָה֙ בָּהֵ֔מָּה
pairs.english: And Betzalel and Ahaliav and every man wise of heart in whom the L-rd has put wisdom and understanding
to know to do all the work for the labor of the sanctuary
shall do all that the L-rd has commanded.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְרָ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶל־בְּצַלְאֵל֮ וְאֶל־אׇֽהֳלִיאָב֒ וְאֶל֙ כׇּל־אִ֣ישׁ חֲכַם־לֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה חׇכְמָ֖ה בְּלִבּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Moses called to Betzalel and to Ahaliav and to every man wise of heart, in whose heart the L-rd had put wisdom,

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר נְשָׂא֣וֹ לִבּ֔וֹ לְקׇרְבָ֥ה אֶל־הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת אֹתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: every one whose heart had lifted him to draw near to the work to do it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּקְח֞וּ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֵ֤ת כׇּל־הַתְּרוּמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵבִ֜יאוּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לִמְלֶ֛אכֶת עֲבֹדַ֥ת הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לַעֲשֹׂ֣ת אֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And they took from before Moses the entire offering that the children of Israel had brought for the work of the labor of the sanctuary, to do it.

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠הֵ֠ם הֵבִ֨יאוּ אֵלָ֥יו ע֛וֹד נְדָבָ֖ה בַּבֹּ֥קֶר בַּבֹּֽקֶר׃
pairs.english: And they brought him yet more offerings every morning.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ כׇּל־הַ֣חֲכָמִ֔ים הָעֹשִׂ֕ים אֵ֖ת כׇּל־מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And there came all the wise men, the doers of all the work of the sanctuary,
each from his work that they were doing.
And they said to Moses:

pairs.hebrew: מַרְבִּ֥ים הָעָ֖ם לְהָבִ֑יא מִדֵּ֤י הָֽעֲבֹדָה֙ לַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ת אֹתָֽהּ׃
pairs.english: The people are bringing more than is needed for the work that the L-rd commanded to do.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֣ו מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיַּעֲבִ֨ירוּ ק֥וֹל בַּֽמַּחֲנֶה֮ לֵאמֹר֒
pairs.english: And Moses commanded, and they announced in the camp, saying:

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֗ה אַל־יַעֲשׂוּ־ע֛וֹד מְלָאכָ֖ה לִתְרוּמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: Let man and woman not do any more work for the offering of the sanctuary.
And the people were held back from bringing.

pairs.hebrew: וְהַמְּלָאכָ֗ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַיָּ֛ם לְכׇל־הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֹתָ֑הּ
pairs.english: And the work [of the bringing] was sufficient [for the builders of the mishkan] for all of the work [of the mishkan], to make it
and to leave (something) over.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ כׇל־חֲכַם־לֵ֜ב בְּעֹשֵׂ֧י הַמְּלָאכָ֛ה אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן עֶ֣שֶׂר יְרִיעֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And all the wise of heart among the doers of the work made the mishkan of ten curtains.

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י
pairs.english: Twisted linen, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool;
cherubs, of artistic work he made them.

pairs.hebrew: אֹ֜רֶךְ הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽאַחַ֗ת שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה
pairs.english: The length of one curtain, twenty-eight cubits;
and the width, four cubits for one curtain —
one measure for all the curtains.
And he attached five curtains one to the other,
and five curtains one to the other.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לֻֽלְאֹ֣ת תְּכֵ֗לֶת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת מִקָּצָ֖ה בַּמַּחְבָּ֑רֶת
pairs.english: And he made loops of purple wool at the edge of one curtain at its edge in the joining.

pairs.hebrew: כֵּ֤ן עָשָׂה֙ בִּשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַקִּ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה בַּמַּחְבֶּ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
pairs.english: So did he do at the edge of the end curtain of the other joining.
Fifty loops he made in the one (end) curtain,

pairs.hebrew: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻלָאֹ֗ת עָשָׂה֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַיְרִיעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּמַּחְבֶּ֣רֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית
pairs.english: and fifty loops he made at the edge of the (end) curtain in the second joining,
the loops [on the respective joinings] directly aligned one with the other.
And he made fifty golden hooks,
and he joined the curtains one to the other by the hooks,
and the mishkan was one.
And he made curtains of goats' hair to tent over the [lower curtains of the] mishkan.
Eleven curtains he made them.
The length of one curtain, thirty cubits;
and four cubits the width for one curtain —
one measure for the eleven curtains.
And he joined the five curtains separately
and the six curtains separately.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לֻֽלָאֹ֣ת חֲמִשִּׁ֗ים עַ֚ל שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַקִּיצֹנָ֖ה בַּמַּחְבָּ֑רֶת
pairs.english: And he made fifty loops at the edge of the end curtain in one joining;

pairs.hebrew: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻלָאֹ֗ת עָשָׂה֙ עַל־שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַחֹבֶ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
pairs.english: and fifty loops he made at the edge of the (end) curtain in the second joining.
And he made fifty copper hooks
to join the tent [the goats' hair covering] to be one.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מִכְסֶה֙ לָאֹ֔הֶל עֹרֹ֥ת אֵילִ֖ם מְאׇדָּמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And he made a cover for the tent, rams' skins dyed red,
and a cover of tachash skins above.
And he made the beams for the mishkan,
standing acacia wood.
Ten cubits the length of the beam,

pairs.hebrew: וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: and a cubit and a half the breadth of each beam.

pairs.hebrew: שְׁתֵּ֣י יָדֹ֗ת לַקֶּ֙רֶשׁ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁ֨לָּבֹ֔ת אַחַ֖ת אֶל־אֶחָ֑ת
pairs.english: Two prongs for each beam, rung-like, one near the other.
So did he do for all the beams of the mishkan.
And he made the beams for the mishkan,
twenty beams for the southern side.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי־כֶ֔סֶף עָשָׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקְּרָשִׁ֑ים
pairs.english: And forty silver sockets he made under the twenty beams;

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו
pairs.english: two sockets under one beam for its two prongs,

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו׃
pairs.english: and two sockets under the next beam for its two prongs.
And for the second side of the mishkan, the northern side,
he made twenty beams.
And their forty silver sockets,
two sockets under one beam
and two sockets under the next beam.
And for the ends [i.e., the back] of the mishkan on the west,
he made six beams.
And two beams he made
for the corners of the mishkan at the ends.
And they were fitted against each other at the bottom,

pairs.hebrew: וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ אֶל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל־הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת
pairs.english: and together they were fitted at the top by the one ring.
So did he do for the two of them, for the two corners.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים
pairs.english: And [on the western side] there were eight beams and their silver sockets, sixteen sockets,

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנֵ֤י אֲדָנִים֙ שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: two sockets under each beam.
And he made bars of acacia wood,
five for the beams of one side of the mishkan.
And five bars for the beams of the second side of the mishkan,

pairs.hebrew: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֤ה בְרִיחִם֙ לְקַרְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לַיַּרְכָתַ֖יִם יָֽמָּה׃
pairs.english: and five bars for the beams of the mishkan at the western ends.
And he made the middle bar
to extend in the midst of the beams from end to end.
And the beams he covered with gold,
and their rings he made of gold [to serve as] housings for the bars;
and he covered the bars with gold.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֙עַשׂ֙ אֶת־הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר
pairs.english: And he made the parocheth of blue wool and purple wool and scarlet wool and twisted linen.
Artistic work he made it, cherubs.
And he made for it four pillars of acacia wood
and he covered them with gold, their hooks of gold.
And he cast for them four silver sockets.
And he made a screen for the entrance of the tent,

pairs.hebrew: תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֹקֵֽם׃
pairs.english: of blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
And its pillars five, and their hooks,
and he covered their tops and their belts with gold;
and their sockets five, of copper.
And Betzalel made the ark [(its making being ascribed to him rather than to the other artisans because of his total dedication to the work)], of acacia wood:
two and a half cubits, its length;

pairs.hebrew: וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֙צִי֙ רׇחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: one and a half cubits, its breadth; and one and a half cubits, its height.
And he covered it with pure gold from inside and from outside.
And he made for it a rim of gold roundabout.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו
pairs.english: And he cast for it four golden rings for its four corners;

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל־צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל־צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
pairs.english: two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
And he made staves of acacia wood
and he covered them with gold.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן
pairs.english: And he inserted the staves in the rings on the sides of the ark
to carry the ark therewith.
And he made a kaporeth of pure gold:

pairs.hebrew: אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֙צִי֙ אׇרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רׇחְבָּֽהּ׃
pairs.english: two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width.
And he made two golden cherubs.

pairs.hebrew: מִקְשָׁה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃
pairs.english: Of beaten work he made them, at the two ends of the kaporeth.

pairs.hebrew: כְּרוּב־אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב־אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: One cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end.
From the kaporeth [itself] he made the cherubs, from its two ends.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּהְי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹֽכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת
pairs.english: And the cherubs had their wings spread on high, covering the kaporeth with their wings from above.
And their faces were towards each other.
Towards the kaporeth were the faces of the cherubs.
And he made the table of acacia wood:
two cubits, its length; one cubit, its breadth;
and a cubit and a half, its height.
And he covered it with pure gold,
and he made for it a rim of gold roundabout.
And he made a frame for it, a handbreadth roundabout.
And he made a golden rim for its frame roundabout.
And he cast for it four golden rings.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: And he placed the rings on the four corners of its four legs.
Opposite the [corners of the] frame were the rings,
housings for the staves for the carrying of the table.
And he made the staves of acacia wood,
and he covered them with gold,
to carry the table therewith.
And he made the implements which were on the table:

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת־כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶ֨ת־הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר׃ {פ}
pairs.english: its [bread-] moulds, its censers, its canes, and its staves, by which [canes] it [the show-bread] was covered — pure gold.
And he made the menorah of pure gold.
Of beaten work did he make the menorah.

pairs.hebrew: יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ׃
pairs.english: Its base, its [central] shaft, its bowls, its bulbs, and its flowers were (fashioned) from it [the one piece of gold].
And six branches emerged from its sides,
three branches of the menorah from one side,
and three branches of the menorah from the other side.

pairs.hebrew: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִ֠ים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶ֒רַח֒
pairs.english: Three chased bowls on one branch, with bulb and flower;

pairs.hebrew: וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח
pairs.english: and three chased bowls on the other branch, with bulb and flower.
So, with (all) six branches that project from the menorah.
And on the [central shaft of the] menorah were four bowls,
chased, its bulbs and its flowers.
And a bulb under the two branches from it [the one piece of gold],
and a bulb under the (next) two branches from it,

pairs.hebrew: וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֙שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
pairs.english: and a bulb under the next two branches from it, (thus) for (all) the six branches that project from it.
Their bulbs and their branches from it were (fashioned),
all one (piece of) beaten work of pure gold.
And he made its lamps, seven,
and its tongs and its snuff-dishes, pure gold.
(Of) a talent of pure gold he made it
[together] with all of its vessels.
And he made the incense altar of acacia wood,

pairs.hebrew: אַמָּ֣ה אׇרְכּוֹ֩ וְאַמָּ֨ה רׇחְבּ֜וֹ רָב֗וּעַ וְאַמָּתַ֙יִם֙ קֹֽמָת֔וֹ
pairs.english: a cubit its length and a cubit its width — square — and two cubits its height.
From it were its horns (made).

pairs.hebrew: וַיְצַ֨ף אֹת֜וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֗וֹר אֶת־גַּגּ֧וֹ וְאֶת־קִירֹתָ֛יו סָבִ֖יב וְאֶת־קַרְנֹתָ֑יו
pairs.english: And he covered it with pure gold, its roof and its walls roundabout and its horns.
And he made for it a rim of gold roundabout.
And he made for it two golden rings,

pairs.hebrew: מִתַּ֣חַת לְזֵר֗וֹ עַ֚ל שְׁתֵּ֣י צַלְעֹתָ֔יו עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י צִדָּ֑יו
pairs.english: beneath its rim at its two corners, on its two sides,
for housings for the staves to carry it thereby.
And he made the staves of acacia wood
and he covered them with gold.
And he made the oil of sacred anointment
and the pure incense spices, the work of a spice blender.
And he made the burnt-offering altar of acacia wood,

pairs.hebrew: חָמֵשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת אׇרְכּ֜וֹ וְחָֽמֵשׁ־אַמּ֤וֹת רׇחְבּוֹ֙ רָב֔וּעַ
pairs.english: five cubits its length and five cubits its width — square —
and three cubits its height.
And he made its horns on its four corners.
From it [the altar itself] were its horns (made).
And he covered it with copper.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת־כׇּל־כְּלֵ֣י הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ אֶת־הַסִּירֹ֤ת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִים֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָקֹ֔ת אֶת־הַמִּזְלָגֹ֖ת וְאֶת־הַמַּחְתֹּ֑ת
pairs.english: And he made all the implements of the altar: the pots, and the shovels, and the sprinkling basins, and the spits, and the fire-pans.
All of its implements he made of copper.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ מִכְבָּ֔ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֶ֣שֶׁת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת
pairs.english: And he made for the altar a copper lattice, netting work,
under its karkov [an encircling decorative band] below, (and the netting extended) until its (the altar's) mid-point.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּצֹ֞ק אַרְבַּ֧ע טַבָּעֹ֛ת בְּאַרְבַּ֥ע הַקְּצָוֺ֖ת לְמִכְבַּ֣ר הַנְּחֹ֑שֶׁת
pairs.english: And he cast four rings on the four edges of the copper lattice,
housings for the staves.
And he made the staves of acacia wood,
and he covered them with copper.

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּבֵ֨א אֶת־הַבַּדִּ֜ים בַּטַּבָּעֹ֗ת עַ֚ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ לָשֵׂ֥את אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And he inserted the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar to carry it therewith.
A hollow of boards did he make it [the altar].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֗עַשׂ אֵ֚ת הַכִּיּ֣וֹר נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְאֵ֖ת כַּנּ֣וֹ נְחֹ֑שֶׁת
pairs.english: And he made the kiyyor (the laver) of copper and its pedestal of copper

pairs.hebrew: בְּמַרְאֹת֙ הַצֹּ֣בְאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר צָֽבְא֔וּ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃ {ס}
pairs.english: with [the copper of] the mirrors of the congregating women, who congregated [to bring their contributions] at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And he made the court (of the mishkan),

pairs.hebrew: לִפְאַ֣ת ׀ נֶ֣גֶב תֵּימָ֗נָה קַלְעֵ֤י הֶֽחָצֵר֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֔ר מֵאָ֖ה בָּאַמָּֽה׃
pairs.english: on the southern side, the curtains of the court of twisted linen, a hundred cubits (long on one side).
Their pillars twenty and their sockets twenty, of copper;
the hooks of the pillars and their belts, of silver.
And on the northern side, a hundred cubits,
their pillars twenty and their sockets twenty, of copper;
the hooks of the pillars and their belts, of silver.
And on the western side, curtains, fifty cubits,
their pillars ten, and their sockets, ten;
the hooks of the pillars and their belts, of silver.
And on the front side, to the east,
fifty cubits.
Curtains, fifteen cubits, on the shoulder,
their pillars three and their sockets three.

pairs.hebrew: וְלַכָּתֵ֣ף הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית מִזֶּ֤ה וּמִזֶּה֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הֶֽחָצֵ֔ר קְלָעִ֕ים חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה אַמָּ֑ה
pairs.english: And on the second shoulder, (one) on either side of the gate of the court, curtains, fifteen cubits,
their pillars three and their sockets three.
All the curtains of the court roundabout,
of twisted linen.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָאֲדָנִ֣ים לָֽעַמֻּדִים֮ נְחֹ֒שֶׁת֒ וָוֵ֨י הָֽעַמּוּדִ֜ים וַחֲשׁוּקֵיהֶם֙ כֶּ֔סֶף
pairs.english: And the sockets for the pillars, of copper, the hooks of the pillars and their belts, of silver,
and the covering of their tops, of silver.

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵם֙ מְחֻשָּׁקִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף כֹּ֖ל עַמֻּדֵ֥י הֶחָצֵֽר׃
pairs.english: And they were belted with silver, all the pillars of the court.

pairs.hebrew: וּמָסַ֞ךְ שַׁ֤עַר הֶחָצֵר֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֔ם תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר
pairs.english: And the screen of the gate of the court, the work of an embroiderer, blue wool, and purple wool, and scarlet wool, and twisted linen;
and (it was) twenty cubits long,

pairs.hebrew: וְקוֹמָ֤ה בְרֹ֙חַב֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת לְעֻמַּ֖ת קַלְעֵ֥י הֶחָצֵֽר׃
pairs.english: and high in (its) width five cubits, as the size [five cubits] of the curtains of the court.
And their pillars four and their sockets four, of copper;

pairs.hebrew: וָוֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף וְצִפּ֧וּי רָאשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃
pairs.english: their hooks, of silver, and the covering of their tops and their belt, of silver.
And all the pegs of the mishkan and of the court roundabout,
of copper.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה פְקוּדֵ֤י הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר פֻּקַּ֖ד עַל־פִּ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה
pairs.english: These are the accountings of the [donations for and the appurtenances of] the mishkan, the mishkan of testimony [testimony to G d's having "bypassed" the sin of the golden calf, having reposed His shechinah there. (The doubling of "mishkan" alludes to the Temple's twice having been taken as "collateral" (mashkon) for the sins of Israel)], (the accountings made) by word of Moses

pairs.hebrew: עֲבֹדַת֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בְּיַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
pairs.english: [of the articles of] the service of the Levites, [the Levites carrying them, setting them up, and taking them down] as designated by Ithamar the son of Aaron the Cohein, [Ithamar assigning to each Levitical "father's house" its specific service.]
And Betzalel the son of Uri the son of Chur of the tribe of Judah

did all that the L-rd had commanded Moses, [even things which Moses had not "relayed" to Betzalel. Moses first charged Betzalel to make the appurtenances and then the mishkan, and Betzalel, in practice, reversed the order, this, ("making the house first and then the furnishing"), indeed, according with what the L-rd had commanded Moses.]
And with him, Ahaliav the son of Achisamach of the tribe of Dan,

pairs.hebrew: חָרָ֣שׁ וְחֹשֵׁ֑ב וְרֹקֵ֗ם בַּתְּכֵ֙לֶת֙ וּבָֽאַרְגָּמָ֔ן וּבְתוֹלַ֥עַת הַשָּׁנִ֖י וּבַשֵּֽׁשׁ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: craftsman, artist, and embroiderer, in blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and linen.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַזָּהָ֗ב הֶֽעָשׂוּי֙ לַמְּלָאכָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: All the gold that was used for the work, in all the work of the sanctuary —

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ זְהַ֣ב הַתְּנוּפָ֗ה תֵּ֤שַׁע וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ כִּכָּ֔ר וּשְׁבַ֨ע מֵא֧וֹת וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: the gold of the offering was twenty-nine kikar [(one kikar = three thousand shekels)] and seven hundred and thirty shekels in the shekel of the sanctuary.
And the silver of the accountings of the assembly: a hundred kikar [(accounting for six hundred thousand people, each giving a half shekel)],

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶ֩לֶף֩ וּשְׁבַ֨ע מֵא֜וֹת וַחֲמִשָּׁ֧ה וְשִׁבְעִ֛ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: and one thousand and seven hundred and seventy-five shekels in the shekel of the sanctuary.

pairs.hebrew: בֶּ֚קַע לַגֻּלְגֹּ֔לֶת מַחֲצִ֥ית הַשֶּׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: A beka [a half shekel] for every head, a half shekel in the shekel of the sanctuary

pairs.hebrew: לְכֹ֨ל הָעֹבֵ֜ר עַל־הַפְּקֻדִ֗ים מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה
pairs.english: for all who passed to be counted, from the age of twenty years and above,

pairs.hebrew: לְשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֙לֶף֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וַחֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וַחֲמִשִּֽׁים׃
pairs.english: for six hundred and three thousand and five hundred and fifty (men).

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י מְאַת֙ כִּכַּ֣ר הַכֶּ֔סֶף לָצֶ֗קֶת אֵ֚ת אַדְנֵ֣י הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וְאֵ֖ת אַדְנֵ֣י הַפָּרֹ֑כֶת
pairs.english: And the hundred kikar of silver were for casting the sockets of the [beams of the] sanctuary [the mishkan (ninety-six sockets for forty-eight beams)] and the sockets of the parocheth [(four sockets for four pillars)].

pairs.hebrew: מְאַ֧ת אֲדָנִ֛ים לִמְאַ֥ת הַכִּכָּ֖ר כִּכָּ֥ר לָאָֽדֶן׃
pairs.english: A hundred sockets for a hundred kikar, a kikar per socket.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־הָאֶ֜לֶף וּשְׁבַ֤ע הַמֵּאוֹת֙ וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה וְשִׁבְעִ֔ים עָשָׂ֥ה וָוִ֖ים לָעַמּוּדִ֑ים
pairs.english: And from the one thousand and seven hundred and seventy-five, he made hooks for the pillars
and covered their [the pillars'] tops and belted them.
And the copper of the offering was seventy kikar
and two thousand and four hundred shekels.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּ֗הּ אֶת־אַדְנֵי֙ פֶּ֚תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד
pairs.english: And he made of it the sockets of the entrance of the tent of meeting,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַנְּחֹ֔שֶׁת וְאֶת־מִכְבַּ֥ר הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְאֵ֖ת כׇּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
pairs.english: and the copper altar, and its copper lattice, and all the implements of the altar.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־אַדְנֵ֤י הֶֽחָצֵר֙ סָבִ֔יב וְאֶת־אַדְנֵ֖י שַׁ֣עַר הֶחָצֵ֑ר
pairs.english: And the sockets of the court roundabout, and the sockets of the gate of the court,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת כׇּל־יִתְדֹ֧ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן וְאֶת־כׇּל־יִתְדֹ֥ת הֶחָצֵ֖ר סָבִֽיב׃
pairs.english: and all the pegs of the mishkan, and all the pegs of the court roundabout.

pairs.hebrew: וּמִן־הַתְּכֵ֤לֶת וְהָֽאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתוֹלַ֣עַת הַשָּׁנִ֔י עָשׂ֥וּ בִגְדֵי־שְׂרָ֖ד לְשָׁרֵ֣ת בַּקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And from the purple wool and the blue wool they made mesh vestments for covering the holy (appurtenances) [see 35:19]
and they made the consecrated garments of Aaron,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.
And he made the ephod

pairs.hebrew: זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מׇשְׁזָֽר׃
pairs.english: of gold, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen.
And they beat the plates of gold and cut [from the thin plate] strands

pairs.hebrew: לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת בְּת֤וֹךְ הַתְּכֵ֙לֶת֙ וּבְת֣וֹךְ הָֽאַרְגָּמָ֔ן וּבְת֛וֹךְ תּוֹלַ֥עַת הַשָּׁנִ֖י וּבְת֣וֹךְ הַשֵּׁ֑שׁ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה חֹשֵֽׁב׃
pairs.english: to work into the blue wool [(i.e., one thread of gold intertwined with six of blue wool, etc.)]. And into the purple wool, and into the scarlet wool, and into the linen, the work of an artist.
Shoulder straps did they make for it, attached —
attached at its two ends.

pairs.hebrew: וְחֵ֨שֶׁב אֲפֻדָּת֜וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֗יו מִמֶּ֣נּוּ הוּא֮ כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֒הוּ֒
pairs.english: And the cheishev [the belt] of his adornment which is above it, was of it, after its manner [see 28:8],

pairs.hebrew: זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר
pairs.english: gold, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ אֶת־אַבְנֵ֣י הַשֹּׁ֔הַם מֻֽסַבֹּ֖ת מִשְׁבְּצֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב
pairs.english: And they made the shoham stones surrounded by golden settings,

pairs.hebrew: מְפֻתָּחֹת֙ פִּתּוּחֵ֣י חוֹתָ֔ם עַל־שְׁמ֖וֹת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: engraved as the engraving of a signet with the names of the children of Israel.
And he placed them on the shoulder straps of the ephod,
stones of remembrance for the children of Israel,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ אֶת־הַחֹ֛שֶׁן מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֖ב כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֵפֹ֑ד
pairs.english: And he made the choshen, artistic work, like the work of the ephod:

pairs.hebrew: זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מׇשְׁזָֽר׃
pairs.english: gold, blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen.
It was square; folded did they make the choshen,
a zereth its length and a zereth its width, folded.
And they filled it with four rows of stone.

pairs.hebrew: ט֗וּר אֹ֤דֶם פִּטְדָה֙ וּבָרֶ֔קֶת הַטּ֖וּר הָאֶחָֽד׃
pairs.english: A row of odem, pitedah and bareketh, the one row.
The second row —
nofech, sapir, and yahalom.
The third row —
leshem, shevo, and achlamah.
And the fourth row — tarshish, shoham, and yashfeh.
They were surrounded by golden settings with their fillings [see 28:20].

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠הָאֲבָנִ֠ים עַל־שְׁמֹ֨ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל הֵ֛נָּה שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה עַל־שְׁמֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names,

pairs.hebrew: פִּתּוּחֵ֤י חֹתָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל־שְׁמ֔וֹ לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר שָֽׁבֶט׃
pairs.english: like the engraving of a signet, each by his name for the twelve tribes.
And they made for the choshen chains at the edge,
braidwork of pure gold.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֗וּ שְׁתֵּי֙ מִשְׁבְּצֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וּשְׁתֵּ֖י טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב
pairs.english: And they made two golden settings and two golden rings,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַחֹֽשֶׁן׃
pairs.english: and they placed the two rings on the two settings of the choshen.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּתְּנ֗וּ שְׁתֵּי֙ הָעֲבֹתֹ֣ת הַזָּהָ֔ב עַל־שְׁתֵּ֖י הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And they placed the two golden braids on the two rings
at the ends of the choshen.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֨ת שְׁתֵּ֤י קְצוֹת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הָֽעֲבֹתֹ֔ת נָתְנ֖וּ עַל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַֽמִּשְׁבְּצֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And the two ends of the two braids they placed on the two settings
and they placed them on the shoulder straps of the ephod on its face.
And they made two golden rings,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּשִׂ֕ימוּ עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י קְצ֣וֹת הַחֹ֑שֶׁן עַל־שְׂפָת֕וֹ אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֶל־עֵ֥בֶר הָאֵפֹ֖ד בָּֽיְתָה׃
pairs.english: and they placed them on the two ends of the choshen on its edge which faces the ephod, inwards.
And they made two golden rings,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּתְּנֻ֡ם עַל־שְׁתֵּי֩ כִתְפֹ֨ת הָאֵפֹ֤ד מִלְּמַ֙טָּה֙ מִמּ֣וּל פָּנָ֔יו לְעֻמַּ֖ת מַחְבַּרְתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: and they placed them on the (origin of the) two shoulder straps of the ephod below, on its face, opposite [i.e., near] where it is attached,
above the cheishev of the ephod.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּרְכְּס֣וּ אֶת־הַחֹ֡שֶׁן מִטַּבְּעֹתָיו֩ אֶל־טַבְּעֹ֨ת הָאֵפֹ֜ד בִּפְתִ֣יל תְּכֵ֗לֶת לִֽהְיֹת֙ עַל־חֵ֣שֶׁב הָאֵפֹ֔ד
pairs.english: And they bound the choshen from its rings to the rings of the ephod with a string of blue wool to be on the cheishev of the ephod.
And the choshen shall not be detached from the ephod,
as the L-rd commanded Moses.
And he made the me'il of the ephod, the work of a weaver,
entirely of blue wool.
And the head-opening of the me'il was (folded over) within it, as the opening of a suit of armor.
Its opening had a border roundabout, so that it not be torn.
And they made on the (lower) hem of the me'il

pairs.hebrew: רִמּוֹנֵ֕י תְּכֵ֥לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֖ן וְתוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֑י מׇשְׁזָֽר׃
pairs.english: pomegranates of blue wool, and purple wool, and scarlet wool, twisted.
And they made bells of pure gold,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אֶת־הַפַּֽעֲמֹנִ֜ים בְּת֣וֹךְ הָרִמֹּנִ֗ים עַל־שׁוּלֵ֤י הַמְּעִיל֙ סָבִ֔יב בְּת֖וֹךְ הָרִמֹּנִֽים׃
pairs.english: and they placed the bells in the midst of the pomegranates, on the hem of the me'il roundabout in the midst of the pomegranates.

pairs.hebrew: פַּעֲמֹ֤ן וְרִמֹּן֙ פַּעֲמֹ֣ן וְרִמֹּ֔ן עַל־שׁוּלֵ֥י הַמְּעִ֖יל סָבִ֑יב לְשָׁרֵ֕ת
pairs.english: A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the me'il roundabout, to minister,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.
And they made the kathnoth of linen, the work of a weaver,
for Aaron and his sons.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ הַמִּצְנֶ֣פֶת שֵׁ֔שׁ וְאֶת־פַּאֲרֵ֥י הַמִּגְבָּעֹ֖ת שֵׁ֑שׁ
pairs.english: And the mitznefeth of linen, and the splendrous migbaoth of linen
and the linen michnasayim of twisted linen.

pairs.hebrew: וְֽאֶת־הָאַבְנֵ֞ט שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֑ם
pairs.english: And the avneit of twisted linen and blue wool, purple wool, and scarlet wool, the work of an embroiderer,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.
And they made the tzitz, the holy crown of pure gold.
And they inscribed it as the engraving of a signet:
"Holy to the L-rd."

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ עָלָיו֙ פְּתִ֣יל תְּכֵ֔לֶת לָתֵ֥ת עַל־הַמִּצְנֶ֖פֶת מִלְמָ֑עְלָה
pairs.english: And they placed on it a string of blue wool to place on the mitznefeth from above,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.
And all the work of the mishkan of the tent of meeting was completed.

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּ֠כֹ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And the children of Israel did [the work]. As all that the L-rd had commanded Moses; thus did they do.
And they brought the mishkan to Moses [to set up (lacking the strength to do it themselves)], the tent and all its implements:
its hooks, its beams, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־מִכְסֵ֞ה עוֹרֹ֤ת הָֽאֵילִם֙ הַמְאׇדָּמִ֔ים וְאֶת־מִכְסֵ֖ה עֹרֹ֣ת הַתְּחָשִׁ֑ים
pairs.english: And the cover of rams' skins dyed red, and the cover of tachash skins,
and the parocheth partition.
The ark of testimony and its staves
and the kaporeth.
The table and all its implements
and the show-bread.

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־הַמְּנֹרָ֨ה הַטְּהֹרָ֜ה אֶת־נֵרֹתֶ֗יהָ נֵרֹ֛ת הַמַּֽעֲרָכָ֖ה וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: The pure menorah, its lamps — the lamps of the arrangement (27:21) — and all its implements
and the oil for lighting.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַזָּהָ֔ב וְאֵת֙ שֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת קְטֹ֣רֶת הַסַּמִּ֑ים
pairs.english: And the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the spice incense,
and the partition for the entrance of the tent.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת ׀ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַנְּחֹ֗שֶׁת וְאֶת־מִכְבַּ֤ר הַנְּחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ אֶת־בַּדָּ֖יו וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֑יו
pairs.english: The copper altar, its copper lattice, its staves, and all its implements,
the kiyyor and its pedestal.

pairs.hebrew: אֵת֩ קַלְעֵ֨י הֶחָצֵ֜ר אֶת־עַמֻּדֶ֣יהָ וְאֶת־אֲדָנֶ֗יהָ וְאֶת־הַמָּסָךְ֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הֶֽחָצֵ֔ר אֶת־מֵיתָרָ֖יו וִיתֵדֹתֶ֑יהָ
pairs.english: The curtains of the court, its pillars and its sockets and the partition for the gate of the court, its cords and its pegs,

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֗ת כׇּל־כְּלֵ֛י עֲבֹדַ֥ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן לְאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: and all the implements of the service of the mishkan of the tent of meeting.
The mesh vestments for covering the holy (appurtenances),

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֤י הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ לְאַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶת־בִּגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו לְכַהֵֽן׃
pairs.english: the consecrated garments of Aaron the Cohein, and the garments of his sons for ministering.
As all that the L-rd had commanded Moses,

pairs.hebrew: כֵּ֤ן עָשׂוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כׇּל־הָעֲבֹדָֽה׃
pairs.english: thus did the children of Israel do all of the work.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨רְא מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־כׇּל־הַמְּלָאכָ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ עָשׂ֣וּ אֹתָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה כֵּ֣ן עָשׂ֑וּ
pairs.english: And Moses saw all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the L-rd had commanded; thus had they done it.
And Moses blessed them.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
On the first day of the first month,
you shall set up the mishkan of the tent of meeting.
And you shall place there the ark of testimony,
and you shall screen the ark with the parocheth.
And you shall bring the table and make its arrangement [the two arrangements of the show bread (see Leviticus 24:5-6)],
and you shall bring the menorah and you shall light its lamps.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֞ה אֶת־מִזְבַּ֤ח הַזָּהָב֙ לִקְטֹ֔רֶת לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵדֻ֑ת
pairs.english: And you shall place the golden altar for (smoking) incense before the ark of testimony,
and you shall place the entrance partition for the mishkan.
And you shall place the burnt-offering altar
before the entrance of the mishkan of the tent of meeting.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָֽתַתָּ֙ אֶת־הַכִּיֹּ֔ר בֵּֽין־אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ
pairs.english: And you shall place the kiyyor between the tent of meeting and the altar
and you shall put water there.
And you shall set up the court roundabout,
and you shall place the screen of the gate of the court.
And you shall take the anointing oil
and you shall anoint the mishkan and all that is in it.
And you shall consecrate it and all of its appurtenances, and it shall be holy.
And you shall anoint the burnt-offering altar and all of its implements.

pairs.hebrew: וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְהָיָ֥ה הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קׇֽדָשִֽׁים׃
pairs.english: And you shall consecrate the altar, and the altar shall be holy of holies.
And you shall anoint the kiyyor and its pedestal,
and you shall consecrate it.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֤ אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֔יו אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: And you shall bring near Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting
and you shall wash them with water.
And you shall clothe Aaron in the holy garments,
and you shall anoint him, and you shall consecrate him,
and he shall minister unto Me.
And his sons shall you bring near,
and you shall dress them in kutanoth.
And you shall anoint them as you anointed their father.
And they shall minister unto Me.

pairs.hebrew: וְ֠הָיְתָ֠ה לִהְיֹ֨ת לָהֶ֧ם מׇשְׁחָתָ֛ם לִכְהֻנַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: and this will serve for their anointment to be for them an eternal kehunah for their generations.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֑ה כְּ֠כֹ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֹת֖וֹ
pairs.english: And Moses did as all that the L-rd had commanded him;
thus did he do.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֞י בַּחֹ֧דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֛וֹן בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And it was in the first month of the second year on the first of the month
that the mishkan was set up.
And Moses erected the mishkan.
