pairs.hebrew: וְזֹ֣את ׀ עֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם וְחָיוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יָמֻ֔תוּ בְּגִשְׁתָּ֖ם אֶת־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים
pairs.english: But do this for them and they will live and not die when they approach the holy of holies:

pairs.hebrew: אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּבָנָיו֙ יָבֹ֔אוּ וְשָׂמ֣וּ אוֹתָ֗ם אִ֥ישׁ אִ֛ישׁ עַל־עֲבֹדָת֖וֹ וְאֶל־מַשָּׂאֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: Aaron and his sons shall come and set them, each man to his service and to his burden.
And they shall not come to see when the holy (things) are being covered [within their sheath (5)]
and die.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Take the count of the sons of Gershon, they too, [as I commanded you in respect to the sons of Kehath, to see how many of them qualify for service],
by their fathers' houses, by their families.

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּן֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה וָמַ֗עְלָה עַ֛ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תִּפְקֹ֣ד אוֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: From thirty years and up until fifty years,

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַבָּא֙ לִצְבֹ֣א צָבָ֔א לַעֲבֹ֥ד עֲבֹדָ֖ה בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: all who enter into service, to serve in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the families of the Gershuni
for service and for burden.
They shall bear the curtains of the mishkan [the ten lower ones] and of the tent of meeting [the goats' hair curtains which tented it],
its covering [the rams' skins dyed red] and the tachash covering that is on it from above,
and the partition for the door of the tent of meeting [i.e., the eastern curtain].

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵת֩ קַלְעֵ֨י הֶֽחָצֵ֜ר וְאֶת־מָסַ֣ךְ ׀ פֶּ֣תַח ׀ שַׁ֣עַר הֶחָצֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֤ן וְעַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ סָבִ֔יב
pairs.english: And the curtains of the court, and the partition for the door of the gate of the court which shield the mishkan and the [copper] altar roundabout,
and their cords, and all their service implements,
and all that is relegated to them [the sons of Gershon] that they may serve.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־פִּי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן וּבָנָ֜יו תִּהְיֶ֗ה כׇּל־עֲבֹדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֔י לְכׇ֨ל־מַשָּׂאָ֔ם וּלְכֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתָ֑ם
pairs.english: By word of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershuni for all of their burdens and for all of their service.
And you shall designate unto them the charge of all their burdens.

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֗ת מִשְׁפְּחֹ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: This is the service of the families of the sons of the Gershuni in the tent of meeting.
And their charge shall be by the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the Cohein.
The sons of Merari —
by their families, by their fathers' house shall you number them.

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּן֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה וָמַ֗עְלָה וְעַ֛ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תִּפְקְדֵ֑ם
pairs.english: From thirty years and up until fifty years shall you number them,

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַבָּא֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לַעֲבֹ֕ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: all who enter into service, to perform the service of the tent of meeting.

pairs.hebrew: וְזֹאת֙ מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת מַשָּׂאָ֔ם לְכׇל־עֲבֹדָתָ֖ם בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: And this is the charge of their burden for all of their service in the tent of meeting:
the beams of the mishkan and its bars, and its pillars and its sockets.

pairs.hebrew: וְעַמּוּדֵי֩ הֶחָצֵ֨ר סָבִ֜יב וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֗ם וִיתֵֽדֹתָם֙ וּמֵ֣יתְרֵיהֶ֔ם לְכׇ֨ל־כְּלֵיהֶ֔ם וּלְכֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the pillars of the court roundabout, and their [the pillars'] pins and cords [for hanging of the curtains on the pillars], with all of their implements for all of their service.
And by name shall you reckon the implements of the charge of their bearing.

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֣את עֲבֹדַ֗ת מִשְׁפְּחֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י לְכׇל־עֲבֹדָתָ֖ם בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: This is the service of the families of the sons of Merari for all of their service in the tent of meeting
by the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the Cohein.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּפְקֹ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן וּנְשִׂיאֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י הַקְּהָתִ֑י
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the congregation numbered the sons of the Kehathi
by their families and by their fathers' house.

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: From thirty years and up until fifty years,
all who entered the service for service in the tent of meeting.
And their numbered ones by their families were
two thousand and seven hundred and fifty.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֤לֶּה פְקוּדֵי֙ מִשְׁפְּחֹ֣ת הַקְּהָתִ֔י כׇּל־הָעֹבֵ֖ד בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: These are the numbered of the families of the Kehathi, all who serve in the tent of meeting,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּקַ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן עַל־פִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ {ס}
pairs.english: whom Moses and Aaron numbered by word of the L-rd by the hand of Moses.
And the numbered ones of the sons of Gershon
by their families and by their fathers' house,

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: From thirty years and up until fifty years,
all who entered the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
Their numbered ones by their families by their fathers' house were
two thousand and six hundred and thirty.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה פְקוּדֵ֗י מִשְׁפְּחֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י גֵרְשׁ֔וֹן כׇּל־הָעֹבֵ֖ד בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: These are the numbered of the families of the sons of Gershon, all who serve in the tent of meeting,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּקַ֥ד מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן עַל־פִּ֥י יְהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: whom Moses and Aaron numbered by word of the L-rd.
And the numbered of the families of the sons of Merari,
by their families by their fathers' house,

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: From thirty years and up until fifty years,
all who entered the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
Their numbered ones by their families were
three thousand and two hundred.
These are the numbered of the families of the sons of Merari,

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּקַ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן עַל־פִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
pairs.english: whom Moses and Aaron numbered by word of the L-rd by the hand of Moses.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּֽל־הַפְּקֻדִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ פָּקַ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן וּנְשִׂיאֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֑ם
pairs.english: All the numbered ones, whom Moses and Aaron and all the chiefs of Israel numbered of the Levites
by their families and by their fathers' house.

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
pairs.english: From thirty years and up until fifty years,

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַבָּ֗א לַעֲבֹ֨ד עֲבֹדַ֧ת עֲבֹדָ֛ה וַעֲבֹדַ֥ת מַשָּׂ֖א בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: all who entered to serve — the service [of song, with cymbals and lutes,] of [i.e., on behalf of] service [the sacrificial service] and the service of bearing in the tent of meeting.
Their numbered ones were
eight thousand and five hundred and eighty.
By word of the L-rd did he count them, by the hand of Moses,
each for his service and for his burden.
And their numbered ones were as the L-rd had commanded Moses [i.e., from thirty years and up until fifty].
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:

Command the children of Israel [(This section was stated on the day that the mishkan was erected)] that they send out of the camp [(There were three camps: the camp of the Shechinah — within the curtains (of the mishkan); the camp of the Levites — the encampment of the Levites roundabout (the mishkan); the camp of Israel — from the camp of the Levites until the end of the encampment of the standards on all four sides)]

every leper, [to be sent out of all three camps)], every zav [to be sent out of the first two camps (see Leviticus 15:2)] and everyone who has become unclean by a dead body [to be sent out only from the first camp].

pairs.hebrew: מִזָּכָ֤ר עַד־נְקֵבָה֙ תְּשַׁלֵּ֔חוּ אֶל־מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה תְּשַׁלְּח֑וּם
pairs.english: From male until female shall you send them out. Outside of the camp shall you send them;

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֤א יְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת־מַ֣חֲנֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י שֹׁכֵ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃
pairs.english: and they shall not make unclean their camps in whose midst I dwell.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְשַׁלְּח֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה
pairs.english: And the children of Israel did so, and they sent them outside the camp.

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ {פ}
pairs.english: As the L-rd spoke to Moses, so did the children of Israel do.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Speak to the children of Israel:

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַעֲשׂוּ֙ מִכׇּל־חַטֹּ֣את הָֽאָדָ֔ם לִמְעֹ֥ל מַ֖עַל בַּיהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: A man or a woman, if they do of all the sins of man to commit a profanation against the L-rd [and swear falsely in denial of a claim],

and that soul be guilty, [(Although this has already been stated (Leviticus 5:21), it is repeated here for two new teachings: First (7) that one is not liable for the fifth and the guilt-offering by the testimony of witnesses, but only by his own confession; second (8) that the stolen property of a proselyte (without heirs) is given to the Cohanim)],
And they confess their sins which they have done,

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵשִׁ֤יב אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ֙ בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַחֲמִישִׁת֖וֹ יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑יו
pairs.english: then he shall make restitution for his guilt by (restoration of) its (the theft's) principal, and its fifth shall he add to it,
and he shall give it to the one to whom he is liable [for payment].

pairs.hebrew: וְאִם־אֵ֨ין לָאִ֜ישׁ גֹּאֵ֗ל לְהָשִׁ֤יב הָאָשָׁם֙ אֵלָ֔יו
pairs.english: And if the man does not have a redeemer to whom to return the debt, [the claimant, a proselyte, having died and left no heirs],
the debt [the principal], which is returned [i.e., "and the fifth"] is the L-rd's [i.e., He has acquired it, and He has given it] to the Cohein [of the officiating watch],

pairs.hebrew: מִלְּבַ֗ד אֵ֚יל הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְכַפֶּר־בּ֖וֹ עָלָֽיו׃
pairs.english: aside from the ram of atonement whereby atonement shall be made for him.
And every terumah of all the holy things of the children of Israel which they present to the Cohein [i.e., bikkurim (first-fruits)],
to him shall it be.
And every man, his holy things, to him shall they be [i.e., he has the privilege of giving them to whichever Cohein he wishes.]
Whatever [designated gifts] a man gives to the Cohein, to him shall it be [i.e., it shall redound to the giver's wealth.]
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them:

pairs.hebrew: אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ כִּֽי־תִשְׂטֶ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וּמָעֲלָ֥ה ב֖וֹ מָֽעַל׃
pairs.english: A man, if his wife go astray, and she be faithless to him,
And [(the faithlessness being that)] a man [(excluding a minor or an animal)] lie with her a lying of seed,

pairs.hebrew: וְנֶעְלַם֙ מֵעֵינֵ֣י אִישָׁ֔הּ וְנִסְתְּרָ֖ה וְהִ֣יא נִטְמָ֑אָה
pairs.english: and it be hid [(but if he saw and made himself "unseeing," the waters do not probe her)] from the eyes [(excluding a blind man)] of her husband, and she had secreted herself [with him long enough for intercourse], and she be defiled,

pairs.hebrew: וְעֵד֙ אֵ֣ין בָּ֔הּ וְהִ֖וא לֹ֥א נִתְפָּֽשָׂה׃
pairs.english: and there be no witness to it [to the act of intercourse (for if there were even one witness to the act, the draught is not administered to her), but there be witnesses to her having secreted herself with him], and she had not been seized [i.e., forced],

pairs.hebrew: וְעָבַ֨ר עָלָ֧יו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָ֛ה וְקִנֵּ֥א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְהִ֣וא נִטְמָ֑אָה
pairs.english: And [before she had secreted herself] there had passed over him a spirit of rancor and he had warned his wife [not to secrete herself with that man], and she were defiled [i.e., she might have been defiled] —

pairs.hebrew: אוֹ־עָבַ֨ר עָלָ֤יו רֽוּחַ־קִנְאָה֙ וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְהִ֖יא לֹ֥א נִטְמָֽאָה׃
pairs.english: Or, there had passed over him a spirit of rancor and he had warned his wife [and she had transgressed his warning (and secreted herself)] and she were not defiled [i.e., it is not known whether she were or were not defiled],
Then the man shall bring his wife to the Cohein,

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵבִ֤יא אֶת־קׇרְבָּנָהּ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ עֲשִׂירִ֥ת הָאֵיפָ֖ה קֶ֣מַח שְׂעֹרִ֑ים
pairs.english: and he shall bring her offering for her, the tenth of an ephah of meal [(not fine flour)] of barley [(not wheat, the offering for a "beastly" act being the food of a beast)].

pairs.hebrew: לֹֽא־יִצֹ֨ק עָלָ֜יו שֶׁ֗מֶן וְלֹֽא־יִתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ לְבֹנָ֔ה
pairs.english: He shall not pour oil upon it, [so that her offering not be beautified], and he shall not place frankincense upon it,

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־מִנְחַ֤ת קְנָאֹת֙ ה֔וּא מִנְחַ֥ת זִכָּר֖וֹן מַזְכֶּ֥רֶת עָוֺֽן׃
pairs.english: for it is a meal-offering of rancors [the L-rd's and her husband's], a meal-offering of memorial, a reminder of sin.
And the Cohein shall draw her near
and stand her before the L-rd [at the gate of Nikanor, the eastern gate, where all entered.]
And the Cohein shall take water consecrated [in the laver] in an earthen vessel.

pairs.hebrew: וּמִן־הֶֽעָפָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה֙ בְּקַרְקַ֣ע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן יִקַּ֥ח הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְנָתַ֥ן אֶל־הַמָּֽיִם׃
pairs.english: And of the dust that is on the floor of the mishkan shall the Cohein take and place it in the water.
And the Cohein shall stand the woman before the L-rd [again (see 16). (They would walk her from place to place to "weary" her into confession)];
and he shall dishevel the hair of the woman [in order to shame her],

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַ֣ן עַל־כַּפֶּ֗יהָ אֵ֚ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַזִּכָּר֔וֹן מִנְחַ֥ת קְנָאֹ֖ת הִ֑וא
pairs.english: and he shall place in her hands the meal-offering of memorial, [to "weary" her into confession so that the Tetragrammaton not be erased in the waters] — it is a meal-offering of rancors —

pairs.hebrew: וּבְיַ֤ד הַכֹּהֵן֙ יִהְי֔וּ מֵ֥י הַמָּרִ֖ים הַמְאָֽרְרִֽים׃
pairs.english: and in the hand of the Cohein will be the bitter [(causing her a "bitter" end)] blighting waters [("blighting" her from the world)].
And the Cohein shall beswear her and he shall say to the woman:

pairs.hebrew: אִם־לֹ֨א שָׁכַ֥ב אִישׁ֙ אֹתָ֔ךְ וְאִם־לֹ֥א שָׂטִ֛ית טֻמְאָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ
pairs.english: If no man has lain with you, and you have not strayed uncleanly from your husband,
then be clean (hinaki) of these bitter, blighting waters.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַ֗תְּ כִּ֥י שָׂטִ֛ית תַּ֥חַת אִישֵׁ֖ךְ וְכִ֣י נִטְמֵ֑את
pairs.english: And you, if you have gone astray from your husband, and if you have become unclean,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אִ֥ישׁ בָּךְ֙ אֶת־שְׁכׇבְתּ֔וֹ מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֖י אִישֵֽׁךְ׃
pairs.english: and a man has put his lying in you aside from your husband, [then chinaki ("be strangled")].

pairs.hebrew: וְהִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ הַכֹּהֵ֥ן אֶֽת־הָאִשָּׁה֮ בִּשְׁבֻעַ֣ת הָאָלָה֒ וְאָמַ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ לָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה
pairs.english: Then the Cohein shall beswear the woman with the oath of the curse, and the Cohein shall say to the woman:

pairs.hebrew: יִתֵּ֨ן יְהֹוָ֥ה אוֹתָ֛ךְ לְאָלָ֥ה וְלִשְׁבֻעָ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ עַמֵּ֑ךְ
pairs.english: May the L-rd render you a curse [(that all curse by you, viz.: "May it happen to you as happened to that woman, etc.")] and an oath [(that all swear by you, viz.: "If I have not spoken truly may it happen to me, etc.")] in the midst of your people

pairs.hebrew: בְּתֵ֨ת יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶת־יְרֵכֵךְ֙ נֹפֶ֔לֶת וְאֶת־בִּטְנֵ֖ךְ צָבָֽה׃
pairs.english: by the L-rd's causing your thigh to fall and your belly to swell [("thigh" precedes "belly" in the curse as it did in the act)].

pairs.hebrew: וּ֠בָ֠אוּ הַמַּ֨יִם הַמְאָרְרִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ בְּֽמֵעַ֔יִךְ לַצְבּ֥וֹת בֶּ֖טֶן וְלַנְפִּ֣ל יָרֵ֑ךְ
pairs.english: And these blighting waters shall enter your innards to swell the belly and to make fall the thigh [of the adulterer (as well)],

and the woman shall say: Amen, Amen [(Amen to the curse, Amen to the oath; Amen, in respect to this man, Amen in respect to any other man; Amen, that I did not go astray while betrothed, married, awaiting levirate marriage, or having been taken in levirate marriage.)]
Then the Cohein shall write these curses into a scroll
and erase into the bitter waters.
And when he makes the woman drink the bitter, blighting waters,

then the blighting waters shall enter into [all of] her, [(and not only into "thigh and belly," those being singled out because they "initiated" the transgression)] for bitterness [i.e., to be sore and bitter to her].

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַ֤ח הַכֹּהֵן֙ מִיַּ֣ד הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֵ֖ת מִנְחַ֣ת הַקְּנָאֹ֑ת
pairs.english: And the Cohein shall take from the hand of the woman the meal-offering of rancors,
and he shall wave the meal-offering before the L-rd [back and forth and up and down. And she waves it with him, her hand above that of the Cohein],
and he shall present it at the [south-west corner of the] altar [before taking the fistful, as with the other meal-offerings].

pairs.hebrew: וְקָמַ֨ץ הַכֹּהֵ֤ן מִן־הַמִּנְחָה֙ אֶת־אַזְכָּ֣רָתָ֔הּ וְהִקְטִ֖יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה
pairs.english: And the Cohein shall take a fistful from the meal-offering as its "remembrance" [see Leviticus 2:2], and he shall smoke it on the altar,
and then he shall make the woman drink the water.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִשְׁקָ֣הּ אֶת־הַמַּ֗יִם וְהָיְתָ֣ה אִֽם־נִטְמְאָה֮ וַתִּמְעֹ֣ל מַ֣עַל בְּאִישָׁהּ֒
pairs.english: And he shall make her drink the water [(to include an instance where she refused to drink after the scroll was blotted out; in which instance she is forcibly made to drink it — unless she admitted having been adulterous.)] And it shall be, if she had been defiled and had been faithless to her husband,

pairs.hebrew: וּבָ֨אוּ בָ֜הּ הַמַּ֤יִם הַמְאָֽרְרִים֙ לְמָרִ֔ים וְצָבְתָ֣ה בִטְנָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה יְרֵכָ֑הּ
pairs.english: then the blighting waters will enter her for bitterness, and her belly will swell and her thigh will fall. [Though in the curses (21) "thigh" precedes "belly," in operation, the waters first enter the belly and then the thigh.]
And the woman will be a curse in the midst of her people.
And if the woman had not been defiled [in this concealment] and she be clean [of any other act],

then she shall be absolved [of the blighting waters] and [what is more,] she will sow seed. [If she had difficult labors, she will have easy ones; if she had borne swarthy children, she will bear fair ones.]
This is the law of the rancors

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּשְׂטֶ֥ה אִשָּׁ֛ה תַּ֥חַת אִישָׁ֖הּ וְנִטְמָֽאָה׃
pairs.english: for a woman who goes astray under her husband and is defiled.

pairs.hebrew: א֣וֹ אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תַּעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֛יו ר֥וּחַ קִנְאָ֖ה וְקִנֵּ֣א אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: If there pass over a man a spirit of rancor, then he shall warn his wife,
and he shall stand his wife before the L-rd

pairs.hebrew: וְעָ֤שָׂה לָהּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֵ֥ת כׇּל־הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
pairs.english: and the Cohein shall do with her all of this law.
And the man will be free of sin [i.e., of liability for her death by the waters],
and that woman shall bear her sin.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them:

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַפְלִא֙ לִנְדֹּר֙ נֶ֣דֶר נָזִ֔יר לְהַזִּ֖יר לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃
pairs.english: A man or a woman, if he utter a vow, the vow of a Nazirite [lit., "one who separates himself"] to separate himself [from wine] unto the L-rd [i.e., for the sake of Heaven], [(The rationale of the juxtaposition of verses — "All who witness a sotah (a woman suspected of infidelity) in her undoing should separate themselves from wine," wine inciting to licentiousness)],
From [new] wine and shechar [old (lit., "intoxicating") wine] he shall separate himself.

pairs.hebrew: חֹ֥מֶץ יַ֛יִן וְחֹ֥מֶץ שֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: Vinegar of wine and vinegar of shechar he shall not drink;
and any steeping of grapes he shall not drink,
and grapes, wet or dry, he shall not eat.
All the days of his Naziritism,

pairs.hebrew: מִכֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה מִגֶּ֣פֶן הַיַּ֗יִן מֵחַרְצַנִּ֛ים וְעַד־זָ֖ג לֹ֥א יֹאכֵֽל׃
pairs.english: of all that is made from the grapevine, from the kernels to the husk, he shall not eat.

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־יְמֵי֙ נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔וֹ תַּ֖עַר לֹא־יַעֲבֹ֣ר עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ
pairs.english: All the days of the vow of his Naziritism a blade shall not pass over his head.

pairs.hebrew: עַד־מְלֹ֨את הַיָּמִ֜ם אֲשֶׁר־יַזִּ֤יר לַיהֹוָה֙ קָדֹ֣שׁ יִהְיֶ֔ה גַּדֵּ֥ל פֶּ֖רַע שְׂעַ֥ר רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃
pairs.english: Until the fulfillment of the days of his Naziritism to the L-rd, holy shall it [his hair] be [by his] letting grow long the growth [pera ("pera" is not less than thirty days)] of the hair of his head.
All the days of his Naziritism to the L-rd,
by a dead body he shall not come.

pairs.hebrew: לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֗וֹ לְאָחִיו֙ וּלְאַ֣חֹת֔וֹ לֹא־יִטַּמָּ֥א לָהֶ֖ם בְּמֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not make himself unclean for them in their death,
for the crown of his G-d is on his head.
All the days of his Naziritism,
holy is he to the L-rd [("holiness" of body — not making himself unclean for the dead)].

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יָמ֨וּת מֵ֤ת עָלָיו֙ בְּפֶ֣תַע פִּתְאֹ֔ם וְטִמֵּ֖א רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ
pairs.english: And if any man die on him [in the tent where he finds himself], of an instant, unexpectedly, and he make unclean the head of his Naziritism,

pairs.hebrew: וְגִלַּ֤ח רֹאשׁוֹ֙ בְּי֣וֹם טׇהֳרָת֔וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י יְגַלְּחֶֽנּוּ׃
pairs.english: then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing [i.e., sprinkling (of the waters of the red heifer, 19:17)]; on the seventh day shall he shave it.

pairs.hebrew: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֗י יָבִא֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֔ים א֥וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֑ה
pairs.english: And on the eighth day [i.e., from the eighth day on], he shall bring two turtle-doves or two young pigeons
to the Cohein, to the door of the tent of meeting.

pairs.hebrew: וְעָשָׂ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶחָ֤ד לְחַטָּאת֙ וְאֶחָ֣ד לְעֹלָ֔ה
pairs.english: And the Cohein shall offer one as a sin-offering and one as a burnt-offering,
and he shall atone for him for having sinned through the (dead) body,
and he shall hallow his head on that day [i.e., He shall begin again the count of his Naziritism].
And he shall consecrate [anew] to the L-rd the days of his Naziritism,
and he shall bring a lamb of the first year as a guilt-offering,

pairs.hebrew: וְהַיָּמִ֤ים הָרִאשֹׁנִים֙ יִפְּל֔וּ כִּ֥י טָמֵ֖א נִזְרֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and the first days shall fall off [from the count] because he made unclean his Naziritism.
And this is the law of the Nazirite.

pairs.hebrew: בְּי֗וֹם מְלֹאת֙ יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔וֹ יָבִ֣יא אֹת֔וֹ אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: On the day of the fulfillment of the days of his Naziritism, he shall bring himself to the door of the tent of meeting.

pairs.hebrew: וְהִקְרִ֣יב אֶת־קׇרְבָּנ֣וֹ לַיהֹוָ֡ה כֶּ֩בֶשׂ֩ בֶּן־שְׁנָת֨וֹ תָמִ֤ים אֶחָד֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה
pairs.english: And he shall offer up his sacrifice to the L-rd: one lamb of the first year without blemish as a burnt-offering,
and one ewe-lamb of the first year without blemish as a sin-offering,
and one ram without blemish as a peace-offering.

pairs.hebrew: וְסַ֣ל מַצּ֗וֹת סֹ֤לֶת חַלֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן
pairs.english: And a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, [ten] cakes [of unleavened bread] mixed with oil,
and [ten] wafers of unleavened bread smeared with oil,
and their [the burnt-offering's and the peace-offering's] meal-offering and their drink-offerings.
And the Cohein shall present (them) before the L-rd,
and he shall offer his sin-offering and his burnt-offering.

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶת־הָאַ֜יִל יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה זֶ֤בַח שְׁלָמִים֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה עַ֖ל סַ֣ל הַמַּצּ֑וֹת
pairs.english: And the ram shall he offer as a sacrifice of peace-offerings to the L-rd for the basket of unleavened bread [i.e., he shall slaughter the peace-offerings with the intent of consecrating the bread],
and the Cohein shall offer its [the ram's] meal-offering and its drink-offering.

pairs.hebrew: וְגִלַּ֣ח הַנָּזִ֗יר פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the Nazirite shall shave — [outside the azarah, after the slaughtering of the peace-offerings, which took place] at the door of the tent of meeting — the head of his Naziritism.

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַ֗ח אֶת־שְׂעַר֙ רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֔וֹ וְנָתַן֙ עַל־הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁר־תַּ֖חַת זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃
pairs.english: And he shall take the hair of the head of his Naziritism, and he shall place it on the fire under the sacrifice of the peace-offerings [i.e., under the cauldron (in the azarah) in which they are cooked (the Cohein being required to take the shoulder after it has been cooked and wave it before the L-rd)].

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַ֨ח הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־הַזְּרֹ֣עַ בְּשֵׁלָה֮ מִן־הָאַ֒יִל֒ וְֽחַלַּ֨ת מַצָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ מִן־הַסַּ֔ל וּרְקִ֥יק מַצָּ֖ה אֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: And the Cohein shall take the cooked shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַן֙ עַל־כַּפֵּ֣י הַנָּזִ֔יר אַחַ֖ר הִֽתְגַּלְּח֥וֹ אֶת־נִזְרֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and he shall place them on the palms of the Nazirite after his shaving of (the head of) his Naziritism.
And the Cohein shall wave them, a waving before the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: קֹ֤דֶשׁ הוּא֙ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן עַ֚ל חֲזֵ֣ה הַתְּנוּפָ֔ה וְעַ֖ל שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֑ה
pairs.english: It [(the cake, the wafer, and the shoulder)] is holy [i.e., terumah] to the Cohein, in addition to the breast of waving and the thigh of lifting, [which revert to the Cohein from all peace-offerings],
and thereafter the Nazirite may drink wine.

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֣את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַנָּזִיר֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדֹּר֒ קׇרְבָּנ֤וֹ לַֽיהֹוָה֙ עַל־נִזְר֔וֹ מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־תַּשִּׂ֣יג יָד֑וֹ
pairs.english: This is the law of the Nazirite who shall vow his offering to the L-rd for his Naziritism, aside from what his hand attains [i.e., if he vows more than the prescribed number of offerings, he must bring them.]

pairs.hebrew: כְּפִ֤י נִדְרוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדֹּ֔ר כֵּ֣ן יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה עַ֖ל תּוֹרַ֥ת נִזְרֽוֹ׃ {פ}
pairs.english: According to the vow that he vows, thus shall he do above [(but not below)] the law of his Naziriteship [i.e., the prescribed number of offerings].
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying:
Thus shall you bless the children of Israel, saying [with full intent and with a whole heart] unto them, [so that they all hear]:
The L-rd bless you [that your possessions increase]
and keep you [that you not be despoiled of your possessions].
The L-rd cause His countenance to shine upon you
and grant you favor.
The L-rd lift His countenance [i.e., quell His anger] unto you
and grant you peace.
And they shall place My name [the Tetragrammaton] on the children of Israel,
and I will bless them [i.e., I will "concur" in their blessing.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֡י בְּיוֹם֩ כַּלּ֨וֹת מֹשֶׁ֜ה לְהָקִ֣ים אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֗ן
pairs.english: And it was, on the day that Moses had finished (kalloth) setting up the mishkan

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּמְשַׁ֨ח אֹת֜וֹ וַיְקַדֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֑יו וַיִּמְשָׁחֵ֖ם וַיְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֹתָֽם׃
pairs.english: and had anointed it and consecrated it and all of its vessels, and (he had set up) the altar and all of its vessels, and had anointed them and consecrated them, [(kalloth): On the day of the setting up of the mishkan, Israel was like a bride (kallah) entering the bridal canopy. ("that Moses had finished"): Although Betzalel and other craftsmen had made the mishkan, it is attributed to Moses for having given heart and soul to see to it that the last detail was executed exactly as the L-rd had revealed it to him on Mount Sinai. ("on the day that Moses had finished setting up"): All of the seven days of the investiture, Moses would assemble and dismantle the mishkan, and it was on the eighth day that he assembled it and did not dismantle it. ("On the day that Moses had finished setting up the mishkan"): It was Rosh Chodesh Nissan. On the second (of Nissan) the red heifer was burned; on the third, the first sprinkling (of the cleansing waters) took place, and on the seventh day (the Levites) shaved (see 8:6)],

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּקְרִ֙יבוּ֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: That the chiefs of Israel, the heads of their fathers' house,

pairs.hebrew: הֵ֚ם נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הַמַּטֹּ֔ת הֵ֥ם הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עַל־הַפְּקֻדִֽים׃
pairs.english: the chiefs of the tribes, [who were their overseers in Egypt, and who were smitten because of them (Exodus 5:14)], they who stood [with Moses and Aaron] over the ones who were numbered [(1:4)], presented (their offerings).
And they brought their offerings before the L-rd,

pairs.hebrew: שֵׁשׁ־עֶגְלֹ֥ת צָב֙ וּשְׁנֵ֣י עָשָׂ֣ר בָּקָ֔ר עֲגָלָ֛ה עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י הַנְּשִׂאִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וֹר לְאֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for every two chiefs, and an ox for each,
and they presented them before the mishkan [(Moses did not take it from their hands until the L-rd told him to do so)].
And the L-rd said
to Moses, saying:

pairs.hebrew: קַ֚ח מֵֽאִתָּ֔ם וְהָי֕וּ לַעֲבֹ֕ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: Take it from them, and they shall be for the service of the tent of meeting,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֥י עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: and give them to the Levites, each according to his service.
And Moses took the wagons and the oxen
and he gave them to the Levites.

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת ׀ שְׁתֵּ֣י הָעֲגָל֗וֹת וְאֵת֙ אַרְבַּ֣עַת הַבָּקָ֔ר נָתַ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י גֵרְשׁ֑וֹן
pairs.english: Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon,
according to their service, [which was lighter than that of Merari, who carried the beams, and the pillars, and the sockets].

pairs.hebrew: וְאֵ֣ת ׀ אַרְבַּ֣ע הָעֲגָלֹ֗ת וְאֵת֙ שְׁמֹנַ֣ת הַבָּקָ֔ר נָתַ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֑י
pairs.english: And four wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari,

pairs.hebrew: כְּפִי֙ עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔ם בְּיַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
pairs.english: according to their service, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the Cohein.
And to the sons of Kehath he gave none,
for the burden of the holy things [the ark, the table, etc.] was theirs, [wherefore] they were to be borne upon the shoulder.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּקְרִ֣יבוּ הַנְּשִׂאִ֗ים אֵ֚ת חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּי֖וֹם הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: And the chiefs presented the inauguration (offerings) of the altar on the day it was anointed [(After they had donated the wagons and the oxen for bearing the wagons, their hearts moved them to donate offerings for the inauguration of the altar)],
and the chiefs presented their offerings before the altar. [Moses did not take them from their hands until the L-rd told him to do so.]
And the L-rd said to Moses:

pairs.hebrew: נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד לַיּ֗וֹם נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לַיּ֔וֹם יַקְרִ֙יבוּ֙ אֶת־קׇרְבָּנָ֔ם לַחֲנֻכַּ֖ת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: Each chief on his day, each chief on his day, shall present his offerings for the inauguration of the altar. [And Moses did not know whether to follow the order of birth or the order of traveling (see section 2), until the L-rd told him to follow the order of traveling.]
And the one who presented his offering on the first day was
Nachshon ben Aminadav of the tribe of Judah.

pairs.hebrew: וְקׇרְבָּנ֞וֹ קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּמֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָהּ֒
pairs.english: And his offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels,

pairs.hebrew: מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: one silver bowl of seventy shekels in the shekel of the sanctuary,

pairs.hebrew: שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם ׀ מְלֵאִ֗ים סֹ֛לֶת בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לְמִנְחָֽה׃
pairs.english: both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a [donative] meal-offering.
One spoon, [weighing] ten gold [shekels],
full of incense [This is the only instance of incense offered by an individual, and on the outer altar — a "one-time ruling"]
One young bullock ["the choice of the herd"], one ram,
one lamb of the first year for a burnt-offering.
One he-goat
for a sin-offering [to atone for (possible) defilement by a "grave in the depths" and for suspicion of uncleanliness].
And for the sacrifice of the peace-offerings: two oxen,

pairs.hebrew: אֵילִ֤ם חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַתּוּדִ֣ים חֲמִשָּׁ֔ה כְּבָשִׂ֥ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֖ה חֲמִשָּׁ֑ה
pairs.english: five rams, five he-goats, five lambs of the first year —
this is the [(personal, not tribal)] offering of Nachshon ben Aminadav.
On the second day,
Nethanel ben Tzuar, the chief of Yissachar, presented.

pairs.hebrew: הִקְרִ֨ב אֶת־קׇרְבָּנ֜וֹ קַֽעֲרַת־כֶּ֣סֶף אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּמֵאָה֮ מִשְׁקָלָהּ֒
pairs.english: He presented his offering: one silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels,

pairs.hebrew: מִזְרָ֤ק אֶחָד֙ כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: one silver bowl of seventy shekels in the shekel of the sanctuary,

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֣את ׀ חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ בְּיוֹם֙ הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֔וֹ מֵאֵ֖ת נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: This is the (accounting of the) inauguration of the altar on the day that it was anointed by the chiefs of Israel. [(On the day that it was anointed they presented their offerings)]:

pairs.hebrew: קַעֲרֹ֨ת כֶּ֜סֶף שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֗ה מִֽזְרְקֵי־כֶ֙סֶף֙ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ר כַּפּ֥וֹת זָהָ֖ב שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵֽה׃
pairs.english: silver dishes, twelve; silver bowls, twelve; golden spoons, twelve.

pairs.hebrew: שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים וּמֵאָ֗ה הַקְּעָרָ֤ה הָֽאַחַת֙ כֶּ֔סֶף וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים הַמִּזְרָ֣ק הָאֶחָ֑ד
pairs.english: One hundred and thirty [shekels was the weight of] each silver dish; seventy [shekels was the weight of] each bowl.

pairs.hebrew: כֹּ֚ל כֶּ֣סֶף הַכֵּלִ֔ים אַלְפַּ֥יִם וְאַרְבַּע־מֵא֖וֹת בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: All the silver of the vessels — two thousand and four hundred shekels in the shekel of the sanctuary. [(The weights, individual and collective, "tallied" exactly.)]

pairs.hebrew: כַּפּ֨וֹת זָהָ֤ב שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵה֙ מְלֵאֹ֣ת קְטֹ֔רֶת עֲשָׂרָ֧ה עֲשָׂרָ֛ה הַכַּ֖ף בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: Golden spoons, twelve, full of incense, each spoon weighing ten [gold shekels] in the shekel of the sanctuary.
All the gold of the spoons — one hundred and twenty [shekels].

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־הַבָּקָ֨ר לָעֹלָ֜ה שְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר פָּרִ֗ים אֵילִ֤ם שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂר֙ כְּבָשִׂ֧ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֛ה שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר וּמִנְחָתָ֑ם
pairs.english: All the cattle for the burnt-offering: twelve bullocks, twelve rams, twelve lambs of the first year, and their meal-offering;
and twelve he-goats for a sin-offering.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹ֞ל בְּקַ֣ר ׀ זֶ֣בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֗ים עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וְאַרְבָּעָה֮ פָּרִים֒ אֵילִ֤ם שִׁשִּׁים֙ עַתֻּדִ֣ים שִׁשִּׁ֔ים כְּבָשִׂ֥ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֖ה שִׁשִּׁ֑ים
pairs.english: And all the cattle for the sacrifice of the peace-offerings: twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty he-goats, sixty lambs of the first year.

pairs.hebrew: זֹ֚את חֲנֻכַּ֣ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ אַחֲרֵ֖י הִמָּשַׁ֥ח אֹתֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: This is the (accounting of the) inauguration of the altar after it was anointed.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֮ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתּוֹ֒
pairs.english: And when Moses came to the tent of meeting to speak with Him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע אֶת־הַקּ֜וֹל מִדַּבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו מֵעַ֤ל הַכַּפֹּ֙רֶת֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־אֲרֹ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֔ת מִבֵּ֖ין שְׁנֵ֣י הַכְּרֻבִ֑ים
pairs.english: he heard the voice [(the same mighty voice which spoke with him at Sinai — which, notwithstanding, did not carry beyond the tent of meeting)] communing with itself above the kaporeth on the ark of Testimony between the two cherubs, [the voice traveling from heaven to between the two cherubs, and thence, to the tent of meeting],
and He spoke to him [to Moses (Aaron being excluded from this communication)].

[The L-rd, beholding Aaron's distress at his exclusion and that of his tribe from the inauguration of the altar (in contrast to the participation of the chiefs of all the other tribes) said to him: Your share (the kindling of the menorah) is greater than theirs.] And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Speak to Aaron and say to him:

pairs.hebrew: בְּהַעֲלֹֽתְךָ֙ אֶת־הַנֵּרֹ֔ת אֶל־מוּל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמְּנוֹרָ֔ה יָאִ֖ירוּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת הַנֵּרֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: When you kindle the lamps (of the menorah), towards the face [the central shaft] of the menorah shall the seven lamps light [i.e., shall their light (by manipulation of the wicks) be directed (so that people not say that He needs the menorah for its light)].
And Aaron did so.
He kindled its lamps towards the face of the menorah,
as the L-rd had commanded Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וְזֶ֨ה מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה הַמְּנֹרָה֙ מִקְשָׁ֣ה זָהָ֔ב עַד־יְרֵכָ֥הּ עַד־פִּרְחָ֖הּ מִקְשָׁ֣ה הִ֑וא
pairs.english: And this was the work of the menorah ["this," as pointed out by the L-rd to Moses, who had difficulty in visualizing it]: [It was made of one talent of] beaten gold, from its base [the thickest part] until its flower [its most delicate part] — of beaten work.

pairs.hebrew: כַּמַּרְאֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶרְאָ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: According to the sight that the L-rd had shown Moses, so did he make the menorah.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Take the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel [("Take them" with words, viz.: "Happy are you, who have merited being servants to the L-rd!")],
and cleanse them.

pairs.hebrew: וְכֹֽה־תַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְטַֽהֲרָ֔ם הַזֵּ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֵ֣י חַטָּ֑את
pairs.english: And thus shall you do to them to cleanse them: Sprinkle upon them the waters of purification [of the red heifer (for those among them who had become unclean by dead bodies)],

pairs.hebrew: וְהֶעֱבִ֤ירוּ תַ֙עַר֙ עַל־כׇּל־בְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְכִבְּס֥וּ בִגְדֵיהֶ֖ם וְהִטֶּהָֽרוּ׃
pairs.english: and have them pass a blade over all their flesh (i.e., have them shave it), and have them wash their clothes and be clean.

pairs.hebrew: וְלָֽקְחוּ֙ פַּ֣ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֔ר וּמִ֨נְחָת֔וֹ סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשָּׁ֑מֶן
pairs.english: And they shall take a young bullock, [this, the "burnt-offering" (12), (a communal offering in atonement for idolatry)], with its meal-offering, fine flour mixed with oil;

and a second young bullock shall you take for a sin-offering [("second"): Just as a burnt-offering is not eaten, so this sin-offering (as opposed to all other outer-altar sin-offerings) is not to be eaten — a hora'ath sha'ah ("one-time ruling")].
And you shall present the Levites before the tent of meeting,

and you shall assemble the entire congregation of the children of Israel. [Because the Levites are "given" (16) as an expiatory offering in place of them (the first-born of Israel), let them come and stand by their offerings and place their hand upon them (the Levites).]
And you shall present the Levites before the L-rd,
and the children of Israel shall place their hands on the Levites.

pairs.hebrew: וְהֵנִיף֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֤ם תְּנוּפָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And Aaron shall wave the Levites, a waving before the L-rd, [just as the guilt-offering of the leper required waving live (Leviticus 14:12)] from the children of Israel,

and they shall serve the service of the L-rd. [Three "wavings" are mentioned in this section. This first applies to the sons of Kehath, upon whom the service of the holy of holies devolved (i.e., the bearing of the ark, the table, etc.) — thus: "and they shall serve the service of the L-rd."]

pairs.hebrew: וְהַלְוִיִּם֙ יִסְמְכ֣וּ אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֔ם עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ הַפָּרִ֑ים
pairs.english: And the Levites shall place their hands upon the head of the bullocks,

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠עֲשֵׂ֠ה אֶת־הָאֶחָ֨ד חַטָּ֜את וְאֶת־הָאֶחָ֤ד עֹלָה֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־הַלְוִיִּֽם׃
pairs.english: and make the one a sin-offering, and the other, a burnt-offering to the L-rd to atone for the Levites.

pairs.hebrew: וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י בָנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And you shall stand the Levites before Aaron and before his sons,

and you shall wave them as a wave-offering to the L-rd. [This second waving, "to the L-rd," applies to the sons of Gershon, who bore the curtains and the hooks, which were visible in the holy of holies.]
And you shall separate the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel,
and the Levites shall be Mine.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד
pairs.english: And after that, the Levites shall come in to do the work of the tent of meeting,

and you shall cleanse them, and you shall wave them as a wave-offering. [This third waving applies to the sons of Merari (who carried the parts for the tent of meeting. Thus, "wave-offering" (unqualified by "before the L-rd" or "to the L-rd")].

pairs.hebrew: כִּי֩ נְתֻנִ֨ים נְתֻנִ֥ים הֵ֙מָּה֙ לִ֔י מִתּ֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: For given, given [(given for bearing and given for singing)] are they [the Levites] to Me from the midst of the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: תַּ֩חַת֩ פִּטְרַ֨ת כׇּל־רֶ֜חֶם בְּכ֥וֹר כֹּל֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָקַ֥חְתִּי אֹתָ֖ם לִֽי׃
pairs.english: In place of the opening of every womb, the first-born of all of the children of Israel, have I taken them unto Me.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י לִ֤י כׇל־בְּכוֹר֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה
pairs.english: For unto Me [by right] were all the first-born of the children of Israel, of man and beast;

pairs.hebrew: בְּי֗וֹם הַכֹּתִ֤י כׇל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם הִקְדַּ֥שְׁתִּי אֹתָ֖ם לִֽי׃
pairs.english: on the day that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt [and defended them from the plague], I sanctified them [and took them (as servants)] unto Me [ — until they went astray with the golden calf].
And [now] I have taken the Levites (who did not go astray with the golden calf)
in place of all the first-born of the children of Israel.

pairs.hebrew: וָאֶתְּנָ֨ה אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֜ם נְתֻנִ֣ים ׀ לְאַהֲרֹ֣ן וּלְבָנָ֗יו מִתּוֹךְ֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒
pairs.english: And I have given the Levites, given to Aaron and his sons from the midst of the children of Israel,

pairs.hebrew: לַעֲבֹ֞ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וּלְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: to perform the service of the children of Israel in the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the children of Israel,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֨א יִהְיֶ֜ה בִּבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נֶ֔גֶף בְּגֶ֥שֶׁת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
pairs.english: that there not be a plague among the children of Israel in the drawing near of the children of Israel to the sanctuary [i.e., if they had to draw near, they would die in doing so.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן וְכׇל־עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַלְוִיִּ֑ם
pairs.english: And Moses and Aaron and the entire congregation of the children of Israel did with the Levites

pairs.hebrew: כְּ֠כֹ֠ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ לַלְוִיִּ֔ם כֵּן־עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: in accordance with all that the L-rd had commanded Moses respecting the Levites; thus did the children of Israel do with them. [Moses presented them, Aaron waved them, and the Israelites placed their hands upon them.]
And the Levites were cleansed, and they washed their clothes,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֨נֶף אַהֲרֹ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: and Aaron waved them a waving before the L-rd,
and Aaron atoned for them to cleanse them.

pairs.hebrew: וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן בָּ֣אוּ הַלְוִיִּ֗ם לַעֲבֹ֤ד אֶת־עֲבֹֽדָתָם֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד לִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְלִפְנֵ֣י בָנָ֑יו
pairs.english: And after that the Levites came to perform their service in the tent of meeting before Aaron and before his sons.

pairs.hebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ צִוָּ֨ה יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה֙ עַל־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם כֵּ֖ן עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶֽם׃ {ס}
pairs.english: As the L-rd commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so did they do to them [(There was no demurral neither from the doers nor from the subjects.)]
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
This is what applies to the Levites ["Years" disqualify them (from service), and not blemishes.]

pairs.hebrew: מִבֶּן֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה יָבוֹא֙ לִצְבֹ֣א צָבָ֔א בַּעֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: From the age of twenty-five and up shall he come to enter into service to work in the tent of meeting. [He studies the service for five years and begins working at the age of thirty.]

pairs.hebrew: וּמִבֶּן֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה יָשׁ֖וּב מִצְּבָ֣א הָעֲבֹדָ֑ה
pairs.english: And from the age of fifty he shall return from the service of the work,
and he shall serve [in that capacity (carrying on the shoulder)] no more, [but he returns to closing the gates, singing, and loading wagons].

pairs.hebrew: וְשֵׁרֵ֨ת אֶת־אֶחָ֜יו בְּאֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣ר מִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת
pairs.english: And he shall serve with his brothers in the tent of meeting, to keep the charge [i.e., to encamp around the tent of meeting and to assemble and dismantle it in traveling.]

pairs.hebrew: וַעֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֣א יַעֲבֹ֑ד כָּ֛כָה תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לַלְוִיִּ֖ם בְּמִשְׁמְרֹתָֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: But service (as indicated above) shall he not perform. Thus shall you do with the Levites in their watches.
And the L-rd spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai

pairs.hebrew: בַּשָּׁנָ֨ה הַשֵּׁנִ֜ית לְצֵאתָ֨ם מֵאֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר׃
pairs.english: in the second year after their going out from the land of Egypt, in the first month (Nissan), saying: [(Bamidbar begins with the second month (1:1) — whence it is derived that "there is no before and after (i.e., strict chronological sequence) in the Torah." (It does not begin with this section for it is disparaging to Israel that all the forty years that they were in the desert they offered only this one Paschal sacrifice.)]
The children of Israel shall offer the Pesach
in its appointed time, [even on the Sabbath, even in a state of (communal) uncleanliness].

pairs.hebrew: בְּאַרְבָּעָ֣ה עָשָֽׂר־י֠וֹם בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֜ה בֵּ֧ין הָֽעַרְבַּ֛יִם תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּמֹעֲד֑וֹ
pairs.english: On the fourteenth day of this month, towards evening shall you offer it, in its appointed time.
According to all of its statutes [the mitzvoth relating directly to its body] and according to all its [attendant] ordinances shall you offer it.
And Moses spoke to the children of Israel
to offer the Pesach. [(He exhorted them prior to observance (having already promulgated it to them when he heard it from Sinai)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֶת־הַפֶּ֡סַח בָּרִאשׁ֡וֹן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י
pairs.english: And they offered the Pesach in the first (month) on the fourteenth day of the month, towards evening, in the desert of Sinai.

pairs.hebrew: כְּ֠כֹ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: According to all that the L-rd had commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel do.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֣י אֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֤וּ טְמֵאִים֙ לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֔ם
pairs.english: And there were men who were unclean by the body of a dead man,
and they could not offer the Pesach on that day,

pairs.hebrew: וַֽיִּקְרְב֞וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
pairs.english: and they drew near before Moses and Aaron on that day.

pairs.hebrew: וַ֠יֹּאמְר֠וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָהֵ֙מָּה֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֲנַ֥חְנוּ טְמֵאִ֖ים לְנֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֑ם
pairs.english: And those men said to him: We are unclean by the body of a dead man.

pairs.hebrew: לָ֣מָּה נִגָּרַ֗ע לְבִלְתִּ֨י הַקְרִ֜יב אֶת־קׇרְבַּ֤ן יְהֹוָה֙ בְּמֹ֣עֲד֔וֹ בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: Why should we be held back, not to offer the sacrifice of the L-rd in its appointed time, in the midst of the children of Israel?
And Moses said to them:
Stand, and I will hear what the L-rd will command concerning you.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:
Speak to the children of Israel, saying:

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ישׁ אִ֣ישׁ כִּי־יִהְיֶֽה־טָמֵ֣א ׀ לָנֶ֡פֶשׁ אוֹ֩ בְדֶ֨רֶךְ רְחֹקָ֜הׄ לָכֶ֗ם א֚וֹ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: A man, if he be unclean by a dead body, or on a distant way [(Not literally "distant"; it is sufficient that he should have been outside the threshold of the azarah all the time of slaughtering.)], of you or of your generations,
he shall (yet) offer the Pesach to the L-rd.

pairs.hebrew: בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֜י בְּאַרְבָּעָ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר י֛וֹם בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבַּ֖יִם יַעֲשׂ֣וּ אֹת֑וֹ
pairs.english: In the second month, on the fourteenth day, towards evening shall they offer it;
with matzoth and bitter herbs shall they eat it.
They shall not leave over of it until the morning,
and a bone shall they not break in it;
according to all the statute of the Pesach shall they offer it.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁר־ה֨וּא טָה֜וֹר וּבְדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא־הָיָ֗ה וְחָדַל֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔סַח
pairs.english: And the man who is clean and was not on the way and who failed to offer the Pesach,
that soul shall be cut off from his people;

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ קׇרְבַּ֣ן יְהֹוָ֗ה לֹ֤א הִקְרִיב֙ בְּמֹ֣עֲד֔וֹ חֶטְא֥וֹ יִשָּׂ֖א הָאִ֥ישׁ הַהֽוּא׃
pairs.english: for the sacrifice of the L-rd he did not offer in its appointed time. That man shall bear his sin.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־יָג֨וּר אִתְּכֶ֜ם גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֤שָֽׂה פֶ֙סַח֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה
pairs.english: And if there live a proselyte among you, and he would offer a Pesach to the L-rd,
then according to the statute of the Pesach and according to its ordinance, thus shall he do.

pairs.hebrew: חֻקָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְלַגֵּ֖ר וּלְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ׃ {ס}
pairs.english: One statute shall there be for you, both for the proselyte and for the native of the land.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְיוֹם֙ הָקִ֣ים אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן כִּסָּ֤ה הֶֽעָנָן֙ אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לְאֹ֖הֶל הָעֵדֻ֑ת
pairs.english: And on the day that the mishkan was erected, the cloud covered the mishkan [which had been made] as a tent for the [tablets of the] Testimony.
And in the evening there would be on the mishkan a semblance of fire until morning.
So was it always: the cloud covered it,
and a semblance of fire at night.

pairs.hebrew: וּלְפִ֞י הֵעָל֤וֹת הֶֽעָנָן֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָאֹ֔הֶל וְאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן יִסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
pairs.english: And when the cloud departed from over the tent, the children of Israel would travel.

pairs.hebrew: וּבִמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁכׇּן־שָׁם֙ הֶֽעָנָ֔ן שָׁ֥ם יַחֲנ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: And in the place where the cloud rested, the children of Israel encamped.

By word of the L-rd the children of Israel traveled [The cloud would fold itself up like a beam over the (encampment of) the children of Judah (by word of the L-rd), and did not start moving until Moses said: "Stand, O L-rd!" (see 10:35)],

and by word of the L-rd they encamped. [The cloud would ascend as a pillar over the children of Judah and would not spread out (over the mishkan) until Moses said: "Rest, O L-rd, etc." (see 10:36). Thus (23): "By word of the L-rd, at the hand of Moses."]

pairs.hebrew: כׇּל־יְמֵ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁכֹּ֧ן הֶעָנָ֛ן עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יַחֲנֽוּ׃
pairs.english: All the days that the cloud abode over the mishkan, they camped.
And when the cloud lingered over the mishkan many days,

pairs.hebrew: וְשָׁמְר֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת יְהֹוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יִסָּֽעוּ׃
pairs.english: the children of Israel kept the charge of the L-rd and did not travel.

pairs.hebrew: וְיֵ֞שׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֧ה הֶֽעָנָ֛ן יָמִ֥ים מִסְפָּ֖ר עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן
pairs.english: And at times the cloud remained over the mishkan but a few days.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־פִּ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְעַל־פִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה יִסָּֽעוּ׃
pairs.english: By word of the L-rd they encamped, and by word of the L-rd they traveled.

pairs.hebrew: וְיֵ֞שׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיֶ֤ה הֶֽעָנָן֙ מֵעֶ֣רֶב עַד־בֹּ֔קֶר וְנַעֲלָ֧ה הֶֽעָנָ֛ן בַּבֹּ֖קֶר וְנָסָ֑עוּ
pairs.english: And at times the cloud remained from evening until morning, and when the cloud departed in the morning, they traveled.

pairs.hebrew: א֚וֹ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה וְנַעֲלָ֥ה הֶעָנָ֖ן וְנָסָֽעוּ׃
pairs.english: Or a day or a night — when the cloud departed, they traveled.

pairs.hebrew: אֽוֹ־יֹמַ֜יִם אוֹ־חֹ֣דֶשׁ אוֹ־יָמִ֗ים בְּהַאֲרִ֨יךְ הֶעָנָ֤ן עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן֙ לִשְׁכֹּ֣ן עָלָ֔יו יַחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְלֹ֣א יִסָּ֑עוּ
pairs.english: Or two days, or a month, or a year — when the cloud lingered over the mishkan, abiding upon it, the children of Israel remained encamped and did not travel;
and when it departed, they traveled.

pairs.hebrew: עַל־פִּ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ יַחֲנ֔וּ וְעַל־פִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה יִסָּ֑עוּ
pairs.english: By word of the L-rd they encamped, and by word of the L-rd they traveled.

pairs.hebrew: אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֤רֶת יְהֹוָה֙ שָׁמָ֔רוּ עַל־פִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ {פ}
pairs.english: The charge of the L-rd they kept — by word of the L-rd, at the hand of Moses.
And the L-rd spoke
to Moses, saying:

pairs.hebrew: עֲשֵׂ֣ה לְךָ֗ שְׁתֵּי֙ חֲצֽוֹצְרֹ֣ת כֶּ֔סֶף מִקְשָׁ֖ה תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: Make for yourself [i.e., from what is yours] two trumpets of silver; beaten work (from a block of silver) shall you make them.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָי֤וּ לְךָ֙ לְמִקְרָ֣א הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וּלְמַסַּ֖ע אֶת־הַֽמַּחֲנֽוֹת׃
pairs.english: And they shall be for you for convoking the congregation [the Sanhedrin and the rest of the people] and for the [signaling of the] traveling of the camps.
And when they [the Cohanim] blow [tekiah] with [both of] them,

pairs.hebrew: וְנֽוֹעֲד֤וּ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ כׇּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
pairs.english: then all the congregation shall gather unto you, to the door of the tent of meeting.
And if they blow with one,

pairs.hebrew: וְנוֹעֲד֤וּ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ הַנְּשִׂיאִ֔ים רָאשֵׁ֖י אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: there shall gather unto you [at the door of the tent of meeting], the chiefs, the heads of the thousands of Israel.
And when you blow a teruah (tremolo), [in sum: tekiah, teruah, tekiah]
then there shall travel the eastern encampments.

pairs.hebrew: וּתְקַעְתֶּ֤ם תְּרוּעָה֙ שֵׁנִ֔ית וְנָֽסְעוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנ֔וֹת הַחֹנִ֖ים תֵּימָ֑נָה
pairs.english: And when you blow a second teruah then there shall travel the southern encampments;
a teruah shall they blow for their travels.
And when the assembly is to be gathered you shall blow a tekiah (an extended blast),

but not a teruah. [In sum: convoking of the congregation, with two trumpets; convoking of the chiefs, with one. In both instances, no teruah. Traveling of the camps, with two trumpets, teruah and tekiah.]
And the sons of Aaron the Cohanim shall blow on the trumpets [for these convocations and travels],
and they shall be to you for a statute forever throughout your generations.

pairs.hebrew: וְכִֽי־תָבֹ֨אוּ מִלְחָמָ֜ה בְּאַרְצְכֶ֗ם עַל־הַצַּר֙ הַצֹּרֵ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֔ם
pairs.english: And when you go to war in your land against the oppressor who oppresses you,
then you shall sound the trumpets

pairs.hebrew: וְנִזְכַּרְתֶּ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְנוֹשַׁעְתֶּ֖ם מֵאֹיְבֵיכֶֽם׃
pairs.english: and you will be remembered before the L-rd your G-d, and you will be saved from your enemies.

pairs.hebrew: וּבְי֨וֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶ֥ם וּֽבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֮ וּבְרָאשֵׁ֣י חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם֒ וּתְקַעְתֶּ֣ם בַּחֲצֹֽצְרֹ֗ת עַ֚ל עֹלֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַ֖ל זִבְחֵ֣י שַׁלְמֵיכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And on the day of your rejoicing and on your appointed times, and on your new moons, you shall sound the trumpets [( — whence is derived "shofaroth" (on Rosh Hashanah)] over your [communal] burnt-offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings.

pairs.hebrew: וְהָי֨וּ לָכֶ֤ם לְזִכָּרוֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲנִ֖י יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: And they shall be to you for a remembrance (zikkaron) [( — whence is derived "zichronoth")] before your G-d. I am the L-rd your G-d [( — whence is derived "malchuyoth" (melech = king)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֧ה הַשֵּׁנִ֛ית בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֖י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים בַּחֹ֑דֶשׁ
pairs.english: And it was, in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month,
that the cloud departed from over the mishkan of the Testimony [(Israel was in Chorev, then, twelve months less ten days.)]
And Israel embarked on their travels from the desert of Sinai [in the order of their standards, as prescribed],
and the cloud came to rest in the desert of Paran [in Kivroth Hata'avah (12:34)].
They traveled for the first time
by word of the L-rd, at the hand of Moses.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסַּ֞ע דֶּ֣גֶל מַחֲנֵ֧ה בְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֛ה בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֖ה לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: The standard of the camp of the children of Yehudah traveled first, according to their hosts.
And over his host, Nachshon ben Aminadav.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Yissachar,
Nethanel ben Tzuar.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Zevulun,
Eliyav ben Cheilon.
And when the mishkan was taken down,

pairs.hebrew: וְנָסְע֤וּ בְנֵֽי־גֵרְשׁוֹן֙ וּבְנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
pairs.english: there set forth the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, the bearers of the mishkan. [When the standard of Yehudah set forth, Aaron and his sons entered and removed the parocheth and covered the ark with it. Then the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari dismantled the mishkan and loaded it in wagons. The ark and holy vessels to be borne by the children of Kehath stood covered and readied on staves until the standard of the camp of Reuven set forth, whereupon (21): "And the Kehathim set forth."]
And the standard of the camp of Reuven set forth according to their hosts;
and over his host, Elitzur ben Shedeur.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Shimon,
Shelumiel ben Tzurishadai.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Gad,
Elyasaf ben De'uel.
And the Kehathim set forth, the bearers of the holy things,

and they [the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari (when they saw the signal for encamping on the standard of the camp of Yehudah)], set up the mishkan [so that it was ready to receive the ark, the table, the menorah, and the altars], by the time they [the sons of Kehath (who were traveling two standards behind)] arrived.
And the standard of the children of Ephraim set forth according to their hosts;
and over his host, Elishama ben Amihud.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Menasheh,
Gamliel ben Pedatzur.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Binyamin,
Avidan ben Gidoni.

pairs.hebrew: וְנָסַ֗ע דֶּ֚גֶל מַחֲנֵ֣ה בְנֵי־דָ֔ן מְאַסֵּ֥ף לְכׇל־הַֽמַּחֲנֹ֖ת לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם
pairs.english: And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan set forth, the rearward of all the camps, according to their hosts;
and over his host, Achiezer ben Amishadai.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Asher,
Pagiel ben Achran.
And over the host of the tribe of the children of Naftali,
Achira ben Einan.
This is the traveling order of the children of Israel according to their hosts.
And [on that day (11)] they set forth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה לְ֠חֹבָ֠ב בֶּן־רְעוּאֵ֣ל הַמִּדְיָנִי֮ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁה֒
pairs.english: And Moses said to Chovav [Yithro] the son of Reuel the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses:

pairs.hebrew: נֹסְעִ֣ים ׀ אֲנַ֗חְנוּ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה אֹת֖וֹ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם
pairs.english: We are journeying to the place of which the L-rd said: It will I give to you [(Within three days we will enter the land)].

pairs.hebrew: לְכָ֤ה אִתָּ֙נוּ֙ וְהֵטַ֣בְנוּ לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־יְהֹוָ֥ה דִּבֶּר־ט֖וֹב עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
pairs.english: Come with us and we will do good with you, for the L-rd has spoken (the doing of) good for Israel.
And he said to him: I will not go;
but to my land, [for the sake of my possessions] and to my kindred, [for the sake of my family], I will go.
And he said: I pray you, do not leave us, [so that it not be said that you became a proselyte only in expectation of a portion in the land, which, seeing not to be forthcoming, you abandoned us.]

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֣י ׀ עַל־כֵּ֣ן יָדַ֗עְתָּ חֲנֹתֵ֙נוּ֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְהָיִ֥יתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְעֵינָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: [Indeed, it becomes you to remain with us] inasmuch as you have known our camping in the desert [and have seen the miracles and wonders wrought for us], and you have been "eyes" for us.
And it shall be, if you go with us,

pairs.hebrew: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ הַטּ֣וֹב הַה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵיטִ֧יב יְהֹוָ֛ה עִמָּ֖נוּ וְהֵטַ֥בְנוּ לָֽךְ׃
pairs.english: that good which the L-rd will accord to us, we shall accord to you. [(The children of Yithro were given the choicest land of Jericho as a holding until it reverted to the tribe of Binyamin.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵהַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה דֶּ֖רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים
pairs.english: And they traveled from the mountain of the L-rd, a journey of three days. [They traveled a three-days distance in one day, the Holy One Blessed be He desiring to bring them immediately into the land.]

pairs.hebrew: וַאֲר֨וֹן בְּרִית־יְהֹוָ֜ה נֹסֵ֣עַ לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים לָת֥וּר לָהֶ֖ם מְנוּחָֽה׃
pairs.english: And the ark of the covenant of the L-rd [the ark with the broken tablets, which went out with them to war)] preceded them, a distance of three days, to look out a resting place for them.
And the cloud of the L-rd was above them by day
when they set forth from the encampment.

[There are signs (inverted nuns) before (this verse) and after (the next verse) to indicate that this is not where these verses actually belong; they were inserted here to create a hiatus between one misfortune and another (see Shabbath 116a)] and it was, when the ark traveled that Moses said:
"Stand [and wait for us (the ark preceding them a three-days distance)], O L-rd, and let Your foes [Your massed foes] be scattered,
and let Your haters [the enemies of Israel (those in pursuit)] flee before You."
And when it came to rest, he said:
"Rest, O L-rd, upon the [two] ten thousands [and two] thousands of Israel," [the Shechinah not resting in Israel upon fewer than twenty-two thousand.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמִתְאֹ֣נְנִ֔ים רַ֖ע בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And the people, [the wicked ones,] were as seekers of a pretext [to forsake Him], that was evil in the ears of the L-rd [i.e., that would antagonize Him when it reached His ears and would provoke Him. They said: "Woe unto us — how this three-days journey has wearied us!"]
And the L-rd heard and His wrath was kindled [(He said:) I did this for your own good, so that you would enter the land immediately! (see 10:33)],

pairs.hebrew: וַתִּבְעַר־בָּם֙ אֵ֣שׁ יְהֹוָ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אכַל בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
pairs.english: and the fire of the L-rd burned in them, and it devoured in the "end" of the camp [i.e., the lowest among them, the eirav rav (the mixed multitude)].
And the people cried out to Moses [to intercede for them],
and Moses prayed to the L-rd,
and the fire sank [in its place, into the earth. (Had it retreated, it would have consumed that area.)]
And he called the name of that place "Taveirah" (conflagration),
for the fire of the L-rd burned in them.
And the rabble that was among them [the mixed multitude that had gathered unto them in Egypt] lusted lust,
and the children of Israel also wept again [with them],
and they said: "Who shall give us flesh to eat!" [(They had flesh [see Exodus 12:38 and Numbers 32:1] — they were only seeking a pretext)].
We remember the fish that we would eat in Egypt, free [of mitzvoth],

pairs.hebrew: אֵ֣ת הַקִּשֻּׁאִ֗ים וְאֵת֙ הָֽאֲבַטִּחִ֔ים וְאֶת־הֶחָצִ֥יר וְאֶת־הַבְּצָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־הַשּׁוּמִֽים׃
pairs.english: the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic. [The (flavor of the) manna would change into any (flavor they desired) except these, for they are harmful to nursing women.]
And now, our souls are dry; there is nothing.
Only to the manna is our eyes [Manna in the morning; manna in the evening!]
[What follows is an "interjection" by the Holy One Blessed be He, viz.: See what My children are railing against!] The manna was [round] like coriander seed,
and it looked like crystal.
The people would stroll out and gather it [effortlessly],

pairs.hebrew: וְטָחֲנ֣וּ בָרֵחַ֗יִם א֤וֹ דָכוּ֙ בַּמְּדֹכָ֔ה וּבִשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּפָּר֔וּר וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ עֻג֑וֹת
pairs.english: and they would grind it in a mill, or beat it in a mortar, or cook it in a pot [i.e., they could make it taste as if it had been ground in a mill, etc.], and they made cakes of it;
and its taste was like the "sap" of oil.
And when the dew descended upon the camp at night,
the manna descended upon it.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־הָעָ֗ם בֹּכֶה֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו אִ֖ישׁ לְפֶ֣תַח אׇהֳל֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Moses heard the people weeping by its families, [who gathered together to air their plaints], each at the door of his tent.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהֹוָה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וּבְעֵינֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה רָֽע׃
pairs.english: And the L-rd was extremely wroth, and in the eyes of Moses it was evil.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־יְהֹוָ֗ה לָמָ֤ה הֲרֵעֹ֙תָ֙ לְעַבְדֶּ֔ךָ
pairs.english: And Moses said to the L-rd: Why have You done evil to Your servant,

pairs.hebrew: וְלָ֛מָּה לֹא־מָצָ֥תִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ לָשׂ֗וּם אֶת־מַשָּׂ֛א כׇּל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה עָלָֽי׃
pairs.english: and why have I not found favor in Your eyes, to place the burden of all this people upon me!

pairs.hebrew: הֶאָנֹכִ֣י הָרִ֗יתִי אֵ֚ת כׇּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אִם־אָנֹכִ֖י יְלִדְתִּ֑יהוּ
pairs.english: Did I conceive all this people? Did I beget them,

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֨ר אֵלַ֜י שָׂאֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקֶ֗ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשָּׂ֤א הָאֹמֵן֙ אֶת־הַיֹּנֵ֔ק
pairs.english: that You say to me: Bear them in your bosom, as a nurse bears a nursling,
to the land which You promised to their fathers? [see Exodus 32:34 and 6:13].

pairs.hebrew: מֵאַ֤יִן לִי֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר לָתֵ֖ת לְכׇל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: Whence am I to take flesh to give to all this people?

pairs.hebrew: כִּֽי־יִבְכּ֤וּ עָלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָה־לָּ֥נוּ בָשָׂ֖ר וְנֹאכֵֽלָה׃
pairs.english: For they weep over me, saying: Give us flesh and let us eat!

pairs.hebrew: לֹֽא־אוּכַ֤ל אָנֹכִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־כׇּל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה
pairs.english: I shall not be able to bear alone all this people,
for it is beyond my strength.

And if thus [You will do to them (The L-rd showed Moses the calamity that He was going to bring upon them)], You are rendering me "at" [(a term for the feminine), Moses' strength waning as that of a woman].

pairs.hebrew: הׇרְגֵ֤נִי נָא֙ הָרֹ֔ג אִם־מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ
pairs.english: Kill me, I pray You, if I have found favor in Your eyes,
and let me not witness my [(a "euphemism" for "their")] evil.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶסְפָה־לִּ֞י שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִישׁ֮ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses [Here is My response to your "I shall not be able to bear alone"]: Gather unto Me seventy men from the elders of Israel [(The original elders had been killed at Taveirah in delayed retribution for their sin [see Exodus 24:11] (delayed so as not to dampen the joy of the giving of the Torah)],

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־הֵ֛ם זִקְנֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם וְשֹׁטְרָ֑יו
pairs.english: whom you know to be the elders of the people and its officers, [who were appointed over them in Egypt (Since they pitied them and were smitten by the Egyptians because of them, it is only fitting that they be raised in Israel's greatness as they shared in its woes.)],

pairs.hebrew: וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֥וּ שָׁ֖ם עִמָּֽךְ׃
pairs.english: and take them to the tent of meeting, and have them stand there with you, [so that the people see, and accord them honor, saying: How beloved these must be, who entered with Moses to hear the Word from the mouth of the Holy One Blessed be He!]
And I shall go down and speak with you, [but not with them,] there.

pairs.hebrew: וְאָצַלְתִּ֗י מִן־הָר֛וּחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: And I shall increase, from the spirit which is upon you, and I will place it upon them, [as all take light from a lamp on a menorah, without that lamp losing any of its own light.]

pairs.hebrew: וְנָשְׂא֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּמַשָּׂ֣א הָעָ֔ם וְלֹא־תִשָּׂ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
pairs.english: And they shall bear with you the burden of the people [Stipulate with them: (This grandeur is being accorded them) on condition that they take upon themselves the wardship of My children, who are troublesome and refractory], and you shall not bear alone. [Thus, the response to "I shall not be able to bear alone."]

pairs.hebrew: וְאֶל־הָעָ֨ם תֹּאמַ֜ר הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמָחָר֮ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם בָּשָׂר֒
pairs.english: And to the people shall you say: Prepare yourselves for [retribution] tomorrow, and you shall eat flesh.

pairs.hebrew: כִּ֡י בְּכִיתֶם֩ בְּאׇזְנֵ֨י יְהֹוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֤י יַאֲכִלֵ֙נוּ֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּי־ט֥וֹב לָ֖נוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם
pairs.english: For you have wept in the ears of the L-rd, saying: Who shall feed us flesh? For it was good for us in Egypt.
And the L-rd shall give you flesh and you shall eat.

pairs.hebrew: לֹ֣א י֥וֹם אֶחָ֛ד תֹּאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֣א יוֹמָ֑יִם
pairs.english: Not one day shall you eat, and not two days,

pairs.hebrew: וְלֹ֣א ׀ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה יָמִ֗ים וְלֹא֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה יָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֖א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃
pairs.english: and not five days, and not ten days, and not twenty days.

pairs.hebrew: עַ֣ד ׀ חֹ֣דֶשׁ יָמִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא֙ מֵֽאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְזָרָ֑א
pairs.english: Until a month of days [(this, with the less wicked, who languished in their beds and their souls expired, see 33)], until it comes out of your nostrils [i.e., until it becomes loathsome to you], and it will be rejected by you [more than you sought it].

pairs.hebrew: יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־מְאַסְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־יְהֹוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֔ם וַתִּבְכּ֤וּ לְפָנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה יָצָ֥אנוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
pairs.english: For you have despised the L-rd who is in your midst [(Had I not reposed My shechinah among you, your hearts would not have been "inflated" unto all these things)], and you have wept before Him, saying: Why, now, did we leave Egypt!

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֘אמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֙לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ
pairs.english: And Moses said: Six hundred thousand foot are the people in whose midst I am,

pairs.hebrew: וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֗רְתָּ בָּשָׂר֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם וְאָכְל֖וּ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃
pairs.english: and You say: Meat shall I give to them, and they shall eat a month of days!

pairs.hebrew: הֲצֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר יִשָּׁחֵ֥ט לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֣א לָהֶ֑ם
pairs.english: If flocks and herds are slaughtered for them, will it be sufficient for them!

pairs.hebrew: אִ֣ם אֶֽת־כׇּל־דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֛ם יֵאָסֵ֥ף לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֥א לָהֶֽם׃ {פ}
pairs.english: If all the fish of the sea are gathered for them, will it be sufficient for them! [i.e., even if You give them what they ask, they will not be satisfied, for they are simply seeking a pretext against You.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הֲיַ֥ד יְהֹוָ֖ה תִּקְצָ֑ר
pairs.english: And the L-rd said to Moses: Shall the hand of the L-rd be found wanting? [i.e., If I do not give it, they will call My omnipotence into question. At this, Moses said: Let me go and attempt to conciliate them — whereupon the L-rd said:]
Now You will see whether My word [that they will not heed you] will befall you or not.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה
pairs.english: And Moses went out and told the people the words of the L-rd, [viz.: "Shall the hand of the L-rd be found wanting?" Did He not give you water from the rock, etc.? (but they did not heed him and denied G-d's ability to satisfy their present need)];

pairs.hebrew: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֞ף שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֹתָ֖ם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הָאֹֽהֶל׃
pairs.english: and, [seeing that he was not being heeded], he gathered seventy men from the elders of the people, and he stood them roundabout the tent.
And the L-rd descended in a cloud and He spoke to him,

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֗אצֶל מִן־הָר֙וּחַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַיִּתֵּ֕ן עַל־שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים
pairs.english: and He increased from the spirit which was upon him [see 17], and He placed it upon the seventy men, the elders.

pairs.hebrew: וַיְהִ֗י כְּנ֤וֹחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָר֔וּחַ וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יָסָֽפוּ׃
pairs.english: And it was, when the spirit rested upon them, that they prophesied — but [after that day], they prophesied no more.

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּשָּׁאֲר֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי־אֲנָשִׁ֣ים ׀ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֡ה שֵׁ֣ם הָאֶחָ֣ד ׀ אֶלְדָּ֡ד וְשֵׁם֩ הַשֵּׁנִ֨י מֵידָ֜ד
pairs.english: And there remained two men [of those who had been chosen as elders] in the camp, the name of the one, Eldad; the name of the other, Medad,
and the spirit rested upon them. And they were among those [designated as "elders"] on the ballots,
but they did not go out to the tent, [saying: We are not worthy of this greatness], and they prophesied in the camp.
And the youth [(some say it was Gershon, the son of Moses)] ran, and told Moses, saying:
Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֜עַן יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֗וּן מְשָׁרֵ֥ת מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִבְּחֻרָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר
pairs.english: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses from his youth, responded and said:
My Lord Moses, cause them to cease [from prophesying ("Saddle them" with community service and they will cease prophesying of themselves.)]

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַֽמְקַנֵּ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לִ֑י
pairs.english: And Moses said to him: Are you zealous for my sake?

pairs.hebrew: וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן כׇּל־עַ֤ם יְהֹוָה֙ נְבִיאִ֔ים כִּי־יִתֵּ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־רוּח֖וֹ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
pairs.english: Would that all the L-rd's people were prophets, that the L-rd would place His spirit upon them!
And Moses retired [from the tent of meeting] into [his tent in] the camp,
he and the elders of Israel. [(The L-rd did not punish Israel until each one of the righteous had entered his tent)].

pairs.hebrew: וְר֜וּחַ נָסַ֣ע ׀ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהֹוָ֗ה וַיָּ֣גׇז שַׂלְוִים֮ מִן־הַיָּם֒
pairs.english: And a wind went forth from the L-rd and "flew in" quail from the sea,

pairs.hebrew: וַיִּטֹּ֨שׁ עַל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה כְּדֶ֧רֶךְ י֣וֹם כֹּ֗ה וּכְדֶ֤רֶךְ יוֹם֙ כֹּ֔ה סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה
pairs.english: and it spread over the camp, about a day's journey on one side and a day's journey on the other, roundabout the camp,
and about two cubits above the face of the earth. [They hovered chest-high so that they could be easily gathered in.]

pairs.hebrew: וַיָּ֣קׇם הָעָ֡ם כׇּל־הַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא וְכׇל־הַלַּ֜יְלָה וְכֹ֣ל ׀ י֣וֹם הַֽמׇּחֳרָ֗ת וַיַּֽאַסְפוּ֙ אֶת־הַשְּׂלָ֔ו
pairs.english: And the people rose all that day and all the night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quail.
He that gathered least, [the indolent and the lame], gathered ten chamarim (homers),
and they spread them in layers roundabout the camp.

pairs.hebrew: הַבָּשָׂ֗ר עוֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ בֵּ֣ין שִׁנֵּיהֶ֔ם טֶ֖רֶם יִכָּרֵ֑ת
pairs.english: The flesh was yet between their teeth [(this, with the wicked, see 10)], not yet consumed,
when the wrath of the L-rd burned against the people;

pairs.hebrew: וַיַּ֤ךְ יְהֹוָה֙ בָּעָ֔ם מַכָּ֖ה רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
pairs.english: and the L-rd smote the people with a very great plague.
And he called the name of that place Kivroth Hata'avah ("the graves of the lust");
for there they buried the people that lusted.
From Kivroth Hata'avah the people traveled to Chatzeiroth,
and they abode in Chatzeiroth.
And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses

pairs.hebrew: עַל־אֹד֛וֹת הָאִשָּׁ֥ה הַכֻּשִׁ֖ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקָ֑ח כִּֽי־אִשָּׁ֥ה כֻשִׁ֖ית לָקָֽח׃
pairs.english: because of [his divorcing] the Cushite woman [(Zipporah, called "Cushite" because she was extremely beautiful in all respects)] that he had taken; for he had taken a Cushite woman, [and now he had divorced her]. [Miriam was with Tzipporah when Moses was told that Eldad and Medad were prophesying in the camp, and she heard her exclaim: "Woe to the wives of these men upon whom prophesy has been conferred, and who will separate from their wives just as my husband (Moses) has separated from me!" Miriam thereupon apprised Aaron of this, (wherefore, being the initiator of the talk against Moses, she is mentioned first)].

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ הֲרַ֤ק אַךְ־בְּמֹשֶׁה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה הֲלֹ֖א גַּם־בָּ֣נוּ דִבֵּ֑ר
pairs.english: And they said: Is it only with Moses that the L-rd has spoken? Has He not spoken also with us? [and we have not separated from our spouses!]
And the L-rd heard.
And the man Moses was extremely humble [lowly and forbearing],
more than any man on the face of the earth.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה פִּתְאֹ֗ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־מִרְיָ֔ם
pairs.english: And the L-rd said suddenly to Moses, to Aaron, and to Miriam ["suddenly," when they (Aaron and Miriam) were unclean through intercourse, and they cried for water (to purify themselves with) — this, by way of impressing upon them that Moses being constantly ("suddenly") subject to a visitation by the Shechinah, did well in separating himself from his wife] (The L-rd said:)

pairs.hebrew: צְא֥וּ שְׁלׇשְׁתְּכֶ֖ם אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שְׁלׇשְׁתָּֽם׃
pairs.english: The three of you go out to the tent of meeting [(the three were called by a single utterance, something which (within the framework of nature) the mouth is not capable of uttering nor the ear of hearing)]; and the three of them went out.

pairs.hebrew: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהֹוָה֙ בְּעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל
pairs.english: And the L-rd descended in a pillar of cloud, and He stood at the door of the tent,
and He called Aaron and Miriam [to separate them from Moses, (all of a man's praise not being mentioned to his face, see Genesis 7:1)], and the two of them came forth.
And He said: Hear, I pray you, My words.

pairs.hebrew: אִם־יִֽהְיֶה֙ נְבִ֣יאֲכֶ֔ם יְהֹוָ֗ה בַּמַּרְאָה֙ אֵלָ֣יו אֶתְוַדָּ֔ע בַּחֲל֖וֹם אֲדַבֶּר־בּֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: If there be prophets among you, "the L-rd" [i.e., the immanence of My Name] I invest him with in a vision; in a dream I speak to him.
Not so My servant Moses.
In all My house he is trusted.

pairs.hebrew: פֶּ֣ה אֶל־פֶּ֞ה אֲדַבֶּר־בּ֗וֹ וּמַרְאֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א בְחִידֹ֔ת
pairs.english: Mouth to mouth I spoke to him [i.e., I told him to separate from his wife (see Deuteronomy 5:27-28)], and [in clear] revelation [of My words], and not in riddles;
and the configuration [i.e., the "back" (see Exodus 33:23)] of the L-rd does he behold.

pairs.hebrew: וּמַדּ֙וּעַ֙ לֹ֣א יְרֵאתֶ֔ם לְדַבֵּ֖ר בְּעַבְדִּ֥י בְמֹשֶֽׁה׃
pairs.english: Why, then, did you not fear to speak against My servant, [even if he were not Moses], against Moses, [even if he were not My servant]!
And the wrath of the L-rd burned against them,

and He departed. [After apprising them of their wrongdoing, He placed them under the ban (whence it is to be derived that one may not manifest anger against his neighbor until he informs him of his guilt.)]

pairs.hebrew: וְהֶעָנָ֗ן סָ֚ר מֵעַ֣ל הָאֹ֔הֶל וְהִנֵּ֥ה מִרְיָ֖ם מְצֹרַ֣עַת כַּשָּׁ֑לֶג
pairs.english: And after the cloud had departed from above the tent — behold, Miriam was as leprous as the snow. [("after the cloud had departed":) As a king would say to a pedagogue: "Punish my son — but wait until I have gone."]
And Aaron turned to Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.
And Aaron said to Moses: Pray, my lord,

pairs.hebrew: אַל־נָ֨א תָשֵׁ֤ת עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ חַטָּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר נוֹאַ֖לְנוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָֽאנוּ׃
pairs.english: do not impute transgression to us in that we have been foolish and have sinned.
Let her [this, our sister,] not be as a dead one [(a leper is reckoned as a dead one, both the leprous and the dead causing uncleanliness by entry (into their domain)].

pairs.hebrew: אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּצֵאתוֹ֙ מֵרֶ֣חֶם אִמּ֔וֹ וַיֵּאָכֵ֖ל חֲצִ֥י בְשָׂרֽוֹ׃
pairs.english: Since he [the "dead one"] comes out of his [brother's] mother's womb, [then if that brother is in a position to help and does not,] it is as if half his (the latter's) flesh had been consumed, [his brother being his "flesh" (Genesis 37:27)].
